payload.author: kt-ai-infra
payload.body:
## Summary

On a fresh global install of `paperclipai` (latest, `2026.529.0`), the **Skills → Catalog** tab fails with `Internal server error`. The API endpoint `GET /api/skills/catalog` returns **500** because the server looks for the skills-catalog manifest at a monorepo-relative path that does not exist in the published npm layout.

## Error

```
ERROR: GET /api/skills/catalog 500 — Skills catalog manifest not found at
/Users/<user>/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/@paperclipai/packages/skills-catalog/generated/catalog.json.
Run pnpm --filter @paperclipai/skills-catalog build:manifest.

    at getCatalogManifest (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/skills-catalog.js:20:15)
    at getCatalogSkills    (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/skills-catalog.js:37:29)
    at listCatalogSkills   (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/skills-catalog.js:92:12)
    at @paperclipai/server/dist/routes/company-skills.js:77:18
```

## Root cause

`@paperclipai/server/dist/services/skills-catalog.js` resolves the manifest relative to its own location, assuming the monorepo directory layout:

```js
const serviceDir = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const repoRoot = path.resolve(serviceDir, "../../..");          // -> node_modules/@paperclipai
const catalogPackageRoot = path.join(repoRoot, "packages/skills-catalog");
const catalogManifestPath = path.join(catalogPackageRoot, "generated/catalog.json");
```

In a published install, `repoRoot` resolves to `node_modules/@paperclipai`, so the code expects `node_modules/@paperclipai/packages/skills-catalog/generated/catalog.json`. That `packages/skills-catalog` directory is never present because:

1. `@paperclipai/server`'s `package.json` does **not** declare a dependency on the catalog package, so it is never installed, and
2. even if installed, the published package name is `@paperclipai/skills-catalog`, not `@paperclipai/packages/skills-catalog`.

`@paperclipai/skills-catalog` *does* exist on npm (currently `0.3.1`) and ships both `generated/catalog.json` and the bundled skill sources — it is simply not wired into the runtime resolution path for published builds.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `npx paperclipai onboard --yes` then `npx paperclipai run` (or install globally) — version `2026.529.0`.
2. Open the UI, go to **Skills → Catalog**.
3. Observe `Internal server error`; server logs show the 500 above. (Installed/local skills work fine.)

## Workaround that confirms the diagnosis

Manually placing the published catalog package at the expected path makes the endpoint return 200 and the Catalog tab populate:

```sh
# from the active npx/global @paperclipai install dir
DEST="node_modules/@paperclipai/packages/skills-catalog"
mkdir -p "$DEST"
npm pack @paperclipai/skills-catalog@0.3.1
tar xzf paperclipai-skills-catalog-*.tgz -C "$DEST" --strip-components=1
```

## Suggested fix

- Add `@paperclipai/skills-catalog` as a runtime dependency of `@paperclipai/server`, and
- resolve the manifest via `require.resolve('@paperclipai/skills-catalog/generated/catalog.json')` (or an env override) instead of the hard-coded `../../../packages/skills-catalog` monorepo path, so it works in both monorepo and published layouts.

## Environment

- `paperclipai` 2026.529.0 (latest), `@paperclipai/server` 2026.529.0
- macOS, Node via Homebrew, install via `npx`
payload.title: Skills Catalog tab returns 500: server resolves manifest via monorepo path not present in published build

payload.author: mrveiss
payload.body:
## Summary

After a server crash or restart, \`reapOrphanedRuns()\` cannot verify liveness for runs where \`processPid = NULL\` (the server died before \`persistRunProcessMetadata\` ran). It immediately marks those runs failed and dispatches replacements — while the original processes remain alive as untracked orphans (reparented to PID 1). Every subsequent restart multiplies the orphan count.

## Reproduction

1. Start the server and dispatch some agents
2. Hard-kill the server mid-execution (before process PIDs are written to DB)
3. Restart the server
4. On startup, \`reapOrphanedRuns()\` (called with \`staleThresholdMs=0\`) finds runs with \`processPid=null\`, marks them \`failed\`, calls \`startNextQueuedRunForAgent\` → duplicate processes spawned
5. Repeat — orphan count grows exponentially per restart cycle

## Observed impact

On a WSL2 host (96 GB RAM, 32 GB WSL cap):
- Pre-existing orphans + new dispatches after restart → 80+ untracked \`claude --tools\` processes within minutes of restart
- Paperclip UI reports all agents \`idle\` (server lost all handles); \`ps\` shows 80 processes
- Pausing all routines does NOT stop the climb (orphans from previous restarts continue accumulating subagents)
- Memory fills the WSL cap → swap → Windows host freeze requiring hard reboot
- \`systemctl stop paperclip.service\` clears orphans via the graceful-shutdown path (PR #7218)

## Root cause

In \`reapOrphanedRuns()\` (\`server/src/services/heartbeat.ts\`):

When \`processPid = null\`, the reaper cannot call \`isProcessAlive\`. It falls through to the no-PID path: \`shouldRetry = tracksLocalChild && (!!run.processPid || ...) = false\`, so it calls \`releaseIssueExecutionAndPromote\` + \`startNextQueuedRunForAgent\` — dispatching a fresh run — while the original process is still alive and untracked.

## Fix (included in PR #7219)

Added a 10-minute grace period for null-PID local-adapter runs. The slot stays \`"running"\` in DB during the grace window, so \`countRunningRunsForAgent()\` returns non-zero and the \`maxConcurrentRuns\` cap is enforced. After 10 minutes the slot is reclaimed as before.

Two new tests verify the boundary: recent null-PID run is preserved (reaped=0), old null-PID run is reclaimed (reaped=1). All 46 process-recovery tests pass.

## Relationship to existing fixes

- PR #7218: cleans up orphans on **graceful shutdown** ✓
- PR #7219: raises OOM score for agents ✓
- **This fix**: prevents duplicate dispatch on **restart** when PID was never stored (now included in PR #7219)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/claude-code)
payload.title: bug: server restart causes exponential orphan accumulation when processPid not stored before crash

payload.body: ## Summary When an imported company's AGENTS.md frontmatter uses YAML single-quoted scalars for string values, the Paperclip UI renders the quote characters as literal text in the agent's configuration page. ## Reproduction 1. Import the community example `newsletter-press` from https://paperclip.community/companies: paperclipai company import --target new 2. Navigate to the imported company → Agents → CEO / Editor → Configuration. 3. The Name field renders as `'CEO / Editor'` with surrounding single quotes shown as literal characters. The Title field renders the same way. ## Expected behavior YAML single quotes around scalar values are syntax, not data. The field should render `CEO / Editor` (no surrounding quote characters). ## Source frontmatter The bundle's `agents/ceo/AGENTS.md` contains: ```yaml --- schema: agentcompanies/v1 slug: ceo name: 'CEO / Editor' title: 'CEO / Editor' reportsTo: null skills: [...] --- ``` The single quotes are standard YAML scalar syntax — required (or applied by default by serializers like ruamel.yaml) when the value contains characters such as `/`, `&`, or other YAML-meaningful characters. The quotes are not part of the data and should not appear in display fields. ## Scope Affects any community bundle with multi-word or special-character names in AGENTS.md frontmatter. Reproduces with multiple bundles on https://paperclip.community/companies (newsletter-press, niche-site-empire, agency-engine, etc. — most CEO and senior-role names contain `/` or spaces). ## Screenshot ## Environment - Paperclip version: [paste output of `paperclipai --version`] - OS: [paste output of `cat /etc/os-release | head -2`] - Install method: [npx onboard / docker / source build — whichever applies] - Source bundle: newsletter-press from paperclip.community/companies - Import path: `paperclipai company import --target new` ## Notes Likely related to but distinct from #4989 (folded/literal scalars). This is the single-quoted scalar variant.

## Summary

An `issue_productivity_review` issue (created by `reconcileProductivityReviews` in `server/src/services/productivity-review.ts`) presents its **Manager Decision** options via `buildReviewMarkdown()` as the **last** section of the issue `description`, below Source / Evidence / Thresholds / Latest Runs / Latest Assignee Run Comments / Usage Samples. Two problems:

1. **Placement.** The reviewer must scroll past a full screen of generated evidence to reach the options. The actionable part should be pinned at the top of the page, above the evidence.
2. **It's inert.** The options ("Close as productive", "Continue with a snooze window", "Request decomposition / reroute / block / stop") are plain markdown text. There is no wired control that applies any of them — resolution is only achievable by manually transitioning the review issue's `status` to `done`/`cancelled` via the generic issue routes. A reviewer reading the decision block has nothing to click.

## Request

Render the Manager Decision as an interactive panel at the **top** of the review issue (above the description), with buttons that actually resolve the review:

- **Close as productive** → set review `status=done` (this arms the existing 6h `findRecentResolvedProductivityReview` snooze, so a still-churning source re-reviews later instead of being suppressed forever)
- **Snooze N hours**
- **Decompose / Reroute / Block (with unblock owner) / Stop** the source work

This is adjacent to a separate report about the decision not persisting / the review surface not refreshing.

## Source refs

- `server/src/services/productivity-review.ts` — `buildReviewMarkdown()` appends the decision text as the final section
- `server/src/routes/issues.ts` — PATCH `/issues/:id` is the only current way to "resolve" a review
payload.title: Productivity review: Manager Decision is inert markdown at the bottom of the description, not an actionable control at the top

payload.author: brendandebeasi
payload.body:
## Summary

Two related ways an `issue_productivity_review` gets stuck in `in_review` forever.

### 1. Orphaned reviews (no assignee) are unreachable

`reconcileProductivityReviews` creates the review with `assigneeAgentId = resolveReviewOwnerAgentId(...)`. When that resolves to `null` (the source agent has no `reportsTo`, and there is no project lead / `cto` / `ceo` owner), the review is created with `assignee_agent_id = NULL`. But:

- the runtime only wakes an issue's **assignee**, and
- `reconcileProductivityReviews` scans **source** issues (`assignee_agent_id IS NOT NULL`), never the review itself.

So the review parks `in_review` and nothing — agent or timer — ever touches it again. It sits as permanent "needs review" noise. (Observed live: a review with `assignee_agent_id IS NULL`, `status='in_review'`, untouched for hours.)

### 2. Resolving doesn't persist / the review surface doesn't refresh

There is no resolution column and no resolve action; "resolved" == `status ∈ {done,cancelled}` (enforced by the `issues_active_productivity_review_uq` partial index and `findOpenProductivityReview`). Actioning a review's decision from the board does not transition status, so after navigating back the review still appears as needing review, and the list doesn't refetch.

## Request

1. **Never create an orphaned review.** If `resolveReviewOwnerAgentId` returns null, either skip creation or fall back to an instance/board-visible owner; and/or have `reconcileProductivityReviews` also reap reviews that are themselves stuck `in_review` with no assignee — resolve them as `done` (arming the 6h snooze so a genuinely-churning source re-reviews later).
2. **Wire a real resolve action** (see sibling issue) that writes `status=done` and refetches the review surface.

## Workaround (for anyone hitting this now)

An out-of-band reconciler that (a) closes `issue_productivity_review` issues that are orphaned / source-moot / stale as `done`, and (b) re-posts dropped decline feedback as a real user comment, restores normal flow. Happy to share the script.

## Source refs

- `server/src/services/productivity-review.ts` — `reconcileProductivityReviews()`, `resolveReviewOwnerAgentId()`, `findOpenProductivityReview()`, `findRecentResolvedProductivityReview()`
- `packages/db/src/schema/issues.ts` — `issues_active_productivity_review_uq`
payload.title: Productivity review can be created with no assignee and then never resolves; resolving doesn't persist/refresh the review surface

I'm running Paperclip for my company and I have custom skills already imported (via GitHub repo). However, I cannot programmatically assign these skills to specific agents via the API.

Add an API endpoint:

PUT /api/agents/{id}/skills
Body: {"skills": ["skill-id-1", "skill-id-2"]}

- Bulk skill assignment
- Role-based auto-assignment (CEO delegates skills to appropriate agents)
- CI/CD integration for skill management

- Skills are from: https://github.com/xcellencecustomer-code/xcellence-amazon-skills
- 11 agents configured for Amazon FBA business

payload.author: CosmicDreamer17
payload.body:
## Summary

`DELETE /api/companies/{companyId}` returns a deterministic **HTTP 500** with an opaque body (`{"error":"Internal server error"}`) for any company that has agents/projects carrying **run / issue / comment / secret-binding history**. The company is **not** deleted (verified intact after every attempt). The same 500 occurs on `DELETE /api/agents/{id}` and `DELETE /api/projects/{id}` for historied entities — so the parent company can't be torn down either.

The UI "delete" path instead **soft-deletes** the company (`status` → `archived`) and succeeds. Only the API hard-delete fails.

## Isolation (points at a cascade gap)

On one company I deleted entities individually:

| Entity | History | `DELETE` result |
|---|---|---|
| agent with no secrets, **never heartbeated** (no runs) | none | **`200 {"ok":true}`** |
| agent with `secret_ref` env + heartbeat/run history | has runs | **`500`** |
| project with issues/comments | has children | **`500`** |
| company (after the clean agent was removed) | — | **`500`** |

The clean, history-free agent deleted fine; every entity with dependent rows (runs, issues, comments, secret bindings) 500s. This strongly suggests the hard-delete cascade does not handle those dependent rows (likely an unhandled FK / missing cascade), whereas the archive path sidesteps it.

## Repro

1. Create a company via import into a new company:
   `paperclipai company import <pkg> --include company,agents,projects,issues,skills --target new --new-company-name "<Name>" --yes`
   (result: agents with `secret_ref` GITHUB_TOKEN bindings + managed instruction bundles, projects with materialized repo workspaces, imported issues with comments, company secrets, plus an approval).
2. Exercise at least one agent (a heartbeat run) so it has run history.
3. Attempt delete — both paths fail identically:
   - CLI: `paperclipai company delete <company-id> --yes --confirm <company-id>`
   - Raw: `curl -X DELETE /api/companies/<company-id>` (board bearer token)
4. Observed: `HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`, deterministic across repeated attempts; company intact.
5. Per-entity teardown also 500s for any agent/project with history (see table); a history-free agent deletes at 200.
6. UI delete on the same company succeeds as a soft-delete (`status` → `archived`).

## Expected

Either a successful hard-delete that cascades over dependent agents/projects/runs/issues/comments/secret-bindings, **or** a 4xx with an actionable message naming what blocks deletion. The current opaque 500 leaves the operator with nothing to act on and no API path to remove a company.

## Asks

1. Surface the real server-side error instead of a bare 500 (log + response detail).
2. Fix (or document) the hard-delete cascade for companies/agents/projects that carry run/issue/comment/secret-binding history.

## Environment

- Paperclip CLI `2026.525.0`
- Self-hosted on Railway, `authenticated` mode, Railway-managed Postgres
- Upstream pinned SHA `b7545823bec49b4a73c3813d8fb634f68fc84b48`
payload.title: Hard-delete API returns deterministic 500 for companies/agents/projects with run/issue/secret history (cascade gap; UI archive works)

payload.author: CosmicDreamer17
payload.body:
# `company import --target new` strands imported agents in `pending_approval` with no approval record (no UI button, no CLI verb → unactivatable)

## Summary

On a self-hosted instance, importing a company with `company import --target new` into a target company that has `requireBoardApprovalForNewAgents: true` leaves every imported agent in status `pending_approval` **but never mints the corresponding `hire_agent` approval record**. The result is a dead state with no supported recovery path:

- `GET /api/companies/{id}/approvals` (CLI `approval list -C {id}`) returns **empty** — there is nothing to approve.
- The web UI exposes no "approve" action for the agent (only *Reset session* and *Terminate*).
- The CLI `agent` command group has no `approve` / `activate` / `unpause` verb (only `list`, `get`, `local-cli`).
- Any attempt to invoke the agent fails: `heartbeat run --agent-id …` → **`Agent is not invokable in its current state`** (status `pending_approval`).

Because `issuePrefix` is platform-locked (only `name`, `description`, `brandColor`, `logoAssetId` are PATCH-editable on `/api/companies/{id}`), export→import-as-new-company is the only supported way to change a company's issue prefix. This bug makes that migration path produce a company whose entire agent roster is stranded.

This contradicts the normal agent-hire path (`POST /api/companies/{companyId}/agent-hires`), which, when `requireBoardApprovalForNewAgents` is true, sets the agent to `pending_approval` **and** creates a linked `hire_agent` approval (`payload.agentId = agent.id`) that the board can resolve. The import path sets the same blocking status without the resolvable approval object — so the two halves of the workflow are out of sync.

Likely related / adjacent (cross-referencing, not claiming exact dup):
- **#3918** — `company import` + `requireBoardApprovalForNewAgents` new-agent handling gap. This report is the "inserted-but-stranded" symptom; if #3918 still describes a "skipped insert", this is the more precise current behavior.
- **#3821** — pending approvals are not discoverable in the UI (explains the missing approve button).
- **#1994** — company import does not replicate the operational defaults of UI/normal agent creation (plausible mechanism: import skips the approval-minting step the normal create path performs).

## Environment

- Deployment: **self-hosted**, Railway (single multi-tenant server, one Postgres), `deploymentMode: authenticated`, private.
- Server `/api/health`: `{"status":"ok","deploymentMode":"authenticated","bootstrapStatus":"ready"}` (no `/api/version` endpoint is exposed; server SHA not externally obtainable).
- CLI: `paperclipai 2026.525.0`.
- Target company created with `requireBoardApprovalForNewAgents: true`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a source company with ≥1 agent. Export it:
   ```
   paperclipai company export <sourceCompanyId> -o pkg.zip
   ```
2. Import as a brand-new company that will require board approval for new agents:
   ```
   paperclipai company import pkg.zip \
     --target new \
     --new-company-name "Example" \
     --include company,agents,projects,issues,skills \
     --yes
   ```
   (The created company has `requireBoardApprovalForNewAgents: true`.)
3. Observe the import warnings — for each agent:
   > `assignee <name> is pending_approval; imported work was left unassigned.`
4. Inspect the imported agents:
   ```
   paperclipai agent list -C <newCompanyId>
   # → every agent: status=pending_approval
   ```
5. Look for something to approve:
   ```
   paperclipai approval list -C <newCompanyId>
   # → (empty)
   ```
6. Try to use any agent:
   ```
   paperclipai heartbeat run --agent-id <agentId>
   # → Agent is not invokable in its current state
   ```

There is now no supported way (UI button, `approval list` entry, or CLI verb) to move the agents out of `pending_approval`.

## Expected behavior

After import into an approval-gated company, imported agents should be in a **resolvable** state —
payload.title: company import --target new strands imported agents in pending_approval with no approval record (no UI button, no CLI verb -> unactivatable)

## Problem

`claude_local` can wedge permanently when resuming a Claude session whose replay includes a modified `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` block. Anthropic rejects every resume with the deterministic validation error below, and Paperclip retries the same poisoned resume path unless the adapter rotates to a fresh session.

Literal observed message:

```text
API Error: 400 messages.N.content.M: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.
```

## Expected behavior

When a resumed Claude session fails with this error, handle it the same way as an unknown/missing session replay failure: log the replay failure, clear/rotate the session, and retry once with a fresh session.

## Regression coverage needed

Add a detector test using the exact backtick-wrapped Anthropic message above. A previous detector pattern that expected whitespace immediately after `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` did not match because Anthropic wraps those tokens in backticks.

## Local verification from downstream incident BEDAAA-111

On a local `@paperclipai/adapter-claude-local@2026.529.0` install, the desired shape is:

- `execute.js` imports `isClaudeModifiedThinkingReplayError`
- resumed-session retry condition includes `isClaudeUnknownSessionError(initial.parsed) || isClaudeModifiedThinkingReplayError(initial.parsed)`
- modified-thinking regex tolerates backtick/quote-wrapped `thinking` and `redacted_thinking`
- direct Node check of `isClaudeModifiedThinkingReplayError({ result: <literal observed message> })` returns `true`

This issue is to make sure the source package carries that behavior and regression test upstream, not just a patched/generated local install.
payload.title: claude-local: auto-recover modified-thinking resume failures with backtick-wrapped Anthropic errors

payload.author: more-than-ok-agents
payload.body:
## Summary

Autonomous agents using `claude_local`, `codex_local`, `acpx_local`, or `hermes_local` can silently fail when their cross-heartbeat session JSONL grows past the context limit. The root cause is that `ADAPTER_MANAGED_SESSION_POLICY` sets all compaction thresholds to `0`, causing `hasSessionCompactionThresholds()` to always return `false` and `evaluateSessionCompaction()` to never rotate sessions for these adapters.

## Root Cause

In `packages/adapter-utils/src/session-compaction.ts`:

```typescript
const ADAPTER_MANAGED_SESSION_POLICY: SessionCompactionPolicy = {
  enabled: true,
  maxSessionRuns: 0,
  maxRawInputTokens: 0,
  maxSessionAgeHours: 0,  // ← causes hasSessionCompactionThresholds() to return false
};
```

For task-scoped heartbeats this is harmless — `shouldResetTaskSessionForWake()` resets the session on new task assignments. But for **autonomous timer wakes** with no task ID, the heartbeat service assigns the synthetic `"__heartbeat__"` key (see `deriveTaskKeyWithHeartbeatFallback`). All autonomous heartbeats share this key, so the JSONL session accumulates indefinitely with no rotation.

## Evidence

An agent using `claude_local` accumulated a 2.7 MB JSONL session file over ~48 hours (spanning every autonomous heartbeat from May 28–30 2026). The May 30 04:00 UTC wake: platform dispatched (confirmed via `lastHeartbeatAt`) but the agent produced zero output — no API calls, no file writes — consistent with silent LLM invocation failure from context overflow.

For comparison, task-scoped agents produce session files of 90–100 KB each (fresh per task assignment).

## Proposed Fix

Add a `maxSessionAgeHours: 48` backstop to `ADAPTER_MANAGED_SESSION_POLICY`:

```typescript
// Adapters with native context management (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) handle
// within-session compaction themselves, so Paperclip skips token- and run-based
// rotation. A 48-hour age backstop is still applied to prevent unbounded JSONL
// accumulation across autonomous heartbeats that reuse the synthetic
// "__heartbeat__" session key (timer wakes with no task ID).
const ADAPTER_MANAGED_SESSION_POLICY: SessionCompactionPolicy = {
  enabled: true,
  maxSessionRuns: 0,
  maxRawInputTokens: 0,
  maxSessionAgeHours: 48,
};
```

This preserves native within-session compaction (Claude Code auto-compact) while enforcing a maximum session lifetime to cap cross-heartbeat JSONL growth. Operators who need longer sessions can override via `runtimeConfig.heartbeat.sessionCompaction.maxSessionAgeHours`.

The fix is implemented in the fork at: https://github.com/More-Than-OK-AB/paperclip/tree/fix-adapter-managed-session-age-backstop

Diff: `packages/adapter-utils/src/session-compaction.ts` — 1 line change (`maxSessionAgeHours: 0` → `48`) plus updated comment.

## Impact

- **Breaking**: No API surface change, no schema migration, no config required.
- **Behavior change**: Native-adapter agents will start a fresh JSONL session after 48 hours of accumulation. Agent persistent state (memory files, issue documents) provides continuity across session rotation.
- **Task-specific sessions**: Unaffected — already reset by `shouldResetTaskSessionForWake()` on new task assignments.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an agent with `claude_local` adapter
2. Set up a timer schedule with no task — this produces a `wakeSource: "timer"` wake with no `taskId`
3. Let the agent run 5+ autonomous heartbeats
4. Observe that the JSONL session file grows continuously with no rotation
5. After ~2 days of heartbeats, the agent produces zero output despite being dispatched
payload.title: bug: ADAPTER_MANAGED_SESSION_POLICY has maxSessionAgeHours: 0, causing unbounded JSONL accumulation for autonomous timer-wake agents

payload.body:
## Summary

When the control plane cancels a heartbeat run that is in `scheduled_retry` status (a pending retry with a future `scheduledRetryAt`), the retry is silently lost and the agent never runs again until manual intervention — even though a single re-invocation would succeed.

Observed on Paperclip `v2026.529.0`, `@paperclipai/adapter-claude-local`.

## Root cause

- `CANCELLABLE_HEARTBEAT_RUN_STATUSES = ["queued", "running", "scheduled_retry"]` (`server/src/services/heartbeat.ts:212`) — so a **pending scheduled retry is cancellable**.
- `cancelRunInternal` (`heartbeat.ts:9802`) sets such a run to **`cancelled`** and then only re-invokes the next **queued** run via `startNextQueuedRunForAgent`. It does **not** preserve or re-arm the pending `scheduledRetryAt`.
- The retry-promotion path only executes rows with **`status = "scheduled_retry"`** (e.g. `heartbeat.ts:5197`, `5322`, `5771`, `5882`, `9222`).

Net: once the scheduled-retry row is flipped to `cancelled`, the promotion tick never picks it up again, and nothing re-schedules the agent — the retry vanishes.

## Reproduction

1. A `claude_local` agent with heartbeat enabled.
2. A heartbeat run fails with a transient error (e.g. an upstream `429`) → the platform schedules a retry: a row with `status = "scheduled_retry"`, `scheduledRetryAt` ≈ now + 2 min, `scheduledRetryAttempt = 1`, `scheduledRetryReason = "transient_failure"`.
3. **Before** that due time, a control-plane cancel fires on the run (in our case via the active-run / liveness path; the run's `livenessState = "failed"`) → `cancelRunInternal` → `status = "cancelled"`, `errorCode = "cancelled"`, `error = "Cancelled by control plane"`.
4. The retry-promotion tick skips it (its status is now `cancelled`, not `scheduled_retry`); **no further retry is scheduled** (the attempt count never advances past 1).
5. The agent ends up in `status = "error"` and is **never re-invoked** — we observed ~20h — until a manual `heartbeat run -a <id>`, which **succeeds immediately**.

### Evidence from our incident
`heartbeat_runs` for the affected agent:
- `20:17` — `failed` / `claude_transient_upstream`
- `20:27` — `cancelled` / `errorCode=cancelled` / `error="Cancelled by control plane"`, with `scheduledRetryAt=20:29`, `scheduledRetryAttempt=1`, `scheduledRetryReason=transient_failure`, `livenessReason="Run ended with failed (claude_transient_upstream)"`
- **No further rows** until a manual invocation ~20h later, which succeeded.

The manual run’s first attempt hit `No conversation found with session ID …` (the original session was orphaned by the cancel’s SIGTERM), and the adapter’s existing `isClaudeUnknownSessionError` fresh-session fallback recovered automatically — confirming the agent was healthy the whole time; it was simply never re-invoked.

## Suggested fix (any one)

- In `cancelRunInternal`, when the run being cancelled is `scheduled_retry` with a pending `scheduledRetryAt`, **preserve/re-arm** the retry (re-create a `scheduled_retry` row for the agent) instead of dropping it; **or**
- **exclude `scheduled_retry`** from the statuses this control-plane cancel terminates (cancel only `queued`/`running`); **or**
- have the cancel path, after terminating, re-schedule the agent’s dropped retry.
- Defense-in-depth backstop: a sweep that re-invokes agents in `error` with no active run and no pending `scheduled_retry`.

## Related

#6324 — adapter-layer session-recovery (`isClaudeUnknownSessionError` regex). Complementary but a **different layer**: our failure is in the heartbeat orchestration (cancel drops the scheduled retry), and our session-error string is the one #6324’s regex **already matches**, so that fix would not address this.
payload.title: heartbeat: cancelRunInternal on a scheduled_retry run silently drops the retry → agent wedged with no auto-recovery

payload.body:
## Summary

The Paperclip heartbeat scheduler is silently dropping scheduled wakes for agents configured with an `intervalSec` heartbeat routine. The scheduler does not error or emit warnings — it simply fails to fire wakes, leaving agents stale for 12–23+ hour windows while their status remains `running`.

## Environment

- Paperclip platform (cloud-hosted)
- Agents using autonomous heartbeat routines with `schedule` triggers
- Observed: 2026-05-29 through 2026-05-30

## Expected Behavior

Each heartbeat routine fires within reasonable tolerance of `lastHeartbeatAt + intervalSec`. For a 6-hour interval, a wake should occur within minutes (or at most tens of minutes) of the scheduled time. `lastHeartbeatAt` should update each time a run completes.

## Observed Behavior

Multiple consecutive wakes are silently not fired at all. `lastHeartbeatAt` does not update during the missed wakes, confirming this is a scheduler-side drop (not an adapter-side failure). Agents remain in `running` status with no indication that scheduled wakes are being skipped.

## Evidence

### Company-wide run volume drop

| Date       | Total runs | Notes                              |
|------------|------------|------------------------------------|
| 2026-05-29 | 22         | 7 `other`-status (coalesced/skipped); typical is 40–100+ |
| 2026-05-30 | 26         | 5 failures                         |

This is a ~60–80% reduction from normal run volume, indicating a platform-wide scheduler degradation.

### Agent-level missed wakes

**Agent MTOKA (ID: `586de30f`), interval: 6h**
- 4 of 7 expected wakes were missed or significantly late
- Observed delays: +17 min, +75 min (when fires did occur)
- 3 wakes delivered no run at all (lastHeartbeatAt not updated)

**Agent Platform Engineer (ID: `c60e03d3`), interval: ~8h (estimated)**
- `lastHeartbeatAt` was `2026-05-29T18:12:30Z`
- Next observed heartbeat: ~23+ hours later
- Agent remained `status: running` throughout the entire gap

### Ruling out agent-side causes

- Both agents had no changes to config, instructions, or skill assignments
- No CEO/board pause or budget-cap actions during the affected window
- Agent statuses were `running` (not `paused`) for the entire period
- No adapter errors logged on successful runs before/after the gap

## Pattern

The drop is scheduler-side, not agent-side:
- `lastHeartbeatAt` only updates when a run actually fires — it did not update during missed wakes
- Successful runs resumed normally after the gap with no config changes needed
- The pattern affects multiple agents simultaneously, suggesting a shared scheduler component

## Proposed Investigation Areas

1. **Scheduler queue**: Are scheduled wake entries being dropped from the queue without being attempted?
2. **Coalescing logic**: Is the scheduler's `coalesced`/`skipped` logic incorrectly merging or cancelling consecutive wakes?
3. **Distributed lock/lease expiry**: If the scheduler uses a distributed lock, is it failing to acquire or renew during the affected window?
4. **Pod restart / scheduler failover**: Does a scheduler restart leave in-flight or pending wakes in a non-recoverable state?

## Reproduction

We cannot provide a minimal repro script since this requires platform-level scheduler access. The evidence above comes from production telemetry. Checking `lastHeartbeatAt` for any long-running agent with a 6h schedule against wall-clock time on 2026-05-29/30 should reveal the gap.

## Impact

- Agents responsible for time-sensitive tasks (monitoring, PR review, issue triage) silently stall for hours/days
- No user-visible warning or alert when wakes are missed
- `lastHeartbeatAt` being stale is the only observable signal, and users must manually inspect it
payload.title: Heartbeat scheduler silently drops/delays scheduled wakes for running agents

# Paperclip upstream bug report (draft — for github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/issues)

**Version:** `2026.512.0` (self-hosted, `paperclip:local` built via `npm install -g paperclipai@2026.512.0`)

---

## Bug 1 — `GET /api/issues/:id/comments` 500s: Date passed as SQL param

**Symptom:** Loading comments on some issues returns 500; the agent assigned to that issue then cannot read board/user replies, so it loops (cancel → scheduled retry → "Run finished") and never responds.

**Error:**
```
GET /api/issues/SKI-65/comments 500 — Failed query: select ... from "heartbeat_runs" where (... coalesce("heartbeat_runs"."finished_at","heartbeat_runs"."created_at") >= $5 ... <= $6) ...
TypeError: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received an instance of Date
    at PostgresJsPreparedQuery.queryWithCache (drizzle-orm/pg-core/session.js:41:15)
    at enrichCommentsWithDerivedAgentAttribution (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/issues.js:1374:22)
    at Object.listComments (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/issues.js:2999:38)
```

**Root cause:** `enrichCommentsWithDerivedAgentAttribution` passes JS `Date` objects for the `$5`/`$6` bounds (`coalesce(finished_at,created_at) >= $5`, `<= $6`) to the `postgres-js`/drizzle driver, which requires strings. Convert to ISO strings (`.toISOString()`) before binding.

**Impact:** High — silently breaks the agent↔user reply loop on affected issues.

---

## Bug 2 — Agent instructions (`AGENTS.md`) omit the `/interactions` payload schema → agents 400

**Symptom:** A minority of `POST /api/issues/:id/interactions` calls 400, so the agent's question/confirmation never reaches the user and the task stalls in `in_review`. Captured wrong shapes:
- `kind: request_confirmation` with `payload: { title, body }`
- `kind: ask_user_questions` with **top-level** `questions: [...]`
- `kind: ask_user_questions` with `payload: { questions: [...] }` but questions using `question`/empty `options: []`

**Root cause:** `onboarding-assets/{default,ceo}/AGENTS.md` tells agents to POST interactions with `kind: ask_user_questions | request_confirmation | suggest_tasks` but **never documents the payload body shape**. Agents that don't already know it guess and 400.

**The actual required shape** (reverse-engineered from `issue_thread_interactions` rows that succeeded):
```jsonc
// ask_user_questions
{ "kind":"ask_user_questions","continuationPolicy":"wake_assignee",
  "payload": { "version":1, "questions":[
    { "id":"slug","prompt":"...","options":[{"id":"a","label":"..."}],"selectionMode":"single" } ] } }
// request_confirmation
{ "kind":"request_confirmation","continuationPolicy":"wake_assignee",
  "payload": { "version":1, "prompt":"...","allowDeclineReason":true } }
```

**Fix request:** document this payload schema in `AGENTS.md` (and ideally return a more descriptive 400 body naming the missing/invalid field).

**Impact:** Medium — intermittently strands tasks; the user never sees the question.

---

## Bonus (UX): structured questions can't be answered by comment
When a user replies to an `ask_user_questions` with a free-text **comment** instead of selecting an option, the interaction is not resolved (shows `cancelled`) and the agent keeps waiting. Consider accepting a comment on an issue with a pending question as an answer, or surfacing clearer UI that an option must be selected.
payload.title: Two bugs blocking the agent↔user loop: comments 500 (Date SQL param) + interactions payload schema undocumented

## Bug

Paperclip defaults `embeddedPostgresPort` to **54329** (hardcoded in `packages/shared/src/config-schema.ts:34` and `server/src/config.ts:305`). On Windows hosts running WSL2, Windows/Hyper-V dynamically reserves TCP port ranges. The range **54327–54426** is commonly reserved, causing all 20 ports in Paperclip's scan window (54329–54348) to return `EADDRINUSE`.

### Symptom

Service crash-loops on every WSL2 restart:
```
Error: Embedded PostgreSQL could not find a free port from 54329 to 54348
    at findAvailablePort (packages/db/src/migration-runtime.ts:75:9)
```

### Root Cause

Windows Hyper-V dynamic port exclusions (visible via `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp`) frequently include the 54327–54426 block. Paperclip's default port 54329 sits at the start of this range.

Verified on WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04, Windows 11):
```
Protocol tcp Port Exclusion Ranges
Start Port    End Port
----------    --------
     54327       54426
     54427       54526
     54527       54626
...
```

All 20 ports in the scan window (54329–54348) return `EADDRINUSE` even though no process is listening — Windows blocks new binds on those ports at the kernel level.

### Affected files

- `packages/shared/src/config-schema.ts:34` — `embeddedPostgresPort: z.number()...default(54329)`
- `packages/db/src/runtime-config.ts:223` — `const port = config?.database?.embeddedPostgresPort ?? 54329`
- `packages/db/src/test-embedded-postgres.ts:37` — constant
- `packages/db/src/backup.ts:39` — fallback
- `server/src/config.ts:305` — `embeddedPostgresPort: fileConfig?.database.embeddedPostgresPort ?? 54329`
- `server/src/worktree-config.ts:409` — equality check: `=== 54329`

### Suggested Fix

Change the default `embeddedPostgresPort` to **54000** (safely in the 52651–54326 free zone on typical WSL2 hosts) across all hardcoded references above.

### Workaround

Set `database.embeddedPostgresPort: 54000` in `~/.paperclip/instances/default/config.json`.
payload.title: Default embedded postgres port 54329 conflicts with WSL2/Hyper-V dynamic port exclusion range

payload.author: eq-pepe
payload.body:
**This proposal introduces the idea of a global concurrency limit for selected adapter types, specifically `opencode` and `litellm`.**

Currently, concurrency can be controlled at the individual agent level, but this does not prevent multiple agents using the same adapter from running at the same time. In practice, this can lead to too many concurrent sessions through the same backend, especially when several agents share a single local CLI adapter or LiteLLM gateway.

The goal is to allow Paperclip to define a shared concurrency bucket per adapter type. For example, all agents using `opencode` could share one global limit, while all agents using `litellm` could share a separate global limit.

**This would help with:**

* preventing too many simultaneous OpenCode sessions
* protecting LiteLLM gateways from overload
* reducing rate-limit and context-window errors
* improving stability when multiple agents share the same adapter
* making company-level resource usage easier to control

The intended behavior would be simple: if the global limit for a given adapter type is already reached, additional runs using that adapter should wait until an active run finishes.

This should apply only to selected adapter types where global coordination is useful, such as `opencode` and `litellm`, rather than changing concurrency behavior for all adapters by default.
payload.title: Idea: Global concurrency limit per adapter type

payload.body:
## Summary

Manager / CEO agents have **no API to cancel a stale heartbeat run** for another agent on the same fleet. When Paperclip's watchdog detects an agent has gone silent it files a `Review silent active run for <Agent>` issue assigned to the manager — but the manager has no programmatic lever to actually reap the run. The only working paths today are:

- Reassign or PATCH the *source* issue's status to invalidate the lingering checkout (indirect, side-effecty)
- Wait for a board/human user to cancel the run from the UI
- Apply the manager 3-step re-assign / `/release` / re-assign dance documented in #6399

So the watchdog ticket the manager receives is, in practice, a notification-only artifact. The watchdog asks the manager to "review and resolve", but the resolution surface only exists in the board UI.

## Real-world impact (Ratiq, 2026-05-30)

- QA Engineer (`codex_local`) had a stale session.
- Paperclip filed `Review silent active run for QA Engineer` watchdog tickets every heartbeat cycle.
- 357 such tickets accumulated, all assigned to the CEO agent.
- CEO closed each one as `done` after triage but had no way to actually kill QA's stuck run.
- After ~5 hours the board user had to manually cancel the QA run from the UI.
- Board feedback (verbatim): *"Why did you spam the issues section with the Silent Active Run for QA Engineer without actually solving the issue?? I had to come and cancel the QAs run manually five hours later. Why didn't you stop or Paperclip stop him when you saw the stale session??"*

The watchdog is doing its job (it correctly detected silence). The platform reaper is doing its job per #3168/#6399 constraints (won't kill an "alive" pid). The gap is: **the manager agent the watchdog notifies has no power to act**.

## Proposed feature

Expose an authenticated, role-gated run-reap endpoint that managers/CEO agents can call themselves:

```
POST /api/agents/{agentId}/runs/{runId}/cancel
POST /api/issues/{issueId}/force-release
```

Behaviour:

- Cancels the named `heartbeat_runs` row (sets terminal status, frees the `issues.executionRunId` lock per #6399).
- Best-effort kills the adapter-side process (same code path as the board's existing Cancel button).
- AuthZ: caller must be a manager of `agentId` per `chainOfCommand`, or be the agent's CEO, or have a `runs:reap` company permission. Refuse cross-company calls (existing company-boundary rule applies).
- Idempotent on already-terminal runs.
- Emits an audit log entry tying the reap to the caller's `runId` (via existing `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` header).

Optional but recommended:

- Have the watchdog `Review silent active run` issue include a one-call hint (e.g. `POST /api/agents/<agent>/runs/<run>/cancel`) in its description so the manager has a runnable action, not just a notification.

## Why this is the right shape

- Watchdog tickets are already routed to a manager. Giving that manager the power to act collapses the loop without requiring board intervention.
- Today the platform forces escalation to a human user for what is, in spirit, an operational reap. That violates Paperclip's own "never ask a human to do what an agent could do" rule.
- This is orthogonal to (and complementary with) #3168 (auto-cancel queued runs whose issues are done), #5871 (claude_local parent-process leak), and #6399 (zombie executionRunId lock). Those fix the *underlying* leak. This issue covers the *recovery surface* an operator agent needs while those longer-term fixes land.

## Related issues

- #3168 — Orphaned runs block agent queue (auto-cancel queued runs on issue close + zombie reaper logic).
- #5871 — claude_local parent process leak after run completion.
- #6399 — Zombie executionRunId lock; proposes board-only `POST /api/issues/:id/admin/force-release`. **The fix proposed here is to lift that endpoint's auth gate to manager/CEO agents, or expose an agent-facing equivalent.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New endpoint(s) documented and shipped; existing boar
payload.title: Feature: agent-facing run-reap API so managers can resolve 'Review silent active run' watchdogs without board intervention

## Summary

The recovery sweep in `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues()` sweeps `in_progress` issues to `blocked` when no active execution path exists, but has no exemption for issues that are the parent of an active routine. Long-lived lifecycle issues whose only continuation path is a scheduled routine appear "orphaned" to the sweep between routine fires.

## Bug Location

- **Package:** `@paperclipai/server`
- **File:** `src/services/recovery/service.ts`
- **Function:** `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues()` (~line 1862)

## Root Cause

The recovery sweep selects all `in_progress` issues with `assigneeAgentId` set. It sweeps them to `blocked` when no active execution path (running run or deferred wakeup) exists. The sweep has **no exemption for issues that are the parent of an active routine**.

A long-lived lifecycle issue (e.g. a weekly market analysis issue that runs for months) whose only continuation path is a weekly routine with `status=active` and a future `nextRunAt`, appears "orphaned" to the sweep between routine fires — even though the routine is a legitimate, active continuation path.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create a long-lived `in_progress` issue with `assigneeAgentId` set
2. Create a recurring routine with `parentIssueId` pointing to that issue
3. Wait for the recovery sweep to run (typically ~5 min interval)
4. Observe the issue is swept to `blocked` with assignee cleared, despite the routine being active

## Impact

- Occurring 3+ times/day in production usage
- Requires manual CEO intervention to restore issue state each time
- A daily keepalive routine workaround is in place but is not a correct fix

## Requested Fix

**Option A (preferred):** In `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues()`, add a skip condition:



SQL equivalent:


This is semantically correct: a routine parent issue has an implicit live continuation path.

**Option B (acceptable):** Expose a `workMode: "lifecycle"` or `dontAutoBlock: true` flag on issues to opt out of the recovery sweep.

## Workaround Currently In Use

A daily keepalive routine (separate from the actual weekly analysis routine) is running checkouts to prevent the sweep. This is wasteful and incorrect — the sweep should recognize routine-backed lifecycle issues natively.

## Version

paperclipai CLI version: 2026.525.0
payload.title: Bug: reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues() sweeps routine-backed lifecycle issues to blocked between routine fires

## Summary

Driving the Kimi Code CLI (`kimi acp`) through the **`acpx_local`** adapter (mode: persistent), the agent's **Shell tool fails repeatedly** with `acp.exceptions.RequestError: Internal error` — including on trivial commands like `echo hello`. The agent reasons fine but cannot reliably execute shell/git/`gh` commands, so it loops, spawns subagents to work around it, and frequently ends a run without completing (the issue resets to `todo`/`blocked`).

## Environment

- Paperclip `2026.525.0` (deploymentMode `local_trusted`, macOS arm64)
- kimi-cli: reproduced on **both 1.37.0 and 1.46.0** (upgrading the CLI did not fix it)
- Adapter: `acpx_local` — `{mode: persistent, agent: kimi, permissionMode: approve-all}`
- Affected: every agent on `acpx_local`/kimi. `codex_local`, `claude_local`, `hermes_local` are unaffected.

## Logs (sanitized — `~/.kimi/logs/kimi.log`)

```
ERROR kimi_cli.soul.toolset:_call - Tool execution failed: Shell (call_id=...)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ... Params(command='sh -c echo hello', timeout=60, run_in_background=False)
  <Future finished exception=RequestError('Internal error')>
acp.exceptions.RequestError: Internal error
```

Second failure mode, on large command output:

```
ERROR kimi_cli.tools.shell - Shell command execution failed:
  curl ... : Separator is not found, and chunk exceed the limit
```

Frequency: ~26 Shell `Internal error`s in a single agent run.

## Impact

Agents on this adapter are unreliable for any shell/git/`gh`-dependent task (code review, PR ops, etc.). One run produced a correct result only after ~26 failed shell calls plus subagent workarounds — high token cost, low reliability.

## Ruled out

- **Not the model** (Kimi-K2.6 / `kimi-for-coding`, 256K ctx — reasoning is fine).
- **Not the CLI version** (persists 1.37.0 → 1.46.0).
- Error originates at the ACP shell-execution boundary (kimi ACP server ⇄ `acpx_local` client returns `Internal error`).

## Repro

1. Configure an agent with `acpx_local` (agent=kimi, mode=persistent).
2. Assign it a task requiring shell (e.g. run `gh`/`git`).
3. Observe `acp.exceptions.RequestError: Internal error` on Shell tool calls in `~/.kimi/logs/kimi.log`.

## Workaround

Route shell-heavy / critical agents to `codex_local` or `claude_local`.
payload.title: acpx_local adapter: Shell tool fails with acp.exceptions.RequestError: Internal error (kimi agents)

payload.author: HaydenRic
payload.body:
## Feature Request

### Problem

When an agent run fails, Paperclip creates a recovery action. If the recovery agent also fails, a new recovery action is created — and this can cascade repeatedly with no ceiling. We experienced this on May 24, 2026:

- **1,136 runs in a single day** (12× our normal daily volume)
- **8% success rate** (95 succeeded, 1,032 failed)
- Root cause: model failures triggered recovery agents, which also failed, generating further recovery actions — 4+ levels deep

Issues carry a `requestDepth` field internally, confirming that recovery depth is already tracked. However, there is no company-level configuration to cap that depth.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `maxRecoveryDepth` field to company-level configuration (recommended default: `2`):

```json
{
  "companySettings": {
    "maxRecoveryDepth": 2
  }
}
```

### Auto-Escalation Behaviour When Depth Is Reached

Instead of creating another recovery action when `maxRecoveryDepth` is exceeded, Paperclip should:

1. **Set the issue to `blocked`** automatically (rather than creating a deeper recovery action)
2. **Send a board notification** indicating the issue was auto-blocked due to recovery depth limit
3. Log the depth exceeded in the heartbeat run for debugging

### Expected Behaviour

| Recovery depth | Current behaviour | Proposed behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 0–(max-1) | Creates recovery action | Same |
| max | Creates another recovery action (unbounded) | Sets issue to `blocked`, notifies board |

### Why `blocked` (not `cancelled` or `failed`)

`blocked` is the right terminal state for this case — the issue is not cancelled or abandoned, it just needs human attention before it can proceed. A board notification ensures the issue does not silently rot.

### Urgency

The root cause of our May 24 storm (model failures) is being fixed separately. But **this circuit breaker is needed as defence-in-depth** — any future model degradation or unexpected failure mode could re-trigger the same cascade pattern without a depth cap.

Our run data for context:
- Normal daily run volume: ~90–250 runs
- May 24 (cascade day): 1,136 runs, 8% success

### Environment

- Paperclip (latest)
- Company with 6 active agents
- Recovery actions currently uncapped at company level

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

A CodeReviewer session in the Crossroads local deployment hit a Cloudflare bot challenge on the issue write surface while trying to POST/PATCH review/handoff evidence. The agent could read enough context to produce a review, but the write path was blocked, forcing evidence to be posted through `local-board` or later recovery paths instead of the active reviewer identity.

## Observed

- Context: Crossroads executionPolicy migration / CRO-6295 recovery, observed 2026-05-28 14:40 UTC in the CR environment.
- A reviewer attempted to write review/handoff state through the normal Paperclip API surface.
- The request path encountered a Cloudflare bot challenge rather than a normal API response the agent runtime could handle.
- Result: reviewer evidence existed, but durable issue-state changes had to be routed through fallback/local-board surfaces, increasing the chance of executionPolicy state drift and manual recovery.

## Expected

Agent-authenticated API POST/PATCH traffic should not receive a browser-oriented Cloudflare bot challenge. If an edge/WAF policy blocks an agent write, the API should return a machine-readable 4xx/5xx with a stable error code and request id, or bypass the challenge for authenticated service/API routes.

## Crossrefs

- Crossroads CRO-6442 board escalation, Bucket B.
- Related but distinct executionPolicy runtime defects: #6983.

No local `/opt/paperclip` patch was made.
payload.title: bug: Cloudflare bot challenge blocks authenticated agent issue writes

payload.author: mrveiss
payload.body:
## Summary

The `claude_local` adapter spawns `script -q -e -c "claude ..."` for each heartbeat run but never reaps those processes after the run completes or the server crashes. On a system running ~10 agents with 600-second heartbeat intervals, orphaned `script` processes (and their `claude` children) accumulate continuously and drive the host to OOM.

## Environment

- Paperclip v0.3.1, `local_trusted` deployment mode
- Adapter: `claude_local`
- OS: Linux 6.6.114 (WSL2), Ubuntu
- ~17 agents configured, 10+ with active heartbeat timers

## Reproduction

1. Configure 10+ agents with `claude_local` adapter and heartbeat `intervalSec: 600`
2. Run for 2–4 hours
3. Observe `ps aux | grep script` — process count grows by ~1–2 per heartbeat fire across all agents
4. After ~2 hours: 170+ orphaned `script` processes, ~50 GB RSS consumed

## Evidence

After ~2 hours of normal operation on a single host:

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,comm | awk '$2==1 && $3=="script"' | wc -l
171

$ ps aux | grep -E 'claude|script' | grep -v grep | \
    awk '{sum += $6} END {printf "RSS: %.1f GB\n", sum/1024/1024}'
RSS: 48.9 GB
```

All 171 `script` processes had `ppid=1` (reparented to init), confirming they were orphaned by Paperclip rather than by any other process. Killing them freed ~47 GB immediately:

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,comm | awk '$2==1 && $3=="script" {print $1}' | xargs kill
$ ps aux | grep -E 'claude|script' | grep -v grep | \
    awk '{sum += $6} END {printf "RSS: %.1f GB\n", sum/1024/1024}'
RSS: 1.8 GB
```

Systemd reported the service at **37.4 GB** before cleanup, causing two OOM-triggered restarts within 3 hours.

## Expected behaviour

When a heartbeat run completes (success, failure, timeout, or cancellation), the adapter should `SIGTERM` the `script` process and wait for it to exit. On server crash/restart, orphaned `script` processes from the previous server instance should be killed during `ExecStartPre` or detected and reaped on startup.

## Suggested fix

Two places to patch:

**1. Adapter run teardown** — after the `claude` subprocess exits (or is killed), explicitly kill the `script` wrapper by PID:

```typescript
// In claude_local adapter, after run completion:
if (scriptProcess && !scriptProcess.killed) {
  scriptProcess.kill('SIGTERM');
  await scriptProcess.exitCode;
}
```

**2. Startup cleanup** — on server start, kill any `script` processes whose parent is PID 1 and whose command line matches the claude invocation pattern:

```bash
# Add to dev:stop or server startup:
pkill -P 1 -f 'script.*claude.*agent-instructions' 2>/dev/null || true
```

## Workaround

Until fixed, a cron job on the host cleans up orphans every 15 minutes:

```bash
*/15 * * * * ps -eo pid,ppid,comm | awk '$2==1 && $3=="script" {print $1}' | xargs -r kill 2>/dev/null
```

## Impact

- **Severity:** High — causes repeated OOM crashes on any multi-agent deployment running for more than ~2 hours
- **Trigger:** Normal operation, no unusual load required
- **Frequency:** Deterministic — every heartbeat fire leaks one process
payload.title: bug(claude_local): orphaned `script` processes accumulate and exhaust memory — adapter never cleans up on run completion or server crash

payload.author: Lattimius
payload.body:
## Summary

Paperclip executionPolicy handling has two related runtime defects that can strand policy-driven issues during review/publish handoff:

1. A reviewer PATCH that explicitly sets `assigneeAgentId` while moving out of review can be silently reinterpreted as `changes_requested`, overriding the caller's explicit assignee and routing back to `returnAssignee`.
2. `POST /api/issues/:id/release` clears `checkoutRunId` / `executionRunId` but leaves execution-policy stage state in place, so subsequent recovery PATCHes can remain blocked by the active-reviewer guard.

Observed in a local Paperclip deployment while migrating a production workflow to embedded `executionPolicy`. No local `/opt/paperclip` patch was made.

## Defect 1: explicit assignee PATCH is silently overwritten

### Observed

A reviewer on an active `review` stage attempted a legacy approval handoff by PATCHing the issue to a non-`in_review` status with an explicit CodePusher assignee. The API accepted the write / comment path, but the executionPolicy interceptor treated the non-`in_review` status as `changes_requested` and routed the issue back to `returnAssignee` instead of the explicit assignee.

Local repro/evidence refs: CRO-6295, CRO-6353. Both had APPROVE / handoff-to-CodePusher comments, then ended up back on the implementer with `executionState.status=changes_requested`, `lastDecisionOutcome=changes_requested`, and `returnAssignee` as the implementer.

### Expected

If a reviewer PATCH provides an explicit assignee that conflicts with workflow-controlled routing, the runtime should either:

- honor the explicit handoff when it is valid for that transition, or
- reject the PATCH with a clear 4xx explaining that workflow-controlled assignment must be advanced through the policy decision path.

It should not return success while silently discarding the explicit assignee and relabeling the action as changes requested.

### Source pointer

`server/src/services/issue-execution-policy.ts` around the reviewer stage branch:

- `requestedStatus && requestedStatus !== "in_review"` enters the changes-requested path.
- The branch requires `returnAssignee`, sets `patch.status = "in_progress"`, applies `patchForPrincipal(existingState.returnAssignee)`, and returns `outcome: "changes_requested"` with `workflowControlledAssignment: true`.
- It does not appear to reject or explicitly account for a caller-provided `assigneeAgentId` that differs from `returnAssignee`.

## Defect 2: release half-clears execution state and leaves a 422 lock

### Observed

After `POST /api/issues/:id/release`, issue rows had `executionRunId: null` and `checkoutRunId: null`, but retained active execution-policy state such as `executionState.currentStageId`, `currentParticipant`, and `lastDecisionId`. Subsequent recovery PATCHes then continued to fail with:

`Only the active reviewer or approver can advance the current execution stage`

Local repro/evidence refs: CRO-6415, CRO-6321, plus related review-deadlock comments on CRO-6295/CRO-6353. CRO-6415 is a clear surviving-state example: `executionRunId=null`, `checkoutRunId=null`, status still `in_review`, and `executionState.currentStageId` / `currentParticipant` still populated.

### Expected

`release` should either:

- fully clear execution-stage state when it clears run/check-out ownership, so manual reassignment/recovery works, or
- expose a documented re-entry/recovery path that does not leave the issue in a permanent active-stage guard state.

### Source pointer

`server/src/services/issues.ts` `release` currently updates fields including:

- `status: "todo"`
- `assigneeAgentId: null`
- `checkoutRunId: null`
- `executionRunId: null`
- `executionAgentNameKey: null`
- `executionLockedAt: null`

It does not appear to clear or reset `executionState`.

The active-stage guard in `server/src/services/issue-execution-policy.ts` later rejects attempted stage advancement with the quoted 422 when the stale stage state still looks active.

## Impa
payload.title: bug: executionPolicy reviewer handoff and release recovery can strand issues

payload.author: pirenjo-dev
payload.body:
## Problem

When an issue is marked as a duplicate of or superseded by another issue, the current wake payload and `GET /api/issues/{id}/heartbeat-context` response contain no structured fields pointing to the canonical execution path. Agents must manually determine which issue is canonical — typically by reading free-text comments or fetching the full issue thread — which generates unnecessary routing overhead (e.g. creating a "this issue is a duplicate of X" child just to communicate what the platform already knows).

**Concrete pattern observed:** An agent receives a wake on a duplicate/superseded issue, finds no structured canonical reference, creates a manual routing issue to explain "Issue A is a duplicate of Issue B, which has status in_review", then closes the duplicate. All of that information was already present in the system state.

---

## Proposed Change

### 1. Wake Payload Extension (Required)

Extend the wake payload and `heartbeat-context` response with four new fields when the woken issue has a `duplicateOf` or `supersededBy` relationship:

```json
{
  "canonicalIssueId": "<uuid>",
  "canonicalIssueIdentifier": "ACME-302",
  "canonicalIssueStatus": "in_review",
  "canonicalIssueTitle": "Deploy production hotfix"
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `canonicalIssueId` | `string (uuid)` | UUID of the canonical issue (`duplicateOf` / `supersededBy`) |
| `canonicalIssueIdentifier` | `string` | Human-readable identifier (e.g. `ACME-302`) |
| `canonicalIssueStatus` | `string` | Current status of the canonical issue at wake time |
| `canonicalIssueTitle` | `string` | Title of the canonical issue |

#### Availability

Fields must appear in **both**:
- `PAPERCLIP_WAKE_PAYLOAD_JSON` (inline wake context)
- `GET /api/issues/{id}/heartbeat-context` response

This allows agents to use canonical info without an additional API call.

#### Null / Absent Handling

When no `duplicateOf` / `supersededBy` is set: fields are **omitted** (not `null`). Agents check for field presence, not `null`.

#### Caching

`canonicalIssueStatus` is a **live read** at wake time — not a cached value from when the duplicate relationship was created. Agents need the current status to decide their triage action.

#### Edge Cases

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Canonical issue is `done` | `canonicalIssueStatus: "done"` → agent can close immediately |
| Canonical is itself superseded (chain) | Payload reflects direct reference only (1 hop); no recursive resolution |
| Canonical issue was deleted | Fields are omitted (no wake error) |
| Circular reference (A supersedes B, B supersedes A) | Platform prevents circular refs at write time — not an edge case in wake |

---

### 2. Standardized Close Reason `superseded_already_closed` (Optional, non-blocking)

Introduce a new `closedReason` value for `PATCH /api/issues/{id}`:

```json
{
  "status": "done",
  "closedReason": "superseded_already_closed",
  "comment": "Superseded by ACME-302."
}
```

**Benefit:** Enables filtering in dashboards/audit: `closedReason=superseded_already_closed` shows all duplicate-triage closures separately from substantive completions. Additive field — no breaking change.

This part is independent and can land in a separate iteration.

---

## Expected Agent Behavior After Change

```
IF canonicalIssueStatus == "done"
  → set issue to done with comment:
    "Superseded by [canonicalIssueIdentifier] — canonical issue is done."
ELSE
  → set issue to blocked, blockedByIssueIds: [canonicalIssueId]
    comment: "Canonical path: [canonicalIssueIdentifier] — status: {canonicalIssueStatus}"
```

No routing issue needed in either case — the agent has machine-readable canonical info inline.

---

## Scope & Impact

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Backend change | Yes — wake payload generation + heartbeat-context endpoint |
| API breaking change | **No** — additive fields only |
| UI change | No |
| Estimate | < 1 sprint (DB lookup + payload mapping) |
| Risk
payload.title: feat(heartbeat-context): add canonicalIssueId/Status to wake payload for duplicate/superseded issues
