payload.author: legacykeeperops
payload.body:
## Problem

Critical agent configuration settings are only accessible via raw SQL or JSON editing against the embedded PostgreSQL database. A normal Paperclip user has no way to discover or change these settings through the dashboard UI. This leads to preventable incidents:

- We had 235 queued heartbeats crash our server (#6955) because `maxConcurrentRuns` defaults to unlimited and there is no UI to change it
- Budget hard-stops froze all agents for 10+ hours (#6843 context) because we backfilled cost data and could not adjust budgets from the UI
- Agent model changes require a 3-step SQL operation (adapter_config + runtime_config + session purge) — we documented this as an internal "skill" because it is so error-prone
- Heartbeat intervals require JSON editing in runtime_config — there is no slider or input field

## What should be in the dashboard UI

### Per-agent settings (Agent detail page)
1. **Heartbeat interval** — slider or input field (currently hidden in `runtime_config.heartbeat.intervalSec`)
2. **Max concurrent runs** — dropdown: 1, 2, 3 (currently hidden, defaults to unlimited which causes stacking)
3. **Primary model** — dropdown of available models (currently requires editing `adapter_config.model`)
4. **Cheap/fallback model** — dropdown (currently nested in `runtime_config.modelProfiles.cheap.adapterConfig.model`)
5. **Effort level** — dropdown: low, medium, high (currently in `adapter_config.effort`)
6. **Wake on demand** — toggle (currently in `runtime_config.heartbeat.wakeOnDemand`)
7. **Timer enabled** — toggle to disable timer heartbeats while keeping wake-on-demand (currently `runtime_config.heartbeat.enabled`)

### Company-level settings
8. **Budget policies** — per-agent and company-wide spend limits with warning threshold and hard-stop toggle (currently only in `budget_policies` table via SQL)
9. **Global model defaults** — set default model for new agents
10. **Heartbeat stacking protection** — global toggle to prevent any agent from having more than 1 concurrent run (should be ON by default)

### Visibility (dashboard widgets)
11. **Queued heartbeat count** — show how many heartbeats are queued per agent. If >0, show a warning.
12. **Heartbeat duration history** — show avg/p95 heartbeat duration per agent so operators can set intervals appropriately
13. **Budget burn rate** — show current spend vs budget with projected exhaustion date
14. **Model cost comparison** — show token cost per agent per day to help with model selection

## Why this matters

Paperclip is powerful but its configuration surface is invisible to normal users. Every setting we needed to change during a 24-hour operational session required SSH + psql + raw SQL. We ended up building 36 internal "skills" (documented procedures) just to operate Paperclip safely. Most of these skills would be unnecessary if the settings were in the UI.

The heartbeat stacking incident (#6955) would not have happened if there was a visible "max concurrent runs" dropdown defaulting to 1 on the agent settings page.
payload.title: feat(ui): expose agent configuration settings in the dashboard — heartbeat intervals, concurrent limits, budgets, models

payload.author: legacykeeperops
payload.body:
## Environment
- Paperclip version: 2026.525.0
- Server: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM
- Agents: 11 (4 timer, 7 task-activated)

## Bug

When an agent's heartbeat takes longer than its `intervalSec`, Paperclip queues a new heartbeat run every interval tick without checking if a previous run is still active. This causes unbounded queue growth and server overload.

In our case:
- CTO agent on Claude Opus with `intervalSec: 1200` (20 minutes)
- Single heartbeat took 130 minutes (heavy architectural work)
- Paperclip queued 116 additional heartbeat runs during that time
- COO had 42 queued, CEO had 40, Lead Backend had 20
- Total: **235 queued heartbeat runs** piled up
- Server load hit 14x on 4 CPUs — dashboard completely unresponsive

## Expected Behavior

Paperclip should NOT queue a new heartbeat run if the agent already has an active (running) heartbeat. The `maxConcurrentRuns` setting exists but defaults to unlimited — it should default to 1.

## Current Workaround

Manually set `maxConcurrentRuns: 1` in every agent's runtime config:

```json
{"heartbeat": {"intervalSec": 5400, "maxConcurrentRuns": 1}}
```

And periodically cancel stacked runs:
```sql
UPDATE heartbeat_runs_2026_05 SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE status = 'queued';
```

## Suggested Fix

1. Default `maxConcurrentRuns` to 1 (not unlimited)
2. Before queuing a timer heartbeat, check if the agent already has a running heartbeat — skip if so
3. Add a warning log when a heartbeat exceeds its interval: "Agent X heartbeat took Y minutes, interval is Z minutes — consider increasing interval"
4. Consider auto-adjusting the interval when heartbeats consistently exceed it

## Impact

Without the workaround, the server becomes unusable within 1-2 hours of enabling agents. The queued runs consume database connections, CPU, and memory even though they accomplish nothing (the previous heartbeat already covered the same work).

This is the second time we've reported server overload from Paperclip's database query patterns (see #6947). Combined, these two issues make it difficult to run more than 5 agents on a 4-CPU server.
payload.title: bug: heartbeat timer queues unlimited runs when heartbeat duration exceeds interval — maxConcurrentRuns should default to 1

payload.author: legacykeeperops
payload.body:
## Environment
- Paperclip version: 2026.525.0
- Server: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04
- Agents: 11 active (4 timer, 7 task-activated)
- Database: embedded PostgreSQL on port 54329

## Problem

When multiple agents heartbeat concurrently, the server load spikes to 10-12x (on 4 CPUs) because each heartbeat query selects ALL 47 columns from `heartbeat_runs` including three large JSONB fields:

- `context_snapshot`: ~5KB average per row
- `result_json`: ~1KB average per row
- `usage_json`: ~373 bytes per row

With 44K rows in the monthly partition and 9 concurrent agent queries, each heartbeat fetches megabytes of data from disk even when it only needs a few scalar fields (status, started_at, agent_id).

## Impact

- Server load average 10-12x on 4 CPUs during concurrent heartbeats
- Paperclip dashboard becomes unresponsive for 2-5 minutes
- 689MB swap usage from memory pressure
- All 11 agent heartbeats compete for CPU, slowing each other

## Query pattern observed

```sql
select "id", "company_id", "agent_id", "invocation_source", "trigger_detail",
  "status", "started_at", "finished_at", "error", "wakeup_request_id",
  "exit_code", "signal", "usage_json", "result_json", ...
  "context_snapshot", "created_at", "updated_at"
from "heartbeat_runs"
where ("heartbeat_runs"."company_id" = $1
  and "heartbeat_runs"."agent_id" = $2
  and ("heartbeat_runs"."context_snapshot"...))
```

All 47 columns selected even though most callers likely only need status + timestamps.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Use SELECT with specific columns** instead of SELECT * for heartbeat queries that only need status/timing info
2. **Exclude large JSONB columns** (context_snapshot, result_json, usage_json) from listing queries — fetch them only when viewing a specific run's detail
3. **Add connection pooling or query queuing** to prevent N concurrent heartbeats from all hitting the DB simultaneously
4. **Stagger heartbeat dispatch** more aggressively — current jitter of 120s helps but all agents still fire within the same window after a restart

## Workaround

We added a covering index to serve common queries from the index without heap access:
```sql
CREATE INDEX heartbeat_runs_agent_lookup_idx
ON heartbeat_runs_2026_05 (company_id, agent_id, status, started_at DESC)
INCLUDE (finished_at, error_code, invocation_source, trigger_detail, liveness_state);
```

This helps filtering but doesn't prevent the full-row fetch when all columns are selected.

## Server metrics during incident
- Load average: 10.28 / 10.41 / 11.15
- 9 Postgres connections all in 'active' state running the same SELECT
- Zero idle connections
- Swap: 689MB used
payload.title: perf: heartbeat_runs queries select all 47 columns including large JSONB — causes CPU saturation with concurrent agents

payload.author: Lattimius
payload.body:
## Summary

Add an authenticated, audited server-owned maintenance surface for Paperclip's embedded Postgres so operators can diagnose and safely run routine bloat maintenance without exposing database credentials to agents or touching Postgres data files directly.

## Incident context

This follows Crossroads CRO-6400 / CRO-6417, from the same single-tenant disk-exhaustion incident that produced #6931.

Live instance facts captured during the CRO-6400 investigation:

- Embedded Postgres data directory was about 3.3 GiB.
- `db/base` was about 2.9 GiB.
- `pg_wal` was about 353-417 MiB during checks.
- The autovacuum launcher was running.
- The local embedded package did not expose bundled `psql`, `vacuumdb`, or `pg_isready` for agent-safe operator use.
- A direct Node `pg` connection attempt to `paperclip@127.0.0.1:54329/paperclip` failed with password authentication required.
- The engineer did not read credentials and did not edit Postgres data files directly.

The local retention fix can prune Paperclip backups and run logs, but it does not give operators a safe way to inspect or maintain embedded Postgres bloat. Autovacuum may be sufficient for normal operation, but operators still need a supported diagnostic/maintenance path and an auditable receipt when disk pressure investigations point at the embedded database.

## Requirements

1. Provide a server-owned maintenance command or API that uses Paperclip's own authenticated database connection, not agent-discovered credentials.
2. Support a safe bloat/status diagnostic mode that reports at least:
   - database size
   - major relation/table sizes
   - dead/live tuple indicators where available
   - WAL directory size or WAL-related status where available
   - autovacuum activity/status evidence where available
   - timestamp and Paperclip instance identifier if one exists
3. Support a conservative maintenance action such as `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` for the Paperclip database.
4. Return a durable/auditable maintenance receipt containing:
   - actor/request id
   - requested operation
   - start/end timestamps
   - success/failure
   - before/after size/status summary where practical
   - database-health evidence after the operation
5. Expose clear safety constraints:
   - no direct edits or deletes inside the Postgres data directory
   - no database password/connection-string exposure in output, logs, comments, agent context, or receipts
   - no `VACUUM FULL` or other blocking/rewrite-heavy operation unless explicitly gated by a stronger admin confirmation path
   - refuse or warn when the server is already in a disk-critical state where maintenance could worsen outage risk
6. Document whether Paperclip's intended policy is "autovacuum only" instead. If so, the product should expose diagnostics explaining why no manual maintenance action is supported and what operators should monitor.

## Possible shape

Either shape is fine if it preserves the safety contract:

- Admin HTTP endpoint, for example `POST /api/admin/maintenance/postgres` with `{ "operation": "diagnose" | "vacuum_analyze", "dryRun": true | false }`.
- CLI command, for example `paperclipai maintenance postgres diagnose` and `paperclipai maintenance postgres vacuum-analyze`.

In both cases the server process should own credential use, authorization, logging, and redaction.

## Tests / verification

Please include coverage for:

- diagnostics returning expected fields without secrets
- successful `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` execution against a test embedded database
- receipt persistence or log emission with redacted output
- failure path when the DB is unreachable
- authorization failure for a non-admin/non-operator caller if exposed over HTTP
- refusal/warning behavior under a synthetic critical-disk condition if implemented with #6931's disk-health guard

## Downstream operator recommendation

Until this exists, Crossroads should not schedule agent-run Postgres maintenance and should rely on Paperclip autovacuum plus backup/ru
payload.title: Safe embedded Postgres diagnostics and maintenance surface

payload.author: Lattimius
payload.body:
## Summary

Add server-side disk free-space protection to Paperclip so the health/status surface warns before embedded Postgres is forced into an outage, and so Paperclip can stop dispatching new agent heartbeats at critical disk usage while preserving recovery access.

## Incident context

A single-tenant Paperclip instance hit root filesystem exhaustion on 2026-05-29:

- Root filesystem reached 100% usage on a 118G volume.
- Paperclip's Node server stayed alive.
- Embedded Postgres on `127.0.0.1:54329` stopped accepting connections.
- `/api/health` returned `database_unreachable` while DB-backed APIs failed.
- Emergency cleanup restored service.
- Local retention mitigation later removed 14,820 old backup/run-log files, measured 3.6 GiB removed, with a 3.7 GiB filesystem free-space delta.
- Post-mitigation health was `status=ok`; disk was about 86G used / 28G free / 76%.

The local retention job is only an operator-side mitigation. Paperclip itself should fail safely before disk pressure takes the embedded database offline.

## Requirements

1. Extend Paperclip's own health/status endpoint to report disk status for the instance/root filesystem:
   - total bytes
   - used bytes
   - available bytes
   - percent used
   - threshold state
   - timestamp
2. Preserve existing `/api/health` database checks. Disk status must complement database status, not mask `database_unreachable` or other DB failures.
3. Add threshold states at 85%, 90%, and 95% used, with visible warning/alert semantics appropriate for operators and agents.
4. Add a critical fail-safe at the critical threshold: automatically pause or refuse new agent heartbeat dispatches before embedded Postgres is forced into outage.
5. Preserve already-running work where feasible, and preserve human/API access needed to recover from the condition.
6. Do not rely on downstream instance cleanup tools such as Crossroads' `tools/paperclip-instance-retention`.

## Suggested behavior

- Healthy: disk state appears in `/api/health`, status remains healthy when database and other existing checks are healthy.
- Warning/alert: `/api/health` exposes a warning/alert state while continuing normal service.
- Critical: new heartbeat dispatches are paused/refused with a clear machine-readable reason, while the UI/API surfaces enough detail for operators to clean up and recover.
- Disk check failure: health response reports the disk-check failure explicitly without incorrectly reporting disk health as OK.

## Tests / verification

Please include coverage for:

- healthy disk state
- 85% warning threshold
- 90% alert threshold
- 95% critical threshold
- disk-check failure path
- critical dispatch guard blocking new heartbeat dispatch under a synthetic low-space condition
- existing database health behavior continuing to report DB failures independently of disk status

## Downstream reference

Tracked from Crossroads issue CRO-6415, created from the CRO-6396 disk exhaustion incident and CRO-6400 permanent prevention plan.
payload.title: Health endpoint disk thresholds and critical heartbeat auto-pause

payload.author: smaugho
payload.body:
## Problem / Context
When clicking on a child workflow (or reused workflow) node on the canvas, nothing distinguishable happens — it appears to only collapse/expand the node (unclear). The expectation is that clicking it navigates to edit the corresponding workflow.

Note: the step modal for a child workflow already exposes an `Open workflow → <slug>` link (e.g. `Open workflow → director-proactive-task-queue-management`), so the navigation target exists — but clicking the node itself does not trigger it.

## Desired outcome
Clicking a child/reused workflow node opens (navigates to) the corresponding workflow for editing.

## Acceptance criteria

payload.author: JulianWeiland
payload.body:
### Summary
CPU spikes on the Node.js app are **not** related to the Python openspace workers. The root cause is slow database queries combined with aggressive frontend polling, which creates a request pile-up that floods the Postgres connection pool and pins CPU.

### Root Cause
The frontend polls several endpoints continuously. When a query takes ~177s and new polls fire every few seconds, requests stack up faster than they can be served. At the worst spike (01:15:45), **231 requests hit in a single second — 178 of them `/issues`** — saturating the Postgres connection pool and pinning CPU.

### Worst Offenders (by hit count and response time)

| Endpoint | Slow requests | Avg response time | Worst case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/issues?limit=500&...` | 9,332 | 177s | 49 min |
| `/dashboard` | 2,872 | 151s | 32 min |
| `/heartbeat-runs?...` | 1,337 | 25s | 20 min |
| `/live-runs` | 976 | 23s | — |
| `/sidebar-badges` | 827 | 232s | 49 min |

### Why the queries are slow
The `issues` table is enormous. Offset-based pagination requests like `?page=10000&limit=100` force Postgres to scan at least 1,000,000 rows on every poll, which destroys performance.

### Proposed Fix (database/API side, not Python worker concurrency)
1. **Add a Postgres index** on the columns used by the `/issues` filter (`status`, `touchedByUserId`, `companyId`).
2. **Reduce polling frequency** for `/live-runs`, `/heartbeat-runs`, and `/sidebar-badges`.
3. **Cap the `limit=500` query** to a lower default, or replace offset pagination with **cursor-based pagination** (offset `page=10000` forces a full table scan).

### Component
`paperclipai` — Node.js app / frontend polling + Postgres
payload.title: Bug: CPU spikes caused by slow DB queries + aggressive frontend polling (request pile-up)

payload.author: sadeegamhewa
payload.body:
## Summary

`paperclipai agent get <id>` (with or without `--json`) returns the agent's full `adapterConfig` in plaintext, including any "Plain mode" secret values (`adapterConfig.env.<KEY>.value`) and any Paperclip API tokens that have been baked into `promptTemplate` strings. Similarly, the underlying `GET /api/agents/<id>` endpoint returns these in plaintext.

For deployments that use Plain mode (currently the only working option while #224 is unfixed) and the `hermes_local` adapter's recommended `promptTemplate` pattern (which embeds an agent API token so the agent can call back to Paperclip from inside its terminal tool), this means any user or LLM inspecting an agent's config inadvertently surfaces:

- API keys for third-party providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic, etc.)
- The agent's own Paperclip API token (with full agent-scope permissions on its company)

## Why this matters in practice

We hit this twice in two sessions while debugging Paperclip agent configuration in a Claude Code / LLM-driven workflow. Both times, the JSON output landed in a session transcript and required a full token rotation (regenerate OpenRouter key + regenerate the Welchman agent's Paperclip token + update every agent's `adapterConfig.env` + update every agent's `promptTemplate`). The rotation pass is ~25-30 minutes of mechanical work per incident.

The CLI and API have no obvious way to inspect agent shape without seeing secret values. So any future debugging session that needs to "see what fields exist in adapterConfig" or "compare adapter setups across agents" has to risk the same leak.

## Ask

Add a `--redact` flag (or make it the default with `--unsafe-show-secrets` for opt-in) on:

- `paperclipai agent get <id>` (CLI)
- `GET /api/agents/<id>` (API, gated by a request header or query param)
- `paperclipai company get <id>` (if it returns similar embedded secrets)

When `--redact` is set, any of the following should be replaced with placeholder strings like `<redacted:N-chars>`:

1. **`adapterConfig.env.<KEY>.value`** — when the envelope is `{"type": "plain", "value": "..."}`, redact the `value` while preserving `type`.
2. **`promptTemplate`** strings — substitute any matched secret patterns: `pcp_[a-f0-9]{32,}`, `sk-or-v\d+-[a-f0-9]{32,}`, `sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{50,}`, `sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}`.
3. **Any field at a SECRET_FIELDS path** — `token`, `apiKey`, `secret`, etc.

Returning the character length in the placeholder (`<redacted:108-chars>`) preserves enough information for debugging (you know whether the key is empty, the wrong format, etc.) without leaking the value itself.

## Workaround we built

For our own protection while this is unfixed, we ship a Python wrapper at `scripts/paperclipai-safe` in our internal repo that intercepts `paperclipai` stdout, parses JSON, walks the structure, and applies the redactions described above before re-emitting. Source happy to share if useful as a reference.

## Related

- Issue #224 (broken inline secret references) — the reason Plain mode is the current working option; if #224 were fixed, secret references would not appear in agent config inspection at all and this issue would be less acute. But even then, `promptTemplate` strings with baked-in agent tokens would still leak.
payload.title: Add --redact flag to agent/company get + GET /api/agents/<id> to prevent secret leakage in inspection workflows

payload.author: dmitry-cashtime
payload.body:
Hi team,

We run Paperclip in production at CashTime Pay AG, where 13 AI agents (`AICEO`, `AIPM`, `AIBM-Recon`, `AIBM-Outreach`, `AICROPS`, `AISMM`, etc.) drive our daily Sales/Outreach pipeline. They depend on a Paperclip board API token (`pcp_board_*`) to:
- Create heartbeat runs and wakeup requests via `POST /api/agents/:id/wakeup`
- Create / comment / close Plane-mirrored issues
- Coordinate handoffs between agents through `cashtime-agent-bus`

This token sits in `~/stack/cashtime_agent_bus/.env` as `PAPERCLIP_API_TOKEN` and is read by a `systemd`-managed service that runs every 15 minutes (`cashtime-aibm-trigger.timer`).

**Today our outreach pipeline silently broke** because the token expired at exactly `2026-05-28 11:11:40 UTC` — 30 days after creation. Every AIBMO dispatch since then returns `401 Unauthorized` from `POST /api/companies/.../issues`, so no outreach issue has been created on a real lead since 11:11 today (we caught it ~5 hours later, after losing ~20 dispatches across V1-Nigeria and V2-Pharma-UA campaigns).

After reading `server/src/services/board-auth.ts` I found the root cause:

```ts
export const BOARD_API_KEY_TTL_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;  // hardcoded 30 days
export const CLI_AUTH_CHALLENGE_TTL_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;

export function boardApiKeyExpiresAt(nowMs: number = Date.now()) {
  return new Date(nowMs + BOARD_API_KEY_TTL_MS);
}
```

Issues with the current design from an operator’s perspective:

1. **No env / config override.** There is no `PAPERCLIP_BOARD_API_KEY_TTL_DAYS` (or similar) to extend the TTL for service accounts. The constant is compiled into the docker image, so even modifying `BOARD_API_KEY_TTL_MS` requires forking and rebuilding `ghcr.io/cashtimepay/cashtimepay-ai-team`.
2. **No expiry warning anywhere.** Paperclip UI, the agent dashboard, the API itself — none of them surface `expires_at` for an existing token. The first signal an operator gets is a flood of `401`s in service logs, often days after the silent failure starts.
3. **No automated renewal path.** The only re-issuance mechanism is `POST /api/cli-auth/challenges` followed by a manual browser-approve step. A human has to remember to do this every 30 days for every service account in every environment.
4. **CLI auth challenge itself has a 10-min TTL** — if the operator misses the window, the whole loop has to be restarted.
5. **No service-account / machine-user model.** All board API keys are tied to a human user, with no concept of an unattended long-lived service identity (the kind GitHub calls a “fine-grained PAT” or AWS calls an “IAM access key”).

What we would like to see (in rough priority order):

- **Env-driven TTL.** A `PAPERCLIP_BOARD_API_KEY_TTL_DAYS` env on the server, defaulting to 30 but allowing `365` / `0` (never) for production deployments. Five-line change in `board-auth.ts`.
- **Service-account tokens** that explicitly bypass the user-TTL policy. UI button: “Create long-lived service token (no automatic expiry)” with an audit log showing who created it and when it was last used.
- **Expiry warning.** UI badge + agent log message starting 7 days before token expiry, with a link to the re-issue flow.
- **Self-rotation API.** `POST /api/board-api-keys/:id/rotate` that issues a new secret while keeping the same ID and skipping the CLI challenge for service accounts. Lets us rotate via cron without human approval.

For now we’re patching this on our side (probably forking + bumping `BOARD_API_KEY_TTL_MS` to `365 days`, or adding a nightly cron that does `UPDATE board_api_keys SET expires_at = now() + interval '30 days' WHERE name='agent-bus systemd (board)' AND revoked_at IS NULL` directly against the postgres). Both are workarounds, not solutions — we’d much rather use a supported upstream mechanism.

Happy to help: I can put together a PR for the env-driven TTL myself if you would accept that as the first step. Just let me know which direction you prefer (env override vs full service-account model)
payload.title: Board API key TTL improvement

payload.author: cyberize-repo
payload.body:
## Summary

`billingCode` is supported by the Paperclip API and the MCP server, but it is not exposed anywhere in the web UI. The New Issue form has no input for it, and the issue detail Properties panel does not display it. This forces users who need `billingCode` populated to create issues exclusively via the API or MCP, which is workable but not ideal.

## Current state (verified on v2026.416.0)

- **API:** `billingCode` field accepted on issue create and update.
- **MCP server (`@paperclipai/mcp-server`):** `paperclipCreateIssue` and `paperclipUpdateIssue` both accept `billingCode`.
- **Web UI New Issue form:** no input for `billingCode`. Checked the default form, both "..." expander menus, and inspected the rendered HTML — the string "billingcode" does not appear anywhere in the form's DOM.
- **Web UI issue detail Properties panel:** `billingCode` is not displayed, even on issues where it is populated.

Tested by creating an issue via the MCP with `billingCode: "example-client-slug"`, then opening it in the web UI. The field is set in the database (confirmed via API readback) but not visible to the user anywhere in the UI.

## Why this matters

For multi-client agencies and any organization that needs to attribute Paperclip work to a billing or cost-tracking dimension, `billingCode` is the natural place to record that. Without UI exposure:

1. Users who create issues manually through the web UI cannot set `billingCode`, so issues created that way are always missing it.
2. Users cannot see at a glance which client or billing dimension an issue belongs to when viewing it in the UI.
3. Any team workflow that depends on `billingCode` accuracy has to enforce it externally (custom validation skills, MCP wrappers, etc.) rather than relying on the UI as the source of truth.

In our case, every Paperclip issue must carry a `billingCode` matching a canonical client slug, and the rule is enforced by a custom validation skill we invoke before every `paperclipCreateIssue` call. That works for AI-driven issue creation, but it leaves UI-created issues uncovered — which is why we've had to make a working rule that "all issue creation must go through the MCP path until the field is exposed in the UI."

## Suggested minimum scope

Two changes that would close the gap:

1. **New Issue form:** add an optional `billingCode` text input. Either inline in the default form or behind one of the existing "..." expander menus.
2. **Issue detail Properties panel:** display `billingCode` as a read/editable field when it is set on an issue.

A nice-to-have but not required for v1: validation hooks (e.g., a regex pattern or a configurable allow-list of values per company) so teams that enforce a canonical set of `billingCode` values can do so at the form level instead of post-hoc.

## Workaround we use today

- All issue creation goes through the MCP, never the web UI.
- A pre-call validation skill checks `billingCode` against a canonical slug list and refuses to call `paperclipCreateIssue` if the value is missing or unknown.
- Agent instructions explicitly tell agents to inherit `billingCode` from the parent issue when creating sub-issues.

Happy to share more detail on the workflow if it would help shape the UI design.

## Environment

- Paperclip version verified: `v2026.416.0`
- Verification date: 2026-05-11
payload.title: Expose billingCode field in New Issue form UI and issue detail panel

payload.author: legacykeeperops
payload.body:
## Environment
- Paperclip version: 2026.517.0 (at time of bug), now 2026.525.0
- Adapter: gemini_local
- Models: gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite
- billing_type: metered_api

## Bug

Gemini cost tracking recorded correctly from May 18-22, then stopped recording cost_cents despite continued massive token usage from May 23-26.

Data from cost_events:
```
May 22: 162 Gemini events, cost = $29.22 (correct)
May 23: 134 events, 630M input tokens, cost = $0.00 (WRONG)
May 24: 175 events, 1.6B input tokens, cost = $0.00 (WRONG)
May 25: 206 events, 2.8B input tokens, cost = $0.00 (WRONG)
May 26: 174 events, 1.3B input tokens, cost = $0.00 (WRONG)
```

The billing_type is correctly set to `metered_api` on all events. Token counts are recorded. But cost_cents is 0.

## What Changed on May 22-23

On May 22-23, we switched agents between Claude and Gemini models multiple times:
1. Some agents were switched from Claude to Gemini 3.5 Flash
2. adapter_config.model was changed
3. runtime_config.modelProfiles.cheap was changed
4. agent_task_sessions were purged

The cost tracking worked for the first few hours of Gemini usage (May 22 shows $29.22) but then stopped.

## Hypothesis

The Gemini adapter's `costUsd` field in the result may have stopped being populated after the model switch, possibly due to:
- The adapter losing its pricing lookup after a reconfiguration
- A session resume issue where the new session doesn't carry pricing context
- The adapter reporting costUsd as null/undefined, which normalizeBilledCostCents() converts to 0

## Impact

$1,100+ in Gemini API charges were not recorded in Paperclip's cost tracking. The operator had no visibility into actual spend until manually backfilling from token counts and published pricing.

## Workaround

We backfilled cost_cents from token counts using published Gemini pricing. This captures the historical data but doesn't fix the underlying adapter issue.
payload.title: bug: Gemini metered_api cost_cents stops recording after model switch — 7B tokens with $0 cost

payload.author: legacykeeperops
payload.body:
## Problem

When using Claude Max (subscription plan), Paperclip correctly detects `billingType: "subscription_included"` and sets `cost_cents = 0` in cost_events. This is technically accurate — there's no per-token charge.

However, operators on subscription plans lose visibility into what their usage WOULD cost at API rates. This makes it impossible to:
- Evaluate whether the subscription is cost-effective vs API billing
- Set meaningful per-agent budgets (budgets in cents are all $0)
- Compare agent efficiency by cost
- Track cost trends over time
- Plan for scaling (adding agents, changing models)

## Current Behavior

`normalizeBilledCostCents()` in heartbeat.js:
```js
if (billingType === "subscription_included") return 0;
```

The `costUsd` from the adapter IS being calculated and stored in `usage_json`, but `cost_cents` in `cost_events` is forced to 0.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `shadow_cost_cents` column (or `market_rate_cents`) to `cost_events` that always calculates the market-rate cost regardless of billing type. The existing `cost_cents` continues to reflect actual charges (0 for subscription, real for metered). Operators can then see both:

- `cost_cents` = what you actually paid
- `shadow_cost_cents` = what it would cost at API rates

Alternatively, expose a per-company config to opt into shadow cost tracking that populates `cost_cents` with market rates even on subscription plans.

## Workaround

We're running a daily cron that backfills `cost_cents` with calculated market rates based on token counts and published pricing. This works but:
- Pricing must be manually updated when models change
- It overwrites the "actual cost" semantics of cost_cents
- It doesn't survive Paperclip updates or schema changes

## Impact

Any operator on Claude Max, Gemini subscription, or similar flat-rate plans has zero cost visibility in the Paperclip dashboard. This affects budgeting, efficiency analysis, and model selection decisions.
payload.title: feat: shadow/market-rate cost tracking for subscription-included plans (Claude Max)

payload.author: legacykeeperops
payload.body:
## Environment
- Paperclip version: updated from 2026.517.0 to 2026.525.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (DigitalOcean)
- Node: v20.x
- Install method: npm install -g paperclipai
- Service: systemd unit running npx paperclipai run

## Bug

After updating Paperclip from 2026.517.0 to 2026.525.0 via npm install -g paperclipai@2026.525.0, the server fails to start with:

```
Paperclip server failed to start.
The requested module '@paperclipai/shared' does not provide an export named 'anchorSnapshotToSelector'
```

All 9 pre-flight checks pass. The crash happens during server initialization.

## Root Cause

The npx cache at ~/.npm/_npx/ retained the old @paperclipai/server@2026.517.0 which imports anchorSnapshotToSelector from @paperclipai/shared. The globally installed @paperclipai/shared@2026.525.0 no longer exports that symbol.

The file importing the removed export: @paperclipai/server/dist/services/document-annotations.js

## Workaround

```bash
rm -rf ~/.npm/_npx/
npm cache clean --force
sudo systemctl restart paperclip
```

## Impact

Server was in a crash loop until the stale cache was cleared. All agents were down.
payload.title: bug: stale npx cache causes crash after update — anchorSnapshotToSelector export removed from @paperclipai/shared

payload.author: Denis-arp
payload.body:
## Summary

`POST /api/issues/{id}/interactions`, `POST /api/issues/{id}/comments`, and `PUT /api/issues/{id}/documents/{key}` reproducibly return HTTP 500 ("Internal server error") when the body contains certain markdown shapes above a per-issue threshold. The 500 leaks through to API clients with no actionable error context (server-side stack trace not surfaced). The threshold depends on the target issue's accumulated state, so the same payload that succeeds on one issue 500s on another.

## Affected endpoints

- `POST /api/issues/{issueId}/interactions` (kinds `request_confirmation`, `ask_user_questions`, `suggest_tasks`) — `body` and `detailsMarkdown` fields
- `POST /api/issues/{issueId}/comments` — `body` field
- `PUT /api/issues/{issueId}/documents/{key}` — `body`/`content` field

## Repro shapes that 500

Any of the following body shapes are sufficient to trigger the 500 once the issue is past the (currently-unknown) per-issue threshold:

- H1/H2/H3 header followed by a blank line and a paragraph
- Two paragraphs separated by a blank line
- Header followed by a bullet list
- Long single-paragraph bodies above ~2KB on some issues

## Repro shapes that survive

- Single short paragraphs (≤~1KB)
- A bare H2 alone
- A single small table
- A single inline code span

## Minimal repro

1. Pick a moderately-populated issue (≥ ~10 comments / interactions worth of accumulated state).
2. POST an interaction with a body like:

   ```markdown
   ## Heading

   First paragraph.

   - Bullet one
   - Bullet two
   ```

3. Observe HTTP 500 with no actionable message; the API client receives a generic "Internal server error".

The same body shape posted on a brand-new issue will succeed, which is why this is a per-issue-state bug, not a payload-validation bug.

## Why we believe it is the markdown renderer

Bisected on 2026-05-27 via 16 probe interactions on issue ADF-645 in our ADF company; pattern was consistently content-shape × per-issue-state. The crash never reached our application logic — the 500 is returned from the endpoint synchronously, suggesting the renderer (or whatever post-processing pipeline runs on the body) is the throwing component.

Two adjacent issues observed in the same session:
- ADF-645 — 500s on almost any multi-paragraph body.
- ADF-652 — accepted a 1.5 KB multi-paragraph + bullets comment without issue.

## Impact

- Agents using interactions for board approvals (e.g., the `request_confirmation` kind with structured `detailsMarkdown`) cannot post legible, structured proposals to "older" issues. They are forced into single-line workarounds that degrade auditability and readability of the human-facing UI.
- The 500 response gives no signal to the agent about *which part* of the body failed, so agents end up bisecting via repeated probe interactions on the parent issue — and those probes get stuck `pending` because agents cannot cancel or reject interactions (board-only). That permanently poisons the parent issue's interaction queue.
- This blocks our CEO agent from filing high-quality structured board confirmations on heavily-used parent issues.

## Asks

1. Identify the per-issue threshold or body-size limit that crosses the renderer over into a 500.
2. Either raise the limit, or return a 4xx with a meaningful error message ("body too large", "renderer cannot process shape X near offset Y", etc.) instead of a 500. A 4xx with a clear reason is the minimum acceptable fix — agents can react to it; they cannot react to an opaque 500.
3. Surface the renderer stack trace in the API response when running with debug enabled, so users can self-diagnose.

## Workarounds we are using today

- Probe with a tiny single-line body first to check the renderer is alive on the target issue.
- For long plans, use a sequence of short single-line comments instead of one structured body.
- For `request_confirmation`, file with a single-paragraph `detailsMarkdown` that links to a document or comment carrying the full content (on a
payload.title: [BUG] POST /api/issues/{id}/interactions returns 500 on multi-paragraph or bulleted markdown body (content-shape × per-issue-state)

Tools registered by a plugin via `ctx.tools.register` and properly returned
by `GET /api/plugins/tools` are not callable from agents running on the
`claude_local` adapter. The plugin tool registry knows about them; the
spawned Claude Code instance does not. The Paperclip spec says "by default,
plugin tools are available to all agents" that holds for the dispatcher
side, but the `claude_local` adapter has no bridge from the plugin tool
registry into the Claude Code child process's MCP/tool universe, so the
agent's `ToolSearch` returns zero hits and the tools are effectively
invisible.

I'm building my first Paperclip plugin (a small Google Maps connector 
that exposes geocode, search_places, and get_place_details as agent tools)
 and I'm at the testing stage. The plugin installs cleanly, the config and Test 
Connection both pass, and paperclipai plugin inspect shows it as ready with 
all three tools properly registered. The trouble starts when I actually try to use 
it through a Paperclip agent: I opened an issue assigned to one of my claude_local 
agents asking it to use the tools, and the agent came back saying the tools aren't 
accessible to it. So the registration side looks healthy end-to-end, but something 
isn't bridging the tools across to the LLM the agent is driving. Filing this in case it's 
a known gap or I'm missing a wiring step.

payload.author: CosmicDreamer17
payload.body:
## Summary

The `paperclipai` CLI (as of `paperclipai@2026.525.0`) exposes `secrets list / create / link / doctor / providers / migrate-inline-env` but does NOT expose `secrets rotate <id>` or `secrets delete <id>`. The corresponding API routes (`POST /api/secrets/{id}/rotate`, `DELETE /api/secrets/{id}`) exist server-side and are board-auth-gated, but the CLI has no commands wrapping them.

Result: operators who want to rotate a secret's value in place (keeping the same `secretId`, just updating the stored value) have to:

- (a) Drop to `curl` with a board session cookie extracted from browser dev tools (not documented; fragile)
- (b) Create a new secret with a new UUID, then PATCH every agent's `adapter_config.env.<KEY>.secretId` to the new UUID

Option (b) is the only viable path with current CLI primitives. It produces version-suffixed secret names (`MY_TOKEN_v2`, `MY_TOKEN_v3`, etc.) and orphans the old secret slot, which is unclean. The architecturally correct pattern (per the upstream SPEC) is rotate-in-place: same UUID, new value, no agent re-binding.

## Requested CLI additions

```
paperclipai secrets rotate <secretId> [--value <new-value>] [--file <path>] [--stdin]
paperclipai secrets delete <secretId>
```

`rotate` would call `POST /api/secrets/{id}/rotate`. `delete` would call `DELETE /api/secrets/{id}` (assuming a delete route exists; if not, that's a separate gap).

## Why this matters

For deployments practicing routine credential rotation (e.g., 90-day cadence per the upstream SECRETS-AWS-PROVIDER doc and similar deployment guides), rotate-in-place is the canonical pattern. Without CLI support, every rotation creates technical debt (versioned secret names) OR requires operators to learn an undocumented curl-with-board-cookie pattern.

## Source

This was surfaced on 2026-05-27 during a credential-rotation incident in a self-hosted Paperclip deployment. The first rotation had to use the new-UUID fallback because the CLI didn't expose rotate; the deployment now carries a `_v3`-suffixed secret name as documented one-time tech debt, with cleanup deferred until CLI rotate support lands. Documented in the deployment's own SECRETS.md under "One-time rotation deviation (2026-05-27)."

If the team prefers contributions, we'd be happy to draft the CLI commands. Pointers to the relevant CLI source files (`cli/src/commands/client/secrets.ts` etc.) would help.

payload.body:
## Summary

`GET /api/agents/:id/configuration` returns env vars of `type: plain` with their raw values in the response body. The `/llms/agent-configuration.txt` doc says "Sensitive values are redacted in configuration read APIs" — they currently are not.

For agents that include credential-shaped values in their `adapter_config.env` (e.g., via the legacy plain-string env binding, or via operator-driven UI flows that store as plain), this surface returns the raw credential value over the API. Any agent that can call its own `GET /api/agents/me/configuration` can read its own credentials in plaintext. This contradicts the architectural intent in `doc/SPEC-implementation.md` §7.13 which says "Secret values are not stored inline in `agents.adapter_config.env`" and "Activity and approval payloads must not persist raw sensitive values."

## Reproduction

1. As a board user, create a company secret via `POST /api/companies/{companyId}/secrets` (e.g., name `MY_TEST_SECRET`, value `dummy-test-value-not-a-real-credential`).
2. Create an agent via `POST /api/companies/{companyId}/agents` with `adapter_config.env.MY_TOKEN = "dummy-test-value-not-a-real-credential"` (legacy plain-string form, which Zod's `envBindingSchema` still accepts for backward compat).
3. As the agent itself (or any actor with access to that agent's record), call `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/configuration`.
4. Observe: response body contains `"env": { "MY_TOKEN": { "type": "plain", "value": "dummy-test-value-not-a-real-credential" } }` — the value is returned verbatim.

## Expected behavior

Per the docs (`/llms/agent-configuration.txt`), sensitive values in `type: plain` env entries should be redacted in the configuration read API response. Either:

- Return a redacted placeholder: `{ "type": "plain", "value": "<REDACTED>" }`
- Or return the metadata only with a flag: `{ "type": "plain", "value_redacted": true }`

The same behavior should apply to `/api/agents/:id` (the parent read endpoint) for any caller below board level, since both endpoints surface env values in the same shape.

## Workaround (current)

Use `type: secret_ref` bindings instead of `type: plain`. `secret_ref` returns `{ type: "secret_ref", secretId: <uuid>, version: "latest" }` from the read API — no value leak. This is the architecturally-correct pattern per `doc/SPEC-implementation.md` §7.13 anyway. Document the redaction gap explicitly in agent-configuration docs so deployments don't rely on the legacy plain-string binding for sensitive material.

## Source

This was surfaced by a self-hosted Paperclip deployment on 2026-05-27 during a credential-rotation incident. Two PATs were stored as `type: plain` and read back in plaintext via `/api/agents/:id/configuration` by the agents themselves. Treated as a credential exposure event; PATs rotated. Storage-side bug fixed in the deployment by switching to `secret_ref` bindings. The read-API redaction gap remains.

Happy to provide additional reproduction detail or contribute a fix if useful. Not blocking us on our side (we've migrated off plain bindings), but the redaction gap is a real platform contract violation that could bite other deployments.
payload.title: Adapter env GET /api/agents/:id/configuration returns type:plain values unredacted, despite docs claim of redaction

payload.body:
## Summary

When Gemini CLI cannot resume a previous session, it exits with the message:

```
Error resuming session: No previous sessions found for this project.
```

The regex in `isGeminiUnknownSessionError` (in `packages/adapters/gemini-local/src/server/parse.ts`) does **not** match this string, so the auto-retry with a fresh session never fires. The run is marked `failed` instead of transparently recovering.

## Affected versions
- Gemini CLI: v0.43.0 (likely all versions that emit this error message)
- Paperclip: latest (confirmed with current dist)
- OS: Windows 11 (but the regex bug is platform-independent)

## Root cause

```ts
// parse.ts — current regex
return /unknown\s+session|session\s+.*\s+not\s+found|resume\s+.*\s+not\s+found|checkpoint\s+.*\s+not\s+found|cannot\s+resume|failed\s+to\s+resume/i.test(haystack);
```

The error message "Error resuming session: No previous sessions found for this project." fails every branch:

| Pattern | Why it doesn't match |
|---|---|
| `session.*not found` | Message says "sessions **found**", not "sessions not found" |
| `resume.*not found` | "resuming" ≠ "resume" + whitespace; and "found" ≠ "not found" |
| `unknown session` | Word "unknown" is absent |
| `cannot resume` | Absent |
| `failed to resume` | Absent |

## Impact

The retry logic in `execute.ts` is correct and already handles this case:

```ts
if (sessionId && !initial.proc.timedOut && (initial.proc.exitCode ?? 0) !== 0 &&
    isGeminiUnknownSessionError(initial.proc.stdout, initial.proc.stderr)) {
  await onLog("stdout", `[paperclip] Gemini resume session "" is unavailable; retrying with a fresh session.\n`);
  const retry = await runAttempt(null);
  return toResult(retry, true, true);
}
```

But the guard returns `false`, so the retry never executes. The run fails permanently until the user manually triggers a fresh-session wakeup.

This is especially common on Windows where previous runs may have failed before Gemini created a session file — leaving a stale session ID in Paperclip's runtime with no corresponding `~/.gemini/tmp/` entry.

## Fix

Add the missing pattern to the regex (one-line change in `parse.ts`):

```diff
- return /unknown\s+session|session\s+.*\s+not\s+found|resume\s+.*\s+not\s+found|checkpoint\s+.*\s+not\s+found|cannot\s+resume|failed\s+to\s+resume/i.test(haystack);
+ return /unknown\s+session|session\s+.*\s+not\s+found|resume\s+.*\s+not\s+found|checkpoint\s+.*\s+not\s+found|cannot\s+resume|failed\s+to\s+resume|no\s+previous\s+sessions\s+found/i.test(haystack);
```

## Related

- PR #2877 (stdin-based prompt delivery, fixes the main Windows quoting issues — but does not address this regex gap)
- Issue #6324 (similar pattern gap in `isClaudeUnknownSessionError` for the claude_local adapter)
- Issue #1160 (stale session ID loop in hermes-local adapter — same class of bug)
payload.title: [gemini_local] isGeminiUnknownSessionError doesn't match "No previous sessions found" — stale session causes failed run instead of auto-retry

payload.author: Prolearnai
payload.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the `claude_local` adapter mis-quotes paths containing spaces when invoking Claude Code, causing every run to fail. The bug affects users whose Windows username (and therefore home directory) contains a space, e.g. `C:\Users\First Last\`.

The bug surfaced in two places, suggesting the same quoting logic is applied to multiple adapter arguments.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- Username with a space: `User One`
- Paperclip: installed via `npx paperclipai run` (latest as of 2026-05-27)
- Claude Code: installed globally via npm to `C:\Users\User One\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.cmd`
- `where.exe claude` confirms the binary is on PATH and resolvable

## Symptom 1 — Executable path quoting

Initial runs failed immediately with:

'"C:\Users\USER\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.CMD"' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.

Note the literal double-quotes wrapping the path. cmd.exe is treating the quotes as part of the filename. The space in the username appears to be what triggers the over-quoting.

**Workaround:** In the agent's `claude_local` adapter config, set Command to the 8.3 short path explicitly:
C:\Users\USER~1\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.cmd

After this, the adapter Test passed (Working directory valid, Command executable, Claude hello probe succeeded).

## Symptom 2 — Append-system-prompt path quoting

After fixing Symptom 1, runs failed at a later stage:

Error: Append system prompt file not found: C:\Users\User.paperclip\instances\default\workspaces<uuid>"C:\Users\User

Two paths are concatenated, the second starts with a literal `"` and is truncated at the space — same root cause (mis-quoting of a path containing a space) on a different argument that Paperclip generates internally for run workspaces.

**Workaround:** Relocate the entire data directory to a space-free path using `paperclipai run --data-dir C:\paperclip-data`. (Note: the config file's `embeddedPostgresDataDir`, `backup.dir`, `logging.logDir`, `storage.localDisk.baseDir`, and `secrets.localEncrypted.keyFilePath` had absolute paths baked in from onboarding, so a naive `Move-Item` of `.paperclip` did not work — the config file had to be edited to replace the old paths before restart.)

After relocation, the originally-failing issue completed successfully end-to-end in ~2 minutes.

## Suggested fix

Wherever the adapter constructs the Claude Code command line on Windows (both for the executable and for the `--append-system-prompt` argument), arguments should be quoted exactly once. Currently it looks like paths are being pre-wrapped in quotes and then the spawn call wraps them again, producing the `'"..."'` you see in cmd.exe error output.

A second smaller suggestion: `paperclipai run --data-dir <path>` could optionally rewrite the absolute paths in `config.json` to be relative to the new data dir, so that moving the data directory works without manual editing.

## Severity

Blocking for any Windows user whose home directory contains a space. Currently the workaround requires both an 8.3 short path AND a separate data directory — neither is discoverable without significant debugging.
payload.title: claude_local adapter fails on Windows when user profile path contains a space

payload.body:
## TL;DR

Declining a `request_confirmation` wakes the assignee agent but hands it nothing to act on: no comment is created (the reject enqueues a wake tagged `issue_commented` with `sourceCommentId: null`), and the wake renderer has no `rejected` branch so it never reads the decline reason from `result.reason`. The agent resumes, sees `pending comments: 0/0`, reports "no input," and re-parks the issue in `in_review`. The human's feedback is silently dropped. Same bug class as #3780 / #3781 (approvals), but in the interactions / `request_confirmation` path.

## Summary

Declining a `request_confirmation` interaction (with `rejectRequiresReason: true`) wakes the assignee agent, but the wake carries nothing actionable, so the agent resumes, sees `pending comments: 0/0`, concludes there is no input to act on, and re-parks the issue in `in_review`. The human's decline reason is silently dropped.

Two compounding defects:

1. **The reject enqueues a comment-shaped wake that points at no comment.** The `agent_wakeup_requests` row created on reject has `reason: "issue_commented"` but a payload with `sourceCommentId: null`:
   ```json
   {
     "mutation": "interaction",
     "interactionKind": "request_confirmation",
     "interactionStatus": "rejected",
     "sourceCommentId": null
   }
   ```
   No `issue_comments` row is ever written from the decline. The reason text lives only in `issue_thread_interactions.result.reason` (`{"outcome":"rejected","reason":"<human text>"}`), which nothing on the wake path reads.

2. **The resume-delta renderer has no `rejected` branch.** In `packages/adapter-utils/src/server-utils.ts`, the planning-mode wake only special-cases acceptance:
   ```ts
   const acceptedPlanContinuation =
     !hasWakeComments &&
     normalized.interactionKind === "request_confirmation" &&
     normalized.interactionStatus === "accepted";
   ```
   A `rejected` status produces no directive, and the renderer never reads `result.reason`. The `pending comments` line is computed purely from `issue_comments` (`includedCount/requestedCount`), so it correctly shows `0/0`. The boilerplate even states (server-utils.ts, near L125): *"for request_confirmation this resumes only after acceptance."*

Net: a decline-with-feedback is a silent drop. The agent is woken but blind.

## Reproducer

1. Agent creates a `request_confirmation` on a planning issue with `allowDeclineReason: true`, `rejectRequiresReason: true`, `continuationPolicy: wake_assignee`, targeting a plan document revision.
2. Issue sits in `in_review`.
3. A board user clicks **Request changes** and submits a reason.
4. Observe: interaction -> `status: rejected`, `result.reason` populated; a wakeup fires (`reason: issue_commented`, `sourceCommentId: null`); the assignee runs and posts something equivalent to *"No response requested. Issue remains in in_review with pending confirmation... 0 pending comments."*

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** a decline routes the reason back to the assignee — either mirrored into `issue_comments` (so the comment-delta surfaces it) and/or surfaced in the wake prompt via a `rejected` / `request_changes` directive that includes `result.reason`.
- **Actual:** the wake fires but carries no comment and no reason; the agent sees `0/0` and treats it as "no input."

## Source

- `packages/adapter-utils/src/server-utils.ts` — `renderPaperclipWakePrompt`: `acceptedPlanContinuation` is the only interaction branch; no `rejected` handling; `result.reason` is never read; `pending comments` derives only from `issue_comments`.
- Reject path: enqueues `agent_wakeup_requests` with `reason: "issue_commented"` + `sourceCommentId: null` instead of materializing a comment.

## Related

- #3780 / #3781 — same bug class in the **approvals** subsystem ("reject / request-revision do not wake the requesting agent"). The fix there should be mirrored for `request_confirmation` interactions.
- #4176 — adjacent `pendingComments` accuracy issue, but a different caus
payload.title: request_confirmation reject fires a comment-shaped wake with no comment — assignee resumes to `pending comments: 0/0` and reports no input; decline reason dropped

payload.body:
## Summary

A companion issue to #6796, which covers `agents.status=error` with no diagnostic context. This issue covers the same root pattern at the **issue level**: `issues.executionRunId` can be left pointing at a now-dead run while `checkoutRunId` is `null`, leaving the issue in a state where every mutation route rejects with `Issue run ownership conflict` and **no self-serve recovery path exists**.

---

## Repro

Observed in the wild on 2026-05-27 when a CEO agent attempted to close a done investigation issue. The run (`63e33617-82b0-4f15-a6b4-0352fb884ab0`) had already finished or died.

**Issue state at time of observation:**
- `executionRunId`: `63e33617-82b0-4f15-a6b4-0352fb884ab0` (stale — run finished/died)
- `checkoutRunId`: `null`

**All four mutation routes rejected:**
- `PATCH /api/issues/{id}` → `Issue run ownership conflict`
- `POST /api/issues/{id}/checkout` → `Issue run ownership conflict`
- `POST /api/issues/{id}/release` → `Issue run ownership conflict`
- `POST /api/issues/{id}/comments` → `Issue run ownership conflict`

The issue was eventually unlocked when the orphan-reaping sweep ran, but the window of unrecoverability was real and there was no admin/self-repair route available.

---

## Root Cause (hypothesis)

When a heartbeat run ends (via SIGTERM, process kill, or unhandled exception), the run cleanup path marks `heartbeatRuns.status = "failed"` but may not clear `issues.executionRunId`. This leaves the issue pointing at a dead run with `checkoutRunId = null` — a state that the `release` and `checkout` routes reject because neither condition for claiming ownership is met.

The same orphan-reaping job that handles `heartbeatRuns` likely sweeps and clears this, but there's a window between the run dying and the next reaping cycle.

---

## Same Root Shape as #6796

| Scope | Stale field | Missing cleanup | Unrecoverable window |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agents` table | `status=error` | No `lastRunError` written (issue #6796) | Until next successful heartbeat |
| `issues` table | `executionRunId` = dead run | Not cleared on run finalization | Until orphan-reaping runs |

Both are caused by run finalization not atomically updating all dependent state.

---

## Proposed Fix

1. In the run finalization path (both `runFinalize` and `reapOrphanedRuns`), after marking a run as `failed`, also clear `issues.executionRunId` for any issue that was associated with the run via its checkout — if the corresponding `checkoutRunId` also matches (or is null).
2. Add a guardrail to the `release` endpoint: accept a `release` call when `executionRunId` matches the dead run's ID even if the actor's current run ID doesn't match — provided `checkoutRunId` is null (i.e., the issue was never actively checked out by a live session).
3. Consider covering both cases (#6796 and this one) in a single "run finalization atomicity" fix, since the root cause is the same: run exit does not atomically clean up all downstream state.

---

## Out of Scope

- Admin API to force-clear stale `executionRunId` (useful operational tool, but a separate concern)
- The agent-level `status=error` / `lastRunError=null` case is tracked separately in #6796
payload.title: issue-level executionRunId lock with null checkoutRunId — no recovery path when run dies without releasing

## Summary

When an agent transitions to `status=error`, the `agents` table row receives no error context — `lastRunError` does not exist as a field, and no equivalent diagnostic is written to the agent record. The `heartbeatRuns` row for the failed run *does* contain the error (`error`, `errorCode`, `exitCode`, `signal`), but `finalizeAgentStatus` does not denormalize any of that context back to the agent row.

This has produced three separate incidents over 4 weeks where operators see an agent at `status=error` with no message, no run ID, and no clue whether to wait, reset, or investigate further.

---

## Repro Pattern (observed three times)

Trigger: any of the following causes `finalizeAgentStatus(agentId, "failed")` to be called:

- SIGTERM / exit-143 during final heartbeat (process killed mid-run, `reapOrphanedRuns` marks the run `failed` with `errorCode: "process_lost"`)
- Transient upstream API 500 during a terminal-run-recovery retry (`adapter_failed: Claude run failed: subtype=success: API Error: 500 Internal server error`)
- Unhandled adapter exception or setup failure

**Resulting agent state in all three cases:**
```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "lastHeartbeatAt": "<timestamp>",
  "lastRunError": null   // field does not exist; no error info on the agent row at all
}
```

Operators cannot distinguish a SIGTERM race from an API 500 from a bad config change — all look identical.

---

## Root Cause

### What happens when a run fails

1. Run finalizer (`runFinalize` / `reapOrphanedRuns`) calls `setRunStatus(runId, "failed", { error, errorCode, exitCode, signal, ... })` — this writes error details to `heartbeatRuns`.
2. Immediately after, `finalizeAgentStatus(agentId, "failed")` is called.
3. `finalizeAgentStatus` computes `nextStatus = "error"` and writes `{ status: "error", lastHeartbeatAt, updatedAt }` to the `agents` table. **No error context is included.**

### Code location

**`server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`, lines 6184–6235** (`finalizeAgentStatus`):

```typescript
const updated = await db
  .update(agents)
  .set({
    status: nextStatus,
    lastHeartbeatAt: new Date(),
    updatedAt: new Date(),
    // ← error context never written here
  })
  .where(eq(agents.id, agentId))
```

Call sites that produce `outcome="failed"`:
- **line 6570** — `reapOrphanedRuns` (SIGTERM / process_lost)
- **line 7966** — normal run finalization post-adapter (API 500, adapter crash)
- **lines 8044, 8087** — setup-phase failure / outer-catch safety net

### Why the `heartbeatRuns` data doesn't help at triage time

The run record exists and has the error, but:
- The dashboard/agent-detail API returns agent-level fields, not the latest run's fields.
- Operators must know to look up runs separately, and must know which run ID to check.
- Health-check automations that read `agent.status` have no way to surface a meaningful error message without a separate query.

---

## Proposed Fix

### 1 — Add `lastRunError` JSONB column to agents schema

**`packages/db/src/schema/agents.ts`**

```typescript
lastRunError: jsonb("last_run_error").$type<{
  runId: string;
  errorCode: string | null;
  message: string | null;
  exitCode: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
  occurredAt: string; // ISO 8601
} | null>(),
```

Migration: a simple `ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN last_run_error jsonb;` (nullable, no default needed).

### 2 — Populate in `finalizeAgentStatus` when transitioning to error

Query the latest failed run in the same function call and write it alongside the status update:

```typescript
async function finalizeAgentStatus(
  agentId: string,
  outcome: "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "timed_out",
) {
  // ... existing runningCount / nextStatus logic ...

  let lastRunError: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined = undefined;
  if (nextStatus === "error") {
    const latestFailed = await db
      .select({
        id: heartbeatRuns.id,
        error: heartbeatRuns.error,
        errorCode: heartbeatRuns.errorCode,
payload.title: agent status=error never populates lastRunError — finalizeAgentStatus drops error context from heartbeatRuns

## Summary On the `/invite/` "pending approval" screen — the panel shown to a user who has just submitted a join request and is waiting on admin approval — the text "**Company Settings → Access**" is rendered as two clickable `` links. The surrounding wording clearly addresses the company admin ("Approval page", "**Ask them** to visit … to approve your request"), but the requester reading the page naturally clicks the only underlined link on the screen. They are routed to `/company/settings/access` — which they have no permission to view — and the app renders the "**No company access**" panel instead. To a first-time invitee the invite flow looks broken: they submitted a request, were told to wait, clicked the only link on the page, and landed at what looks like an error screen. ## Reproduction 1. As an instance admin, generate a `company_join` invite that requires admin approval (`humanRole: owner` / `requires_company_admin_approval: true`). 2. In a fresh browser profile, open the invite link. 3. Fill the **Create your account** form and submit. 4. The **"Request to join \"** panel renders (correct). 5. Click "**Company Settings → Access**" — either the link inside the "Approval page" box, or the inline one in "Ask them to visit …". 6. → Browser navigates to `/company/settings/access` and renders "**No company access — This account is signed in, but it does not have an active company membership or instance-admin access on this Paperclip instance.**" ## Expected Both "Company Settings → Access" references should be **non-interactive instructional text** describing where the admin needs to go — not navigation the requester can follow. The requester has nothing actionable to do on that route. ## Actual `ui/src/pages/InviteLanding.tsx` (`AwaitingJoinApprovalPanel`, lines 178, 199–204, 207): ```tsx const approvalUrl = `${window.location.origin}/company/settings/access`; // ... Company Settings → Access // ... Ask them to visit Company Settings → Access to approve your request. ``` Both anchor elements navigate the requester to a route they cannot access. ## Requested fix Render both occurrences as plain styled text (`

` / `` with the same `text-zinc-200` styling, no underline, no `href`). The surrounding copy ("**Ask them** to visit …") already makes clear this is guidance the requester relays to the admin, not a navigation target. The now-unused `approvalUrl` constant can be removed. Happy to send a PR if this direction looks right. ## Environment - Paperclip: master @ `242a2c2f` (2026-05-17) - Deployment mode: `authenticated`, `bind=lan`, embedded Postgres - Browser: Chrome stable (also reproduces in Playwright Chromium) ## Related Surfaced while debugging #5731 (blank page on `/invite/` for non-member authenticated users). Once the React tree no longer crashes during the invite flow, the user lands on this pending-approval panel and the misleading link becomes the next visible failure in the same scenario. ## Severity Low (cosmetic / UX) but high-confusion for first-time invitees, because the broken link is the **only** call-to-action on the page.

payload.body:
## Summary

Add support for custom uploaded image avatars for agents, so each agent in a Paperclip company can have a distinct visual identity instead of only using the current icon-based representation.

## Background

Paperclip models agents as employees within a company structure, including org charts, roles, reporting lines, budgets, governance, and task ownership. As users build out multi-agent companies, especially across multiple companies, visual identity becomes increasingly useful for quickly recognizing who is who.

The current agent UI appears to support selecting an icon for an agent. That is helpful, but it does not allow users to upload custom portraits, branded character images, or agent-specific avatar artwork.

There is a related open request for company logo upload and avatar rendering support in #152. This request is similar in spirit, but scoped to individual agents rather than companies.

## User Story

As a board operator, I want to upload a custom avatar image for each agent, so my Paperclip companies feel more personal, easier to scan, and easier to manage visually.

I have created distinct images for all of my agents, and I would love to see those images represented throughout my Paperclip companies.

## Proposed Change

Add optional custom avatar support to agents.

### Scope

- Agent create/edit form: allow optional avatar image upload.
- Agent detail page: display avatar when available.
- Agent list: display avatar when available.
- Org chart: display avatar when available.
- Task/issue views: display avatar beside assigned agents or agent comments where appropriate.
- Agent icon picker: keep the existing icon picker as the fallback/default path.
- Backend storage/update handling: persist and return an agent avatar path or URL on the agent model.

## Suggested Behavior

1. If an agent has a custom avatar image, show it.
2. If no custom avatar exists, fall back to the current selected icon.
3. If no selected icon exists, fall back to the existing default icon/avatar behavior.
4. Users should be able to upload, replace, and remove an agent avatar.
5. Existing agents should continue working without migration issues or broken UI.

## Supported File Types

Suggested initial support:

- image/png
- image/jpeg
- image/jpg
- image/webp
- image/gif

SVG support could be considered separately because of security and rendering concerns.

## Functional Requirements

- Agent create flow supports optional avatar upload.
- Agent settings/edit screen supports upload, replace, and remove.
- Avatar image appears consistently in common agent surfaces:
  - agent list
  - agent detail page
  - org chart
  - task/issue assignment UI
  - comments/activity where agent identity is shown
- Existing icon-based display remains available.
- Upload errors are surfaced clearly and do not corrupt other agent settings.
- Permissions and company scoping are enforced.

## Data/API Requirements

A possible implementation could add a nullable field such as:

Summary
Add a Data Room to Paperclip: a first-class, company-scoped document repository where humans can upload context files and agents can store their deliverables in an organized, searchable way.

Problem
Today, there is no native place in Paperclip for:

Human-to-agent knowledge transfer — if I want an agent to have access to contracts, SOPs, templates, or reference docs, I have to inject that context manually in every prompt/skill/issue. There's no persistent, structured store the agent can pull from.
Agent deliverable persistence — when an agent finishes a task, its output lives in the issue comment thread and nowhere else. There's no canonical place where generated docs accumulate, get versioned, or become reusable by other agents.


Proposed Solution
Introduce a Data Room section at the company level with two flows:
1. Human uploads (inbound context)

UI to upload files (PDF, DOCX, MD, CSV, JSON, etc.) organized into named folders or tags.
Files become available to agents at runtime via a data_room_search / data_room_get capability injected into the host services.
Optionally, files can be scoped to specific agents or goals.

2. Agent uploads (outbound deliverables)

When an agent completes a task, it can call a data_room_save tool to store its output document in the Data Room with metadata: agent_id, issue_id, goal_id, timestamp, tags.
The UI surfaces these files organized by agent, goal, or date — making it easy to find "everything Agent X produced for Goal Y".

3. Cross-agent reuse

An agent working on a downstream task can query the Data Room for deliverables produced by upstream agents, enabling true multi-agent handoffs without manual copy-paste.


User Stories

As a company operator, I want to upload my SOP library so all agents have access to the same ground truth without me re-injecting it into every issue.
As a company operator, I want to see all documents produced by my agents organized by project, so I can review and ship them.
As an agent, I want to persist my final deliverable to a shared store so other agents can consume it in future tasks.


Notes on Scope
This fits naturally within Paperclip's existing primitives:

Company-scoped (same isolation model as everything else).
Plugin-compatible — a data_room plugin exposing host services + UI contribution would work well.
File storage could use the existing local file storage in dev and swap to S3/R2 in production, matching the current pattern.

Happy to contribute a spec or prototype if the direction is validated.
payload.title: [Feature Request] Data Room — shared document layer for agents to read and write deliverables

## Production City escalation — Paperclip recovery evaluator platform gaps

**From:** Jordan Ashworth, CTO, Production City
**Date:** 2026-05-26
**Internal tracking:** [PRO-6017](https://app.production.city/PRO/issues/PRO-6017) (escalation), [PRO-6016](https://app.production.city/PRO/issues/PRO-6016) (investigation), [PRO-5104](https://app.production.city/PRO/issues/PRO-5104) (impacted issue)
**Outline doc (full technical brief, proposed fixes):** https://app.outline.production.city/doc/aperim-escalation-recovery-evaluator-platform-gaps-pro-6017-zzdyFM8KG6

---

### Background

Production City's recovery evaluator instance is showing three structural gaps that are actively impacting agent operations — specifically, PRO-5104 holds a stuck `activeRecoveryAction` that we cannot clear and that the evaluator will not re-resolve on its own because the inputs it sees are stale.

We have completed the investigation (PRO-6016) and the escalation brief (PRO-6017). The brief and proposed fixes are detailed in the Outline doc above; the summary below covers what we are asking Aperim to confirm or correct.

---

### Three gaps

#### Gap 1 — Stale evidence snapshot (High)

**Observed:** The evaluator creates the evidence object at recovery-action creation time and never refreshes it. Issues that have since transitioned to `blocked` with a named external owner and active interactions still show stale `in_progress` evidence the next time the evaluator runs, so retain/expire decisions are made on out-of-date state.

**Proposed fix:** Refresh live issue state (status, assignee, `blockedByIssueIds`, last activity) before each retain/expire decision rather than relying on the snapshot taken at action creation.

#### Gap 2 — No admin clear endpoint (High — most urgent)

**Observed:** `PATCH /api/issues/{id}` accepts `clearRecoveryAction` and `resolveRecoveryAction` fields without error, but the fields are silently ignored — subsequent `GET` confirms the recovery action remains active. There is no documented admin endpoint to force-clear a stuck recovery action. This is the immediate blocker for PRO-5104 and the reason this escalation is High urgency.

**Proposed fix:** `POST /api/issues/{id}/recovery-actions/{recoveryActionId}/resolve` with `{ "reason": "...", "actorAgentId": "..." }` body, audit-logged. Either that, or document a supported workaround.

#### Gap 3 — No re-evaluation on issue update (Medium)

**Observed:** The evaluator runs on its cadence only. Status, assignment, blocker, or interaction changes on issues with active recovery actions do not enqueue an evaluation event, so the evaluator's view of the world only updates at the next cadence tick. Combined with Gap 1, this means corrective changes by humans or agents take an unpredictable amount of time to influence retain/expire outcomes.

**Proposed fix:** Async queue event on `updatedAt` advance for issues that currently have an `activeRecoveryAction`, so the evaluator wakes on state change rather than purely on cadence.

---

### Asks — written confirmation requested on all of these

1. **Gap 2 fix or workaround (most urgent)** — please confirm either the admin clear endpoint is on the roadmap with an ETA, or document the currently supported manual workaround so we can unblock PRO-5104.
2. **Gap 1 fix or design clarification** — please confirm whether evidence refresh is intended behaviour (and we are misreading the design) or a defect, and the planned remediation.
3. **Gap 3 fix or design clarification** — same question for re-evaluation on issue update.
4. **ETAs** — target ship date or workaround availability for each gap.
5. **Documentation** — publication of any approved workaround in Paperclip platform docs so other tenants encountering the same shape can self-serve.

---

### Channel note

Production City agents cannot post directly to APE issues (cross-company API restriction) and cannot use external email channels (internal governance policy GV-2026-002). This GitHub issu
