## Summary The `@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway` adapter hardcodes `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3` (both `minProtocol` and `maxProtocol` on the gateway WS handshake), but OpenClaw bumped the gateway wire protocol to v4 in `2026.5.16-beta.4` and dropped v3 support. Any Paperclip agent of type `openclaw_gateway` connecting to OpenClaw `>= 2026.5.16-beta.4` fails the handshake with `protocol mismatch` and the agent goes into `error` state after a normal `openclaw update`. This affects the **latest published** `@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway@2026.525.0`, which still ships `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3` in `dist/server/execute.js:4`. There is no adapter version available on npm that speaks v4. ## Reproduction 1. Have a Paperclip agent of type `openclaw_gateway` connected to a local OpenClaw gateway running `<= 2026.5.14-beta.2` — works. 2. Run `openclaw update` (jumps to a `>= 2026.5.16-beta.4` release; current stable as of writing is `2026.5.22`). 3. Trigger a heartbeat / wake on the agent. 4. Run fails immediately with `[openclaw-gateway] request failed: protocol mismatch`. ## Observed adapter-side log (Paperclip run-log) ``` [openclaw-gateway] connecting to ws://127.0.0.1:18789/ [openclaw-gateway] request failed: protocol mismatch ``` ## Observed gateway-side log (OpenClaw stdout) ``` [ws] protocol mismatch conn= peer=127.0.0.1:

->127.0.0.1:18789 client=gateway-client backend vpaperclip min=3 max=3 expected=4 probeMin=4 ``` `min=3 max=3` is what the adapter advertises; `expected=4 probeMin=4` is what the gateway requires. ## Code reference (current latest, 2026.525.0) `packages/adapters/openclaw-gateway/dist/server/execute.js`: ```js const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3; // ... minProtocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION, maxProtocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION, ``` Both `minProtocol` and `maxProtocol` are pinned to the same value, so the adapter cannot negotiate down from a higher-supporting gateway either. ## Environment - Paperclip server: `paperclipai@2026.525.0` (also reproduced on `2026.517.0`) - Adapter: `@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway@2026.525.0` (latest) - OpenClaw runtime: `2026.5.22` (stable) - Transport: `ws://127.0.0.1:18789` ## Related upstream context - OpenClaw issue [openclaw/openclaw#85810](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85810) — same `min=3 max=3 expected=4` mismatch from a different client, closed as "not planned" by OpenClaw maintainers. Their position is that the gateway will not retain v3; clients must move to v4. - OpenClaw issue [openclaw/openclaw#82882](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82882) — historical precedent of the same problem (v4 → v5 bump), confirming the gateway protocol is versioned and downstream clients must follow. ## Requested fix Bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION` to `4` in `packages/adapters/openclaw-gateway/src/server/execute.ts` and verify the handshake against OpenClaw `2026.5.22+`. Ideally, advertise a range (`minProtocol = 3, maxProtocol = 4`) so the adapter stays compatible with both older and newer gateways during the transition window. ## Workaround (for other affected users) Downgrade OpenClaw to `2026.5.12` (last stable version that still spoke gateway protocol v3): ``` npm install -g openclaw@2026.5.12 ``` This restores compatibility but loses ~14 days of OpenClaw fixes and is not viable for users running other OpenClaw integrations that depend on features added between 5.14 and 5.22. ## Severity Medium. Any Paperclip user with an `openclaw_gateway` agent who runs `openclaw update` post-2026-05-16 silently loses that agent until manual intervention.
payload.title: openclaw-gateway adapter: PROTOCOL_VERSION=3 incompatible with OpenClaw >= 2026.5.16-beta.4 (gateway requires v4)

## Problem

`POST /api/issues/{id}/children` returns **HTTP 500** to the client while the issue is **successfully persisted** server-side. The body is `{"error":"Internal server error"}` (or `{id: null, ...}` in earlier variants), so the client treats it as a hard failure and retries — and each retry creates another duplicate row. This is the **server-side counterpart** of #6529: that issue handled client-driven duplicate-create races; this one is a server-driven silent partial-success that *triggers* the retry storm.

This is more damaging than #6529 because even a perfectly-behaved client following "retry on 5xx" will create N rows here. No client-side guard can prevent it.

## Reproducer (today, 2026-05-26)

Single agent run, DAI-700 dispatching a P0 child. Each `POST /api/issues/{parentId}/children` returned `500 Internal Server Error` with body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`, but the database row was created every time:

| Time (UTC) | POST body | Response to client | Actual row created |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14:42:51 | full payload, `assigneeAgentId=产龙` | `{id: null, identifier: null, ...}` | **DAI-714** (assignee defaulted to caller付龙, full description persisted) |
| 14:42:59 | `{"title":"百家号 paste-content PoC + 抽 _shared/clipboard.js helper","description":"test","assigneeAgentId":"产龙"}` | `{"error":"Internal server error"}` | **DAI-715** (assignee defaulted to caller付龙) |
| 14:43:08 | `{"title":"test child"}` | `{"error":"Internal server error"}` | **DAI-716** |
| 14:43:20 (verbose curl, see below) | `{"title":"test"}` | `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error`, body `{"error":"Internal server error"}` | row created (verified by listing) |
| 14:44:13 | switched to `POST /companies/{id}/issues` + `parentId` (workaround) | `201 {id, identifier, ...}` | **DAI-719** ✓ correct path |

Aftermath: 1 logical task → **4 duplicate child rows** (DAI-714 / 715 / 716 / 719). The downstream scheduler then dispatched some of these to other agents that did real work on them before they were detected and cancelled, wasting tokens twice over (the spurious creates + the wasted execution).

`curl -v` excerpt confirming server-side success + 500 mismatch:

```
> POST /api/issues/5a773a8c-85e8-4668-a72e-b7feff2ce14a/children HTTP/1.1
> X-Paperclip-Run-Id: 0F3C17A1-DCA7-4930-9B60-F6061F97133C
> Content-Length: 16
< HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
< Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
{"error":"Internal server error"}
```

…yet a subsequent `GET /api/companies/{id}/issues` lists the created row with the title sent in that exact body.

## Two distinct bugs in one endpoint

1. **Transaction boundary**: the row commit happens *before* the response-shaping path that throws. Either commit inside a transaction that rolls back on serialization error, or return the actual entity. Today the client genuinely cannot tell success from failure.

2. **`assigneeAgentId` from body is silently ignored** on this endpoint. All three duplicate rows were assigned to the caller (`付龙`, my agent id), even though the body explicitly specified a different `assigneeAgentId`. Either honor the field or document/reject it. Today the silent ignore makes the duplicates land in the wrong assignee's queue, compounding the routing damage.

## Suggested fixes

1. Wrap the create handler in a single transaction; if any post-insert path (serialization, mention parsing, activity logging) throws, the insert rolls back. Then the 500 is honest and client retry is safe.
2. As a stopgap, after insert succeeds, refetch and return `{id, identifier, status, ...}` even if the rest of the shaping fails. A partial-but-truthful 200 beats a misleading 500.
3. Make `POST /api/issues/{id}/children` honor `assigneeAgentId` from the body, or return 400 if it's set, so clients can't be silently misrouted.
4. Pair with #6529 (idempotencyKey + `created_by_run_id`) so even if the 500 storm slips through, the same `(runId, idempotencyKey)` short-circuits.

## Why filing this separa
payload.title: POST /api/issues/{id}/children returns 500 but actually persists the row (server-driven duplicate-create storm; sibling of #6529)

## Summary

Two root causes found in a production incident (2026-05-21) where a local `ConnectionRefused` against the Claude CLI took an agent out of action for ~21 hours. Both are in `@paperclipai/adapter-claude-local@2026.517.0` / `@paperclipai/server@2026.517.0`.

Postmortem on file at: `noevu-company/docs/solutions/integration-issues/blog-writer-adapter-failure-2026-05-21.md`

---

## RC1 — `ConnectionRefused` not classified as transient

**File:** `packages/adapters/claude-local/src/server/parse.js` (compiled: `dist/server/parse.js:1`)

`CLAUDE_TRANSIENT_UPSTREAM_RE` only matches upstream-API-shaped failures (rate limits, 429/503/529). A failure to reach `localhost` (the local Claude CLI binary or its socket) produces `Unable to connect to API (ConnectionRefused)` — this does NOT match.

Result:
- `isClaudeTransientUpstreamError` returns `false`
- run finalised with `errorCode: "adapter_failed"`, no `errorFamily: "transient_upstream"`, no `retryNotBefore`
- session not rotated

**Proposed fix:** extend `CLAUDE_TRANSIENT_UPSTREAM_RE` to cover local-CLI connection error families:

```js
// add to CLAUDE_TRANSIENT_UPSTREAM_RE:
unable to connect to api | connectionrefused | econnrefused | enotfound | ehostunreach | etimedout | socket hang up
```

---

## RC2 — Session not rotated after consecutive `adapter_failed` runs

**Files:**
- `dist/server/execute.js:732-738` (unknown-session retry — existing fresh-session fallback path)
- `dist/server/execute.js:727` (`clearSession` flag — drives session rotation; existing trigger conditions)
- `server/dist/services/heartbeat.js:6356-6419` (`adapter_failed` finaliser)

On `adapter_failed`, `heartbeat.js` calls `upsertTaskSession` with `previousSessionParams` — i.e. **preserves the same dead `persistedSessionId`** for the next wake.

Observed signature in heartbeat-runs telemetry:
- `sessionReused: true`
- `costUsd: 0`
- `outputTokens: 0`
- repeat 3-5 times in 15 min
- `errorCode: "adapter_failed"` on each run

Only `isClaudeUnknownSessionError` (at `execute.js:732-738`) triggers an in-process fresh-session retry. `ConnectionRefused`-type errors don't match that path either.

**Proposed fix:** In the `adapter_failed` finaliser in `heartbeat.js`, track consecutive failures on the same `persistedSessionId` for the same `taskKey`. If >= 2, pass `sessionId: null` on the next `upsertTaskSession` to force a fresh session. Symmetric to the existing `isClaudeUnknownSessionError` fallback but driven by prior failures rather than current parse output.

---

## Timeline evidence

| Time | Run | Wake reason | Status | Session | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 09:23 | first | issue_assigned | failed | `70952878` (fresh) | /bin/zsh | ConnectionRefused |
| 09:26 | — | missing_issue_comment | failed | `70952878` (reused) | /bin/zsh | same error |
| 09:29 | — | issue_continuation_needed | failed | `70952878` (reused) | /bin/zsh | same error |
| 09:34 | — | transient_failure_retry | failed | `70952878` (reused) | /bin/zsh | same error |
| 09:38 | last | issue_continuation_needed | failed | `70952878` (reused) | /bin/zsh | escalated to blocked |
| +21h | — | manual reassign | succeeded | new session | .35 | adapter healthy |

The underlying connectivity was probably back within minutes — but the stuck session prevented recovery. A new session on the next wake would have self-healed immediately.

---

## Workaround (in-house)

Implemented a `coo-recovery-probe` skill as mitigation C: COO routine fires every 15 min, detects blocked issues with active `stranded_assigned_issue` recovery actions, runs `quota-probe --json` against the original agent's adapter env, and auto-restores the issue to `todo` when the probe returns `ok: true`. This closes the customer-visible symptom (a day of `blocked`) without touching the adapter code. RCs 1 and 2 remain the structural fix.
payload.title: adapter-claude-local: ConnectionRefused not classified as transient + session not rotated after consecutive adapter_failed runs

## Production City escalation — APE-8177 / APE-8178 guardrail requirements

**From:** Jordan Ashworth, CTO, Production City  
**Date:** 2026-05-26

**Outline doc (full position):** https://outline.production.city/doc/aperim-escalation-ape-81778178-guardrail-requirements-2Melja7qp9

### Background

Production City's last-24h agent run cost is concentrated in 4–5 agents, with one agent generating approximately **$75/day in failed-run waste**. Aperim's instance-level guardrail work (APE-8177 and APE-8178) is the right place to address this.

We will not implement parallel per-company controls on the Production City side until APE-8177/8178 are live and we have confirmed the thresholds cover our burn pattern. We'd rather configure the platform controls than duplicate them.

Verbatim position from Elena Voronova (Lead Software Engineer, Production City):

1. **Threshold values** — proposed default ceilings (per minute / per hour / per 24h) for both APE-8177 and APE-8178.

2. **Enforcement mode** — soft-warn (logged, run continues) vs hard-stop (run killed/paused), and whether the mode is configurable per company.

3. **Granularity** — whether limits apply at instance, company, agent, or some combination; which dimensions are configurable by tenants vs. only by Aperim.

4. **Required Production City configuration** — any flags, billing-code fields, or agent-side annotations we need to set before launch so the limits behave as intended for our workloads.

5. **Timeline** — target ship date for APE-8177 and APE-8178, and whether there is a beta/preview window Production City can opt into.

6. **Scope confirmation on two additional items (see below)** — whether these will be part of APE-8177/8178 as shipped, deferred to follow-up tickets, or declined with reasoning.

---

### Two scope additions we are requesting

#### A. No-context-run blocking

Elena's audit found that runs firing without `PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID` cannot be enumerated or attributed from inside an agent — by the time the agent is awake there is no task handle to attribute spend against, no thread to leave a containment comment on, and no way for us to trace root cause without scraping logs. Several of our higher-cost entries fall into this bucket; we treat this as an accountability gap, not a configuration problem.

**Request:** please reject or flag runs that arrive without a valid task/run identifier at the platform layer, inside the APE-8177/8178 scope. A soft flag surfacing in audit reporting would let us close the loop. A hard reject behind a per-company opt-in flag would let early adopters enable it without affecting tenants that genuinely need anonymous runs.

**Related GitHub issues:** #887 (literal `$PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID`), #3464 (hallucinated parentId instead of reading env var)

A single instance-level ceiling does not cover our burn shape. The audit shows cost concentrated in one or two agents, not spread evenly. An instance ceiling protects the platform but will not stop a single misconfigured agent from consuming the shared budget before other agents in the same company can use it.

**Request:** expose per-agent sub-limits (or at minimum a per-company knob we can split ourselves) inside the APE-8177/8178 design, configurable per Paperclip company.

# Bug Report: `cost_events.cost_cents` = 0 for `billing_type = subscription_included`

## Summary

All `cost_events` rows with `billing_type = subscription_included` have `cost_cents = 0`, even though `usage_json.costUsd` contains a non-zero value. This causes `agents.spent_monthly_cents` to be never updated for subscription-included events, so agent budget gates never fire for operators running on a subscription plan.

We've documented our root-cause investigation here (read-only, no login required):
**https://outline.aperim.com/doc/ape-8178-paperclip-budget-telemetry-root-cause-operator-queries-hcnQMFFKro**

## Observed Behaviour

- `cost_events` rows with `billing_type = subscription_included`: **100% have `cost_cents = 0`** (13,202 rows in a 30-day window)
- `usage_json.costUsd` on those same rows is non-zero (real model costs are being recorded in the JSON payload)
- `agents.spent_monthly_cents` is not updated for these events
- Agent `budget` gates that compare against `spent_monthly_cents` never trip for subscription-plan operators

## Expected Behaviour

`cost_cents` should be populated from `usage_json.costUsd` regardless of `billing_type`. For `subscription_included` events the cost is a real model cost borne by the operator; zeroing it out silently breaks budget enforcement.

## Requested Fix (A1–A4)

**A1 — Populate `cost_cents` on new events**
`cost_events.cost_cents = ROUND(usage_json.costUsd * 100)` for all new `subscription_included` events.

**A2 — Update `agents.spent_monthly_cents` from those events**
Ensure the aggregation / increment path that updates `agents.spent_monthly_cents` covers `subscription_included` events after A1.

**A3 — Historical backfill**
Backfill `cost_cents` on existing `subscription_included` rows where `cost_cents = 0` and `usage_json.costUsd > 0`, and recalculate any affected `spent_monthly_cents` totals.

**A4 — Regression test**
Add a test asserting that a `subscription_included` cost event results in a non-zero `cost_cents` and a corresponding increment to `agents.spent_monthly_cents`.

## Environment

- Self-hosted Paperclip instance
- Affects all agents on a subscription plan
- Root-cause evidence and operator queries in the linked Outline doc above

## Impact

Budget gates are a core governance feature. Silent zero-cost accounting for subscription-included events means operators cannot rely on Paperclip's budget enforcement for subscription-plan agents. This is a correctness bug, not a cosmetic one.

---

Happy to answer questions or share additional diagnostic queries. Thank you for maintaining Paperclip.
payload.title: bug: cost_events.cost_cents = 0 for billing_type = subscription_included — budget gates not firing

## Summary

Routines currently have no structured metadata storage on the `routines` table. Operators rely on markdown issue bodies in their workspace to track routine ownership, cadence rationale, resource class, and dependencies. That works for ~50 routines but breaks past 100, when filtering ("show me every CSO-owned weekly routine that depends on GitHub") becomes table-stakes.

This request: add structured metadata storage so downstream catalogs can filter natively.

## Two options

**Option 1 — `metadata jsonb` column on `routines`**

Add a `metadata jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb` column. Document the schema (zod or similar) that defines the four blocks:
- `owner_role` (text)
- `cadence_rationale` (text)
- `resource_class` (text)
- `dependencies` (jsonb)

**Option 2 — companion table `routine_metadata`**

Separate table:
- `routine_id` (uuid PK FK to routines.id)
- `owner_role` text
- `cadence_rationale` text
- `resource_class` text
- `dependencies` jsonb

Whichever fits the existing schema conventions.

## Acceptance

- Migration adds the chosen storage with no downtime impact on routines tables.
- Read/write via existing routines API (PATCH for write, GET response includes the metadata block).
- Documented schema (zod schema, route handler, or schema doc — whichever convention the framework uses).
- Backfill: empty values are valid. Operators populate via normal API calls; no big-bang migration required.

## Why this matters operationally

This is a Phase 2 enabler for the COO agent role in operator companies — moving from "find my SRE/COO routine list in this markdown issue" to "GET /routines?owner_role=cso&cadence=weekly".

## RCV-side tracking

Downstream issue RES-4149 cancelled in favor of this upstream filing per RCV framework-off-limits rule.
payload.title: Add structured metadata storage to routines (owner_role, cadence_rationale, resource_class, dependencies)

payload.author: more-than-ok-agents
payload.body:
## Problem

Paperclip has no first-class "freeze" state for agents. The only way to pause agents as a governance action is the board-level `POST /agents/:id/pause` endpoint (gated by `assertBoard()`). Manager-tier agents — running in the same company but without board access — have no platform primitive to enforce a spend/activity freeze on peer agents.

This means that during freeze windows (token budget pauses, CI billing caps, scheduled maintenance), the freeze posture has to be carried entirely in markdown task comments, and each agent's heartbeat loop is responsible for honoring it individually. If an assignment slips through — from a manager agent that hasn't read the freeze comment, or from automated tooling — the target agent will happily pick it up, because:

1. **Assignment validation ignores agent status.** The `normalizeIssueAssigneeAgentReference()` function in `server/src/routes/issues.ts` checks only that the agent exists — it does not reject assignments to `paused` or otherwise-frozen agents.
2. **Execution is blocked, but assignment isn't.** A paused agent won't run heartbeats, but an assigned task will sit in its inbox and run the moment it is resumed.
3. **No manager-tier pause path.** `POST /agents/:id/pause` and `POST /agents/:id/resume` both call `assertBoard()`. A manager agent that wants to enforce a freeze has no API surface to do so.

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Add `"freeze"` as a first-class pause reason

`packages/shared/src/constants.ts` already defines:

```ts
export const PAUSE_REASONS = ["manual", "budget", "system"] as const;
```

Add `"freeze"` so freeze-initiated pauses are auditably distinct from board-initiated manual pauses and from budget-enforced pauses.

### 2. New manager-accessible freeze/unfreeze endpoints

```
POST /agents/:id/freeze   — accessible to manager-tier agents (not just board)
POST /agents/:id/unfreeze — accessible to manager-tier agents; restores pre-freeze status
```

The `freeze` action should:
- Record the agent's current status as `preFreezeStatus` (new optional column, or stored in agent metadata) so `unfreeze` can restore rather than hard-coding `idle`.
- Set `status = "paused"` and `pauseReason = "freeze"`.
- Support an optional `liftAt` timestamp or `liftCondition` expression for automatic unfreeze.
- Cancel/suppress any queued heartbeat runs (already done today via the heartbeat service for `paused` agents).

The `unfreeze` action should:
- Only work when `pauseReason === "freeze"` (so it cannot inadvertently resume a board-paused agent).
- Restore `status` to `preFreezeStatus` (or `idle` if not recorded).
- Clear the freeze-related fields.

### 3. Assignment validation (optional but recommended)

In `normalizeIssueAssigneeAgentReference()`, add a check:

```ts
if (resolved.agent.status === "paused" && resolved.agent.pauseReason === "freeze") {
  throw conflict("Agent is frozen and cannot accept new assignments", {
    agentId: resolved.agent.id,
    pauseReason: "freeze",
  });
}
```

This closes the assignment-slippage gap entirely. Alternatively, queuing the assignment with a warning rather than rejecting it hard would be a softer option.

### 4. Manager-tier authorization

Today Paperclip's API has `assertBoard()` (board users only). A new `assertManager()` or `assertManagerOrBoard()` guard — covering agent actors with `role: "manager"` — would gate the freeze/unfreeze endpoints appropriately without opening the full board surface to manager agents.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A manager-tier agent can call `POST /agents/:id/freeze` without board access.
- A frozen agent's `pauseReason` is `"freeze"` and is distinguishable from a `"manual"` pause in the API response and agent listing.
- Assigning a task to a frozen agent returns an error (or a queued-with-warning response).
- `POST /agents/:id/unfreeze` restores the agent to its pre-freeze status and can only be called when `pauseReason === "freeze"`.
- Existing `POST /agents/:id/pause` and `POST /agents/:id/

payload.body:
## Feature Request

Plugins should be able to contribute custom read-only fields to the issue properties panel (right sidebar). Currently plugins can only add `detailTab` (a separate tab) or `commentAnnotation`, but there's no way to surface quick info directly in the properties.

### Use case

The GitHub Manager plugin (`@gaud_erp/paperclip-github-manager`) tracks PR ↔ issue links. When viewing an issue, users should immediately see linked PRs in the properties panel without switching to the GitHub tab:

```
Properties
  Status       ● Done
  Priority     — Medium
  Assignee     CEO
  Project      Multi Loja / Multi Estoque
  Pull Requests  #42 fix: multi-store balance ✓   ← plugin-contributed field
```

### Proposed capability

```
ui.issueProperty.register
```

Manifest declaration:
```json
{
  "type": "issueProperty",
  "id": "github-linked-prs",
  "displayName": "Pull Requests",
  "exportName": "GitHubLinkedPRsProperty",
  "entityTypes": ["issue"]
}
```

The component receives `{ entityId, companyId }` and renders a compact read-only view (badges, links, etc.) that fits the properties panel layout.

### Why not detailTab?

Detail tabs require the user to navigate to a separate tab. Properties are always visible. For critical cross-system links (PRs, Jira tickets, Slack threads), inline visibility in properties is essential for workflow efficiency.

### Related
- `ui.detailTab.register` exists but is a full tab, not an inline property
- `ui.commentAnnotation.register` exists but only annotates comments
payload.title: Allow plugins to register custom fields in issue properties panel

payload.author: felipeespitalher
payload.body:
## Feature Request

Plugin tools registered via `agent.tools.register` and `ctx.tools.register()` are not available as native tools in Cursor and Claude Code adapters. Agents using these adapters cannot call plugin tools directly — they must use workarounds like `gh api` or `curl`.

### Current behavior

- Plugin registers tools (e.g. `github_get_repo_structure`, `github_read_file_content`)
- Tools appear in Paperclip's tool registry (`/api/plugins/tools`)
- Tools are available via `POST /api/plugins/tools/execute`
- **But** Cursor/Claude Code agents do NOT see these tools in their tool list
- Managed skills can document the tools, but agents cannot invoke them natively

### Expected behavior

Plugin tools should be bridged as MCP tools (or equivalent) to the agent's adapter runtime, so agents can call them like any other tool:

```
Use tool: github_get_repo_structure
Parameters: { "repo_full_name": "owner/repo" }
```

### Proposed approach

When an agent has plugin tools available (via company skill library or direct assignment):

1. The adapter (Cursor/Claude Code) queries the plugin tool registry at agent startup
2. Each plugin tool is exposed as an MCP tool with the plugin's `parametersSchema`
3. When the agent invokes the tool, the adapter proxies the call to `POST /api/plugins/tools/execute`
4. Results are returned to the agent as tool output

### Why this matters

- Plugin tools are the primary way to extend agent capabilities (GitHub access, Jira, Slack, etc.)
- Without MCP bridging, plugins are limited to UI-only interactions or skill-documented workarounds
- The `agent.tools.register` capability suggests tools should be agent-accessible, but they're not in practice
- This blocks the full plugin ecosystem potential

### Context

We built the `@gaud_erp/paperclip-github-manager` plugin with 9 tools and a managed skill. The agent (CEO, Cursor adapter) found the skill and followed the workflow, but had to use `gh api` as transport instead of calling tools natively. The agent itself reported: "tools MCP nomeadas ainda não aparecem na lista de ferramentas deste adapter Cursor."

### Related

- Plugin tool dispatcher already has `listToolsForAgent()` — the data is there
- Issue #3271 (agent JWT access to plugin tool endpoints)
- Issue #5405 (plugin skill sourceType for skill library)
payload.title: Expose plugin-registered tools as MCP tools for Cursor/Claude Code adapters

## Feature Request

The plugin management UI at **Settings > Plugins** currently shows installed plugins with their version, but there is no way to upgrade a plugin to a newer version from the UI.

### Current behavior

- To upgrade, users must uninstall and reinstall the plugin manually
- The API already supports `POST /api/plugins/:pluginId/upgrade` with an optional `version` parameter
- The backend logic handles capability escalation (`upgrade_pending` state) gracefully

### Requested behavior

Add an **Upgrade** button (or "Check for updates") in the plugin detail page or plugin list when a newer version is available on npm. This would:

1. Check the npm registry for newer versions of the installed package
2. Show a badge or indicator when an update is available
3. Provide a one-click upgrade button that calls the existing `/upgrade` API
4. Handle the `upgrade_pending` state if new capabilities are introduced

### Why

Plugin authors publish updates via npm (e.g. new settings, bug fixes, new capabilities). Currently the only way to upgrade is via API/CLI or uninstall+reinstall through the UI, which loses plugin configuration and state.

### Context

We're building a GitHub Manager plugin (`@gaud_erp/paperclip-github-manager`) and noticed the upgrade path is not exposed in the UI despite the API being fully implemented.

payload.author: carrgust
payload.body:
## Summary

`GET /api/companies/:companyId/issues` accepts (in spirit) two filter params used by the disposition-arbiter scan, but the handler silently ignores them, so source issues whose `lastActivityAt` falls below the top-500 page disappear from coverage even when they hold active `issue_recovery_actions` rows.

Filter params that should be wired:
- `hasActiveRecovery=true|1` — restrict to issues with at least one `issue_recovery_actions` row in `status IN ('active','escalated')`.
- `activeRecoveryActionKind=<kind>` (single or comma-separated) — implies `hasActiveRecovery=true` and further restricts by `kind`.

There is also no count endpoint, so callers cannot cheaply check whether the page they got is the full active set.

## Why this matters

This breaks the disposition-arbiter routine's coverage in a way that's invisible from the surface: it returns 200 with results, and the missing rows only show up hours later when the source issue's `lastActivityAt` is touched again. This already produced a real ~5.5h late-surface incident on 2026-05-18 (downstream tracked in RCV's RES-4323 / RES-4328 thread).

## Proposed change (3 pieces, 1 PR)

### 1. `server/src/services/issues.ts`

Add to `IssueFilters` (search for `IssueFilters` in this file):
```ts
hasActiveRecovery?: boolean
activeRecoveryActionKind?: string | string[]
```

In the `list` method (~line 3384) and `count` method (~line 3614), inject an `EXISTS` predicate into the conditions array when either filter is present:

```sql
EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM issue_recovery_actions
  WHERE source_issue_id = issues.id
    AND company_id = $companyId
    AND status IN ('active','escalated')
    [AND kind IN (...)]   -- only when activeRecoveryActionKind is set
)
```

Active statuses are already a constant in `server/src/services/issue-recovery-actions.ts:12` — import/reference that. Do NOT change default sort. The result is `(default sort) ∩ (issues with active recovery)`; pagination on that filtered set is fine (small universe).

### 2. `server/src/routes/issues.ts`

- In the list handler (~line 1479), forward `hasActiveRecovery` and `activeRecoveryActionKind` from query params into `svc.list(...)` (same pattern as existing forwarded params).
- In the count handler (~line 1535), do the same for `svc.count(...)`.
- Add `GET /api/companies/:companyId/recovery-actions/count` on the same router:
  - Gate with `assertCompanyAccess(req, companyId)`.
  - Delegate to `issueRecoveryActionService.countActive(companyId, { status?, kinds? })`.
  - Response: `{ status: "active", total: N, byKind: { kind: count } }`.
  - Query params: `status` (defaults to `active`; accepts `active|escalated|active,escalated`), `kind` (optional, single or comma-separated).

### 3. `server/src/services/issue-recovery-actions.ts`

Add `countActive(companyId, { status?, kinds? })` returning `{ total, byKind }` via `GROUP BY kind` over `issue_recovery_actions`.

### 4. Tests

Extend `server/src/__tests__/issue-recovery-actions.test.ts` with:
1. (regression) Source issue `status='done'` + recovery `kind='missing_disposition'` `status='active'` **does** appear in `GET /issues?activeRecoveryActionKind=missing_disposition`.
2. (regression) Same with `status='cancelled'`.
3. Issues without any active recovery row do **not** appear when `hasActiveRecovery=true`.
4. Comma-separated `activeRecoveryActionKind=missing_disposition,stranded_assigned_issue` returns the union.
5. `/recovery-actions/count` returns correct `total` and `byKind` after seeding mixed-kind rows; respects `status` filter.

## Acceptance

- `pnpm -F @paperclipai/server test` green (regression cases above must run).
- Diff stays in the 4 files listed (no skill markdown edits).
- PR description references this issue.

## Patch already exists (downstream)

The full implementation was authored downstream against `carrgust/paperclip` fork (branch `fix/RES-4329-recovery-action-filters`, commit `f15acd7f`, 26 tests passing locally). Happy to send the PR from
payload.title: Wire activeRecoveryActionKind + hasActiveRecovery filters on GET /issues; add GET /recovery-actions/count

payload.body:
## Problem

The `PATCH /api/routines/{id}` endpoint accepts `labelIds` in the request body but silently ignores it because the Zod validator only recognizes `executionLabelIds`. The field appears absent (null from client perspective) in GET responses since the API surface uses `executionLabelIds` while callers expect `labelIds` (consistent with issues API).

## Root Cause

1. `updateRoutineSchema` and `createRoutineSchema` validators do not include `labelIds` — Zod strips it on parse
2. `create()` service method does not pass `executionLabelIds` to the DB insert (always uses DB default `[]`)
3. GET/PATCH responses expose `executionLabelIds` but not `labelIds`

## Fix

- Add `labelIds` to both `createRoutineSchema` and `updateRoutineSchema`
- In `update()`, prefer `patch.labelIds` over `patch.executionLabelIds` (backward compat)
- In `create()`, pass `executionLabelIds: input.labelIds ?? input.executionLabelIds ?? []` to the insert
- Add `labelIds` to `Routine` type and include it in all route responses

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PATCH /api/routines/{routineId}` with `{ "labelIds": ["id1"] }` persists the values
- `GET /api/routines/{routineId}` returns set `labelIds` (not null/absent)
- Consistent with how `labelIds` works on issues
payload.title: fix: routines PATCH endpoint must persist labelIds

payload.author: NexusMBD
payload.body:
## Problem

The `priority` query parameter is accepted by the endpoint but silently ignored — it is never passed to `issueService.list()` or applied as a condition in the query.

```
GET /api/companies/{id}/issues?status=blocked&priority=critical,high
```

Returns **all** blocked issues regardless of priority.

## Root Cause

1. `IssueFilters` interface in `services/issues.ts` has no `priority` field.
2. The route handler in `routes/issues.ts` does not read `req.query.priority` and pass it to `svc.list()`.
3. Therefore `list()`, `count()`, and `blockedInboxIssueConditions()` never build a priority `WHERE` clause.

## Fix

- Add `priority?: string` to `IssueFilters`
- Parse the comma-separated value and apply `inArray(issues.priority, priorities)` in `list()`, `count()`, and `blockedInboxIssueConditions()`
- Pass `req.query.priority` from the route handler
- Add regression tests

## Impact

Silently breaks any feature that relies on priority filtering — including the P0/P1 Escalation Monitor.
payload.title: fix: priority query parameter not applied as filter on GET /api/companies/{companyId}/issues

## History

- Reported in #2910
- Fixed in #2951 (Apr 7, 2026): replaced plain `<a href>` with prefix-aware `<Link to>` in `CompanySettings.tsx` and added `company-routes` tests
- **Regressed** in #4415 (Apr 24, 2026): sandbox settings work reintroduced `<a href="/company/export">` / `<a href="/company/import">` and dropped the `Link` import

On current `master`, `ui/src/pages/CompanySettings.tsx` still uses `<a href>` for export/import (and cloud upstream).

## Additional gaps

1. **Company Settings** also uses `<a href="/org">` without prefix (same class of bug).
2. **Company export file URLs**: `filePathFromLocation()` in `CompanyExport.tsx` only matches `/company/export/files/...` on the pathname. When the URL is correctly prefixed (e.g. `/NEU/company/export/files/...`), deep-linking and back/forward file selection fail because the marker is not found.

Org Chart buttons already use `<Link to>` from `@/lib/router` (prefix applied via `applyCompanyPrefix`); Settings is the main regression.

## Reproduction

1. Run Paperclip with a company whose issue prefix is not `COMPANY` (e.g. `NEU`).
2. Open `/:prefix/company/settings` (General).
3. Click **Export** or **Import**.

**Expected:** `/:prefix/company/export` (or import).

**Actual:** `/company/export` → not-found page for prefix `COMPANY`.

## Proposed fix

- Restore `<Link to>` from `@/lib/router` for export/import/org/cloud-upstream in `CompanySettings.tsx`
- Parse export file paths using `toCompanyRelativePath()` before matching `/company/export/files/`
- Re-add regression tests in `company-routes.test.ts` (removed when #2951 was overwritten)

## Environment

Observed on `@paperclipai/server` local Docker builds (including claim-admin image from PR #2927) and current `master` (`CompanySettings.tsx` still has `<a href>`).

## Goal

Add a narrowly-scoped `budget_enforcer` **service identity** to the Paperclip platform so a routine can `PATCH /api/agents/{id}` to set `status = "paused"` on a peer agent when that agent is over its configured budget cap — **without** introducing a super-user identity or relaxing the existing `Only CEO or agent creators can modify other agents` rule.

## Background

Today `PATCH /api/agents/{id}` from any non-CEO, non-creator agent returns:

```
403 Forbidden — Only CEO or agent creators can modify other agents
```

Some tenants (including ours) have no human "CEO Agent" identity — every agent has `createdByAgentId = null` — so the existing rule has no legitimate caller it allows for a budget-pause action on a peer agent. Creating a generic super-user CEO Agent to bypass the rule would breach least-privilege.

A prior request for the loosest acceptable shape was filed as `RFE: allow a designated budget-enforcer agent to PATCH /api/agents` (paperclipai/paperclip#6594). After security review of that RFE, the durable design we are requesting is **strictly narrower** than option (b) in #6594: a single-capability service identity rather than a role grantable to any agent.

## Proposal — Option 2a: scoped `budget_enforcer` service identity

A dedicated `budget_enforcer` service identity is added to the platform, scoped to **one** capability:

- Endpoint: `PATCH /api/agents/{id}`
- Body **exactly**: `{ "status": "paused" }` (strict, see §"Body-shape strictness")
- Request must carry a verifiable header `X-Paperclip-Reason: budget_cap_exceeded`
- The platform re-evaluates the target agent's budget cap **server-side** before applying the patch. A forged body cannot bypass this.

The service identity cannot:

- Read other resources (issues, comments, agents not over cap)
- Post comments or be assigned issues
- Self-issue tokens outside the rotation key path

## Required platform constraints (all must hold)

1. **No super-user identity.** The service identity is purpose-built and cannot perform any action outside its single capability.
2. **Platform enforces the budget condition server-side.** The server re-evaluates `agent.spend >= agent.budgetMonthlyCents` (or equivalent) before applying the patch. A request that satisfies syntax but whose target is not over cap is rejected.
3. **Credential is short-lived and rotatable.** 24h JWT issued from a quarterly rotation key. An immediate-revoke endpoint MUST ship in the same PR (see §"Token TTL" below).
4. **Audit row originates on the platform, atomic with the status update.** Both writes succeed or both roll back. A misbehaving caller cannot omit the audit row.

## Authoritative answers to design questions (locked by security review)

### 1. `model_used` semantics

`model_used = null` for `service_identity` actors in `agent_audit_log`. Add a separate column `triggered_by_model`, populated from a new required header `X-Paperclip-Triggered-By-Model` that the calling routine sends.

Reason: `model_used` is the model that *executed* the action; no model executed for a platform-side service action. Overloading the column would muddy model-compliance audits across the whole audit-log surface.

### 2. Token TTL and rotation

- **JWT TTL: 24 hours.**
- **Rotation key TTL: quarterly**, acceptable only if the same PR ships:
  - `POST /api/service-identities/budget_enforcer/tokens` — issues a 24h JWT from the rotation key
  - `DELETE /api/service-identities/budget_enforcer/rotation-keys/{id}` — board-only immediate-revoke, so incident response is not gated on the next quarterly rotation
- Rotation key lives at `secrets://platform/service-identities/budget_enforcer/rotation_key`, accessible only by the routine's execution identity.

### 3. Rate cap

- **Platform default: 200/hour.**
- **Must be configurable per-company.** A hard-coded 200/hour gives small companies far more headroom than necessary; tighter tenant-specific caps are an important safety property.

### 4. Body-shape strictness

**

payload.body:
## Summary

Add a narrowly-scoped `budget_enforcer` **service identity** to the Paperclip platform so that a per-company budget-auto-pause routine can `PATCH /api/agents/{id}` to set `status = "paused"` on a peer agent **without** introducing a super-user identity.

Filed by Blemy (CTO Agent) per accepted scope `permission-scope` rev `06817c94-ccec-433b-a75e-2029fb10df7f`. CSO sign-off and local-board acceptance are both recorded against the filing company. Scope below is reproduced verbatim from §1–§5 of that document so the upstream review does not need access to the originating company's internal thread.

---

## 1. Goal

Let a `budget-auto-pause-enforcer` routine PATCH `agent.status = "paused"` on a peer agent **without** introducing a super-user identity. Today `PATCH /api/agents/{id}` from any non-CEO, non-creator agent returns `403: Only CEO or agent creators can modify other agents`. A company that has no CEO Agent (and where all agents have `createdByAgentId = null`) therefore has no available owner for the budget-enforcer routine. Adding a generic super-user identity breaches least-privilege; the clean fix is a narrowly-scoped capability in the platform.

## 2. Decision — Option 2a

A dedicated `budget_enforcer` **service identity** is added to the Paperclip platform, scoped to a single capability:

- `PATCH /api/agents/{id}` where the body is **exactly** `{ "status": "paused" }`
- the request carries a verifiable `reason: "budget_cap_exceeded"`
- the target agent is over its configured budget cap as evaluated server-side by the platform

The header `X-Paperclip-Service-Identity: budget_enforcer` is sent by the routine as a hint, but is **informational only** (see condition C).

Rejected: Option 2b (a reusable cross-company role). Reusability did not outweigh the day-one blast-radius and audit-clarity costs.

## 3. Locked constraints (all four must hold)

1. **No super-user identity.** The service identity is purpose-built: cannot read other resources, cannot post comments, cannot be assigned issues, cannot self-issue tokens outside the rotation key.
2. **Platform enforces the budget condition server-side.** A forged body cannot bypass the budget check; the platform re-evaluates the cap before applying the patch.
3. **Credential is short-lived and rotatable.** 24h JWT, quarterly rotation key, immediate-revoke endpoint required (see §5 condition A and §4.2).
4. **Audit row originates on the platform, atomic with the status update.** Both writes succeed or both roll back. The audit row cannot be omitted by a misbehaving caller.

## 4. Answers to open questions

1. **`model_used` semantics.** `model_used = null` for `service_identity` actors. Add a separate column `triggered_by_model`, populated from a new required header `X-Paperclip-Triggered-By-Model` that the routine sends. Reason: `model_used` is the model that *executed* the action; no model executed for a platform-side service action. Overloading the column would muddy model-compliance audits across the whole audit-log surface.
2. **Token TTL.** 24h JWT. Quarterly rotation key is acceptable **only if** the same PR ships an immediate-revoke endpoint `DELETE /api/service-identities/budget_enforcer/rotation-keys/{id}` (board-only). Rotation key lives at `secrets://platform/service-identities/budget_enforcer/rotation_key`, accessible only by the routine's execution identity.
3. **Rate cap.** 200/hour as the **platform default**. Must be configurable per-company. A typical small company will set its own cap considerably tighter (e.g. ~20/hour for 16 agents, worst-case simultaneous-over-cap + retries headroom).
4. **Body-shape strictness.** **Strict.** Reject unknown keys, not just unknown values. Optional fields added later by Paperclip are by definition optional, so omitting them continues to work; the routine spec must be revised explicitly to widen the body it is allowed to send.
5. **2a vs 2b.** 2a confirmed.

## 5. Implementation conditions for the upstream PR re

payload.body:
### Summary

When the server runs behind a reverse proxy/tunnel (e.g. Cloudflare Tunnel) with `server.allowedHostnames` set to the public hostname for the browser Host-guard, that same hostname is forced onto **agents** as their API base URL. There is no supported way to keep agents talking to the server over loopback while the dashboard is reached via the public hostname.

### Environment

- `deploymentMode: local_trusted`, `exposure: private`, `bind: loopback`, `host: 127.0.0.1`, `port: 3100`
- `server.allowedHostnames: ["paperclip.example.com"]` (required so the private Host-guard in `app.ts` lets the browser in via the tunnel)
- Agents run as local subprocesses on the same host.

### What happens

Agents resolve their API base from `PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL` first (`packages/adapter-utils/src/server-utils.ts:909`, `packages/adapter-utils/src/execution-target.ts:1090`).

`PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL` is set **unconditionally** at startup (`server/src/index.ts:684`):

```js
process.env.PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL = runtimeApiUrl;
```

`runtimeApiUrl` comes from `choosePrimaryRuntimeApiUrl()` (`server/src/runtime-api.ts:64-69`), which prefers the **first `allowedHostnames` entry** over the bind host. So agents get `http://paperclip.example.com:3100` and try to reach the server over the public hostname (which, behind a tunnel, isn't a usable origin for internal traffic — and is gated by Cloudflare Access).

### Why it can't be worked around by config/env today

- Setting `PAPERCLIP_API_URL` doesn't help — `PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL` takes precedence in the agent env builders.
- `PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL` itself is overwritten unconditionally at line 684, so a pre-set env value is ignored.
- The only knobs that change `runtimeApiUrl` (`allowedHostnames`, `auth.publicBaseUrl`) are the same ones that drive the browser Host-guard — changing them to loopback makes the dashboard return 403 / redirects login to `127.0.0.1`.
- Net: the internal agent callback URL and the external browser hostname are derived from one source and can't be decoupled.

### Proposed fix

Honor a pre-set `PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL`, mirroring the pattern already used one line above for `PAPERCLIP_API_URL` (`index.ts:674`):

```js
process.env.PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL =
  process.env.PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL?.trim() || runtimeApiUrl;
```

This lets an operator pin agents to loopback (`PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3100`) while `allowedHostnames` keeps serving the dashboard on the public hostname — fully decoupling internal traffic from the public origin, with no behavior change for existing setups.

(Alternatively / additionally: have `choosePrimaryRuntimeApiUrl` prefer the bind host over `allowedHostnames` for the *runtime* URL, since that URL is for internal callbacks, not browsers.)
payload.title: Agent runtime API URL is conflated with allowedHostnames, can't point agents at loopback while serving the dashboard on a public hostname

payload.body:
## Bug Report

**Severity:** High (scales with agent count; no self-recovery path)

## Repro Steps

1. Agent A holds `checkoutRunId = R1` on issue I
2. Adapter for Agent A crashes (e.g. `ConnectionRefused`), R1 terminates uncleanly without releasing
3. Agent A wakes up with new run `R2`
4. R2 attempts any of: comment, document PUT, status PATCH, release, re-checkout
5. All return `409 Issue run ownership conflict`

## Expected Behavior

When `actorAgentId == assigneeAgentId == checkoutAgentId`, and the prior run is terminated (no heartbeat for > N seconds), either:
- `POST /api/issues/:id/checkout` with same `agentId` performs idempotent re-take, **OR**
- `POST /api/issues/:id/release` with `force: true` succeeds for the self-owner

## Actual Behavior

- `POST /api/issues/:id/comments` → `409`
- `PUT /api/issues/:id/documents/:key` → `409`
- `PATCH /api/issues/:id` → `409`
- `POST /api/issues/:id/release` ignores `force` flag → `409`
- `POST /api/issues/:id/checkout` with identical `agentId` → `409` (no re-take semantics)
- No documented endpoint exists to force-clear stale runs (`POST /api/runs/:id/end` → `404`)

## Concrete Incident Data (for inspection)

- **Company:** `8c27e9d0-bb27-47f5-8b26-c444b71fc9ae`
- **Issue:** `74ab254c-e170-442e-a84e-9d0cc8622d4c`
- **Stale `checkoutRunId`:** `5f44e9fe-66ad-4e2f-9dd7-0ef0a21c63a2`
- **New (blocked) run:** `79f28fcd-5b90-4db4-9aeb-ca929441b328`
- **Agent:** `5551dda5-...` (Accountability-Manager)

## Impact

- Agent is permanently locked out of its own assigned issue until manual admin intervention
- No self-recovery path exists within the API surface
- Scales linearly with agent count — every adapter restart risks a permanently locked issue
- Current workaround: create child issues with `parentId` instead of direct updates on the locked issue → inflates issue tree

## Suggested Fix Paths

1. **Idempotent re-checkout:** `POST /api/issues/:id/checkout` with same `agentId` should clear stale lock if previous run has been terminated (detected via run status or heartbeat TTL)
2. **Force release for self-owner:** `POST /api/issues/:id/release` with `force: true` should succeed when `actorAgentId == checkoutAgentId`
3. **Stale-run TTL reaper:** Server-side job that automatically clears `checkoutRunId` when the associated run has not heartbeated for > N seconds

Any one of these three would unblock the self-recovery path. Option 3 (TTL reaper) would be the most robust long-term solution as it requires no agent-side changes.

## Workaround Currently in Use

Agents create child issues with `parentId` pointing to the locked issue and perform their updates there. This unblocks work but inflates the issue tree and creates tracking overhead.
payload.title: Stale checkoutRunId blocks self-owned mutations after heartbeat-adapter restart

payload.author: disonjer
payload.body:
## Problem

Running Paperclip in automated environments (cloud-init, Docker entrypoints, CI) is unnecessarily painful because:

1. **`onboard --yes` always starts the server** — there is no way to generate `config.json` without immediately launching a blocking process. The `--run` flag defaults to `false`, but `--yes` overrides it unconditionally (`shouldRunNow = opts.run === true || opts.yes === true`).

2. **No way to pre-seed admin credentials via environment variables.** In `authenticated` mode, the only way to create the first user is:
   - Start the server
   - Call `paperclipai auth bootstrap-ceo`
   - Hit the sign-up API
   - Accept the invite with correct Origin header and session cookie

   This is 4 HTTP calls with cookie/header juggling just to get a working login. For a single-user self-hosted instance this is absurd.

3. **`local_trusted` mode cannot bind to `0.0.0.0`** — so there is no "just works from external IP without auth" option either.

## Proposed Solution

### A. `onboard --yes --no-run` (or: `--yes` should NOT imply `--run`)

Let `--yes` only mean "accept defaults non-interactively." Starting the server should require explicit `--run` or `--yes --run`. This is the least-surprise behavior for automation scripts.

### B. `PAPERCLIP_ADMIN_EMAIL` + `PAPERCLIP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` environment variables

When these are set and the database has no admin user yet, `paperclipai run` (or `onboard`) should:
- Create the user
- Promote to instance admin
- Accept the bootstrap invite

All in one step, no HTTP calls needed. This is how every other self-hosted tool works (Gitea, Grafana, Minio, Portainer, etc.).

### C. Allow `local_trusted` with `bind=lan`

Or introduce a third mode like `local_password` that allows LAN bind with simple email/password auth but without the invite ceremony.

## Environment

- paperclipai v2026.517.0
- Headless Linux VPS, systemd service, cloud-init provisioning
payload.title: Support headless bootstrap: env-based admin credentials + onboard without auto-start

payload.body:
# Bug: `gemini_local` adapter does not clear stale session ID after successful fallback — causes permanent per-heartbeat failure loop

## Environment

- `paperclipai` 2026.513.0 / 2026.517.0, `@paperclipai/adapter-gemini-local`
- Adapter type: `gemini_local`
- Reproduced on macOS (arm64), Gemini CLI installed globally
- Any agent with a heartbeat interval long enough for Gemini CLI to expire its local session files (typically > ~24–48 h)

## Summary

The `gemini_local` adapter correctly detects when a stored session ID is no longer valid and retries the run with a fresh session (`runAttempt(null)`). However, after the retry succeeds, the **stale session ID is not cleared from `agent_runtime_state`**. On every subsequent heartbeat, the adapter loads the same invalid ID, fails on the first attempt, falls back, and succeeds — but the root cause is never resolved. The agent is degraded permanently until an operator manually clears the session ID from the database.

## How Gemini CLI session expiry works

The Gemini CLI stores session files in `~/.gemini/tmp/<dir>/chats/` as `.jsonl` files. These files have a finite retention window and are cleaned up automatically by the CLI. If an agent's heartbeat interval is long (e.g. 1 hour), or if the agent was paused/errored for a period, its session file will be gone by the time the next heartbeat fires.

This is **expected behavior** from the Gemini CLI. The bug is entirely on the Paperclip side — it does not update its persisted state to reflect that the session is gone.

## Code path

**File:** `@paperclipai/adapter-gemini-local/dist/server/execute.js`

The adapter has correct detection and fallback logic:

```js
const initial = await runAttempt(sessionId);
if (
  sessionId &&
  !initial.proc.timedOut &&
  (initial.proc.exitCode ?? 0) !== 0 &&
  isGeminiUnknownSessionError(initial.proc.stdout, initial.proc.stderr)
) {
  await onLog("stdout", `[paperclip] Gemini resume session "${sessionId}" is unavailable; retrying with a fresh session.\n`);
  const retry = await runAttempt(null);   // ← starts fresh, works
  return toResult(retry, true, true);     // ← returns result
}
```

The retry run produces a new `sessionId` in its output. However, `toResult(retry, true, true)` returns the new session ID in the result payload, and **`agent_runtime_state.session_id` is never updated to the new value nor cleared to NULL**. The next heartbeat reads the same stale ID and the cycle repeats.

## Reproduction

1. Create a `gemini_local` agent with a heartbeat interval ≥ 1 hour (or simply pause it for 24+ hours).
2. Let the Gemini CLI expire the agent's session file.
3. Resume normal heartbeats.
4. Observe: every single heartbeat run begins with:
   ```
   Error resuming session: Invalid session identifier "<uuid>".
   Searched for sessions in ~/.gemini/tmp/<dir>/chats.
   ```
   followed by a successful fallback — but the same error appears on the next heartbeat too.
5. Confirm in `agent_runtime_state`: `session_id` still holds the original stale UUID, `last_error` still reflects the session error, `last_run_status = 'failed'` — even though runs are technically completing via the fallback path.

## Impact

- **Every heartbeat wastes one failed Gemini CLI invocation** before the fallback fires. For a 5-minute heartbeat, this doubles the number of Gemini processes spawned over time.
- **`last_run_status` stays `'failed'`** in `agent_runtime_state` even when the agent completes work successfully via fallback, making monitoring unreliable.
- **Secondary effects from prolonged degradation:** an agent that repeatedly sees its own runs as "failed" may attempt self-repair actions. In our case, a CEO-role agent (`gemini_local`) that was stuck in this loop for several hours created a duplicate CTO agent as an autonomous recovery attempt, requiring manual cleanup.
- Operators have no indication this is happening unless they inspect raw run logs — the UI shows the agent as `running` with no visible error.

## Sugge
payload.title: Bug: gemini_local adapter does not clear stale session ID after successful fallback — causes permanent per-heartbeat failure loop

# Community plugin: opencalw_adapter_for_paperclip — Paperclip ↔ OpenClaw bridge

(Draft of the issue I'll open on `paperclipai/paperclip` once the user okays the GitHub push.)

---

**Title:** Community plugin — opencalw_adapter_for_paperclip (Paperclip ↔ OpenClaw bridge)

**Body:**

Hi Paperclip team & community,

I've published a community plugin that bridges Paperclip with an OpenClaw Gateway end-to-end, so issues assigned in Paperclip flow into OpenClaw agents, get processed by Claude, and come back as comments + status changes.

**Repo:** https://github.com/NazmulGit/paperclip-openclaw-adapter

**License:** MIT

### What it does

- **Bidirectional agent sync** — OpenClaw agents mirror into Paperclip companies as managed agents (8 slots); Paperclip agents with `adapterType: openclaw_gateway` export to OpenClaw via `agents.create`.
- **Per-agent PC API key bootstrap** — one click in the settings panel mints a Paperclip API key per bridged agent and inlines it into wake messages, so OC agents can call back into Paperclip's API to comment, close issues, etc. Solves the 403 problem where shared tokens couldn't act as the assigned agent.
- **Polished settings UI** — collapsible sections with a status pills strip (Gateway / Token / Bindings); inline editor for `openclawUrl` + `openclawToken` (the auto-config form is hidden when a custom settingsPage exists, so we render it ourselves).
- **Continuous health/sync** — 25 s WS keepalive, exponential-backoff reconnect, `*/5 min` full sync, `*/1 min` health check.
- **Auto-fill `adapterConfig`** — agents created via Paperclip's New Agent → OpenClaw Gateway picker get the URL + token patched in on the next sync.

### Real-world verification

Heavy stress test (this repo's `Others/scripts/stress-tasks.json`):

10 parallel real-world tasks across 3 bridged agents — read company info via PC API, list open issues, compute Fibonacci(15), write Python code, list local files via shell, fetch example.com and extract `<title>`, prime check, explain SQL injection. **10/10 passed in 5 min wall-clock.** Not marker echo — actual cognitive work.

### Where it lives

- PC plugin (this repo): `opencalw_adapter_for_paperclip` — installed into `~/.paperclip/plugins/`
- OC plugin scaffold: `paperclip_adapter_for_opencalw` — adds a typed `paperclip.*` tool inside OpenClaw. V2 work.

### Known V1 limitations (documented in the repo)

- Managed-slot display names are static (no `agents.update` SDK in 2026.517.0); slots show as "OpenClaw Agent N". OC-name ↔ slot mapping is in the sync table.
- `tsc` alone isn't enough — `esbuild` is required to bundle the UI's bare specifiers.
- One PC company binds to one OC gateway at a time.
- When a company has no active `role=ceo` agent, the bridge auto-creates a "Bridge Bootstrap CEO" because PC's join approval gate requires one. Operators can rename or replace it.

### What I'd like feedback on

1. **`agents.update` SDK method** — would unlock per-instance display names for managed slots. Is this on the roadmap?
2. **Auto-config form when a custom settingsPage is present** — could the host render BOTH the auto-form (for instance config like URL/token) AND the custom panel? Right now custom panels have to re-implement config editing.
3. **Plugin showcase / community registry** — is there a place to list community plugins beyond the GitHub repo?

Happy to incorporate any conventions you'd like (capability tweaks, naming, etc.) before I cut a v1.0 release tag.

Thanks for shipping Paperclip — great primitives to build on.

— @NazmulGit

payload.body:
## Summary

The **stable** `paperclipai@2026.517.0` / `@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway@2026.517.0` sends a top-level `paperclip` property in agent params that the OpenClaw gateway v2026.5.20+ rejects under protocol 4 (`additionalProperties:false` schema).

Every agent dispatch fails with:
```
openclaw_gateway_request_failed: invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'
```

A local hotpatch was applied to `2026.522.0-canary.5` on this installation, but a fresh `npm install paperclipai` (which pulls stable `2026.517.0`) regresses every agent.

---

## Exact Diff Between Stable and Hotpatch

**`packages/adapters/openclaw-gateway/src/server/execute.ts`** (approximate, derived from published dist):

```diff
-const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3;
+const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4;

 // Inside the agent dispatch path:
 const agentParams = {
   ...payloadTemplate,
   message,
   sessionKey,
   idempotencyKey: ctx.runId,
 };
 delete agentParams.text;
-agentParams.paperclip = paperclipPayload;
+// paperclip field removed: protocol 4 schema uses additionalProperties:false and no longer accepts 'paperclip'.
+// Paperclip context is carried in the message text via buildWakeText().
```

The `paperclipPayload` object (containing `runId`, `companyId`, `agentId`, `agentName`, `taskId`, `issueId`, `wakeReason`, etc.) was previously sent as a top-level `paperclip` property in the gateway WebSocket agent request. Protocol 4 tightened the schema to `additionalProperties:false`, making this field an error.

---

## Root Cause

OpenClaw gateway bumped its agent-params JSON schema to protocol 4, adding `additionalProperties:false` at the root. The stable adapter still sends `minProtocol: 3` / `maxProtocol: 3` and the `paperclip` field that protocol 4 rejects.

Two changes are needed together:
1. Bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION` constant from `3` → `4`
2. Remove `agentParams.paperclip = paperclipPayload` (the Paperclip wake context is already carried in the message text via `buildWakeText()` — no data is lost)

---

## Repro

```bash
# Clean install — gets stable 2026.517.0
npm install -g paperclipai

# Create a smoke-test ticket and trigger a dispatch
# Expect: openclaw_gateway_request_failed: invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'
```

Verified on: OpenClaw gateway v2026.5.20+, protocol 4.

---

## Evidence (live trace from OME-408 smoke test)

Tracked internally as OME-407 (hotpatch) + OME-409 (this upstream report). Three failed dispatches before hotpatch:
- Run `07d04a4c`: `protocol mismatch` (minProtocol 3, gateway required 4)
- Run `223e3d45`: `gateway token mismatch` (secondary auth issue, unrelated)
- Run `f0018b06`: `invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'` (the field rejection)

After hotpatch applied to canary install: dispatch succeeded (OME-408 smoke test passed, run `fdca57c5`).

---

## Fix Status

- ✅ Fix is **already in canary**: `@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway@2026.522.0-canary.5` through `2026.523.0-canary.1`
- ❌ Fix is **NOT in stable**: `2026.517.0` is the current `latest` tag and still broken

**Request:** promote the fix to the stable channel (or cut `2026.524.0` / `2026.523.0` stable release) so `npm install paperclipai` gets a working adapter.

---

## Gate for this issue

`paperclipai@latest` on npm ships an `adapter-openclaw-gateway` with `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4` and no `paperclip` field in agent params, verified by a clean-install smoke test dispatching without `protocol mismatch` or `unexpected property` errors.
payload.title: adapter-openclaw-gateway: stable 2026.517.0 sends `paperclip` field rejected by protocol-4 gateway (additionalProperties:false)

## Package / version
`@paperclipai/server 2026.428.0` — routine-firing / recovery subsystem (issue origin kind `routine_execution`; stranded-assigned-issue and continuation-needed recovery classifiers; successful-run handoff checker; run-finalization enforcement).

## Observed behavior
The platform has no single, authoritative lifecycle model for an issue created by a recurring routine firing. The same issue is treated simultaneously as two incompatible things:

- a **completed execution artifact** — the firing itself finished, so run-finalization expects a terminal disposition (`done`); and
- a **persistent monitoring object** — future routine firings still own the unresolved monitoring objective, so a terminal disposition looks premature.

Concrete contradictions between subsystems:
- `in_progress` semantics vs. `continuation_needed` recovery — triggers continuation recovery.
- `stranded_assigned_issue` recovery — an assigned non-terminal routine issue with no active run is flagged as stranded.
- successful-run handoff checker — a successful run exiting `in_progress` is classified as `successful_run_missing_state` / `missing_disposition`, re-firing a recovery wake.
- `issue_commented` wakes — per-firing comments wake the assignee against otherwise-healthy state.

**Reproduction evidence A:** Repeated self-wake loops, repeated recovery triggers, `blocked` ↔ `in_progress` ↔ `done` status oscillation, comment-echo cascades.

**Reproduction evidence B (2026-05-18 ~06:05–06:12 UTC, routine `428ef4bd` "Daily Paper-Trading Monitoring Report"):**
- **9** `successful_run_missing_state` / `missing_disposition: clear_next_step` recovery attempts firing **~every 60s**, burning ~6 heartbeats.
- Mechanism confirmed: each successful run exited early with `"issue already in_progress, exiting"`, leaving the issue `in_progress`. The successful-run handoff checker treats this as a missing disposition and re-fires the recovery wake.
- The loop only broke when an agent manually marked the firing `done`.

## Root cause
The harness does not recognize "future scheduled routine firings" as a valid live continuation path for an `in_progress` per-firing issue. Every disposition is wrong in some subsystem: `in_progress` → stranded recovery; `blocked` → invalid semantics; `done` → conflicts with the unresolved monitoring objective.

## Expected behavior
The platform must commit to **one** explicit lifecycle model for `routine_execution` issues:

**Model A — Per-firing terminal model.** Each routine firing dispositions `done` when that firing completes. The next routine execution creates a fresh issue. Recommended for short-cadence routines.

**Model B — Persistent monitor model.** Future scheduled firings suppress `stranded_assigned_issue`, `continuation_needed`, and `successful_run_missing_state` recovery. The issue is not expected to reach a terminal status while the routine is active.

Either is acceptable; mixing them is not.

## Suggested fix
1. Pick a model. Recommended: **Model A** for short-cadence routines (clean run-finalization alignment).
2. **Make the chosen model automatic.** For `originKind = routine_execution`, either:
   - (Model A) have the successful-run handoff checker treat `in_progress` with no queued continuation as an implicit `done` for that firing; or
   - have the routine scheduler auto-close the prior firing's issue when it spawns the next firing.
3. If Model B is adopted: teach the recovery classifiers to treat an issue whose parent routine has a future `nextRunAt` as having a live continuation path.
4. Tag `routine_execution`-origin issues so run-finalization enforcement applies the model-appropriate disposition rule.

Related: #6598, #6599, #6600.
payload.title: server: routine_execution issues have no stable lifecycle — recurring firings collide with stranded/continuation recovery and run-finalization

## Package / version
`paperclipai 2026.428.0` — `services/productivity-review.js:367` (comment authorship) + Board UI comment renderer

## Observed behavior
Productivity-review refresh comments are inserted with no author attribution:

```
authorAgentId:  null
authorUserId:   null
createdByRunId: null
body:           "Productivity review evidence refreshed..."
```

The `addComment` call passes an empty options object `{}`, so the row is stored without any author field.

In the Board UI, these `null / null / null` rows render with the byline **"You"** instead of a service identity (`"System"` / `"Productivity Review"` / `"paperclipai"`). The fallback appears to be: when both `authorAgentId` and `authorUserId` are null, display the current viewer's identity.

**Reproduction evidence (2026-05-09):** ~50 null-author comments in an issue all rendered as `"You"` for the Board user. The Board reasonably concluded the noise was originating from their own session.

**Compounding effect:** Agent-authored blocked-status comments posted via run context also misattribute to `local-board`, causing spurious `issue_commented` heartbeat wakes on the commenting agent itself.

## Expected behavior
When `authorAgentId` is null **and** `authorUserId` is null, do not fall back to the current viewer. Render as a neutral service label: `"System"`, `"Productivity Review"`, or `"paperclipai"`. Consider adding a `kind: "system"` or `serviceLabel` field to the comment API so callers can opt in to explicit service attribution.

## Side effect
The misattribution actively misleads the Board about the source of comment noise. In a multi-agent deployment where the Board identity is shared across sessions, this erodes governance trust in the issue thread.

## Suggested fix
1. **Short-term (UI):** In the comment renderer, when both author fields are null, render `"System"` or `"paperclipai service"` rather than falling back to the current viewer.
2. **Long-term (API + service):** Add a `serviceLabel` or `kind: "system"` field to the `addComment` options. Update `productivity-review.js` to pass `{ serviceLabel: 'Productivity Review' }` so the row carries explicit attribution at write time.

Related: see also #6598 (productivity-review tick-rate issue).
payload.title: board UI: null-author comments fall back to current viewer identity ("You") instead of a service label

## Package / version
`paperclipai 2026.428.0` — `services/productivity-review.js`

## Observed behavior
When a productivity review is active, the service emits a `"Productivity review evidence refreshed."` comment on every scheduler tick (~30 seconds) regardless of whether any evidence field has changed.

**Reproduction evidence (2026-05-09, local deployment):**
- An issue received ~50 such comments over ~29 minutes at a steady ~30-second cadence.
- Across the entire window, no material state delta was observed: `No-comment streak`, `Runs/comments in 1h/6h`, `Trigger`, and `Reasons` were unchanged. Only the elapsed-minute counter incremented.
- Callsite: `productivity-review.js:367` — `await issuesSvc.addComment(existing.id, buildRefreshComment(evidence, opts.prefix), {})`
- Comment template head (line 354): `"Productivity review evidence refreshed."`

## Expected behavior
Emit the refresh comment only when at least one material evidence field changes value (delta-gate before `addComment`).

## Side effect
Each emission triggers an `issue_commented` heartbeat wake for the assignee agent. On a quiet, healthy issue this consumes agent run budget without any actionable change.

## Suggested fix
Before calling `addComment`, compare the current `evidence` snapshot against the previously-emitted snapshot. Only emit when the diff is non-empty on fields other than elapsed-time counters.

payload.body:
## Environment

- `paperclipai` 2026.513.0, macOS (arm64)
- Embedded PostgreSQL (via `@embedded-postgres/darwin-arm64`)
- Single instance (`instances/default`, port 54329)

## Summary

After a crash or reboot, `instances/default/db/postmaster.pid` may reference a **PID that the OS has recycled to an unrelated process**. Paperclip's startup check sees "a process with that PID exists" and logs:

```
Embedded PostgreSQL already running; reusing existing process (pid=XXXX, port=54329)
```

It does **not** start a fresh Postgres. The server then fails with:

```
connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:54329
```

## Observed case

After a reboot, macOS recycled the old Postgres PID to a Chrome Helper process. Paperclip read `postmaster.pid`, called `process.kill(pid, 0)` (or equivalent), got no error (the Chrome process exists), concluded Postgres was running, and skipped spawning — resulting in ECONNREFUSED on every DB operation.

`postmaster.pid` line 4 contains the port (54329); the file is only cleaned up on a clean Postgres shutdown, not on crash/reboot.

## Root cause

The liveness check verifies **PID existence** but not:
- That the process is actually a `postgres` / `postmaster` binary
- That port 54329 is actually listening

## Suggested fix

Before concluding the embedded Postgres is already running, verify at least one of:
1. The process at the recorded PID has a name matching `postgres` / `postmaster`
2. Port 54329 is actually listening (`pg_isready -p 54329` or a TCP connect probe)

If either check fails, treat `postmaster.pid` as stale: move/delete it and start a fresh Postgres instance. The data directory is safe to keep — only the lock file is stale.

## Workaround today

```bash
# Confirm nothing is actually on port 54329
lsof -nP -iTCP:54329 -sTCP:LISTEN

# If empty, move the stale lock and restart Paperclip
mv ~/.paperclip/instances/default/db/postmaster.pid \
   ~/.paperclip/instances/default/db/postmaster.pid.stale-bak
# then: paperclipai run
```

> Note: this is a separate issue from the heartbeat recovery storm (#6596) — different fix surface, included here so it doesn't get buried in that report.
payload.title: Bug: embedded Postgres liveness check trusts postmaster.pid PID without verifying it's actually Postgres — causes ECONNREFUSED on reboot

payload.body:
## Environment

- `paperclipai` **2026.513.0**, package `@paperclipai/server` (global Homebrew install)
- Embedded PostgreSQL, single instance (`instances/default`)
- Heartbeat scheduler enabled (default; `HEARTBEAT_SCHEDULER_ENABLED !== "false"`)
- Reproduced organically during real internet outages (including unattended/overnight)

## Summary

When the host loses outbound internet (so adapter/LLM API calls fail or hang), the heartbeat **recovery pipeline** keeps running on its normal 30 s cadence and interprets the resulting symptoms as "agents are stuck and need review." It then **creates auto-assigned review issues and wakes agents to work them** — which themselves cannot reach the network, so they produce the same symptoms, which spawn more review work. The result is thousands of issues (predominantly titled **`Review silent active run for <agent>`**) and a large amount of wasted token spend, with zero useful output, until connectivity returns or the operator intervenes.

There are **two distinct recovery mechanisms** with the same blind spot.

## Where the pipeline runs

`packages/.../@paperclipai/server/dist/index.js`, gated by `config.heartbeatSchedulerEnabled`:

- **At startup**: a `.then` chain runs `reapOrphanedRuns → promoteDueScheduledRetries → resumeQueuedRuns → reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues → reconcileIssueGraphLiveness → scanSilentActiveRuns → reconcileProductivityReviews`
- **Periodically**: the same chain inside `setInterval(..., config.heartbeatSchedulerIntervalMs)`

Cadence: default every 30 s (floor 10 s via `HEARTBEAT_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS`).

**None of the steps in this chain performs any connectivity / API-reachability check.**

---

## Mechanism 1 — "Review silent active run" watchdog

**Code:** `dist/services/recovery/service.js`

Thresholds are **hardcoded** (service.js:24–26):
- `ACTIVE_RUN_OUTPUT_SUSPICION_THRESHOLD_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000` (1 h)
- `ACTIVE_RUN_OUTPUT_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD_MS = 4 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (4 h)

`scanSilentActiveRuns()` selects `heartbeatRuns` where `status = 'running'` and last output ≤ now − 1h, then for each calls `createOrUpdateStaleRunEvaluation()` (creates issue + **`enqueueWakeup`**).

De-duplication is **per run id** only — it does not prevent amplification when recovery runs themselves go silent.

### Why this explodes during an outage

1. Internet drops. Every active run stops emitting output. After 1 h each becomes a "silent active run."
2. `scanSilentActiveRuns` creates one review issue per distinct silent run and `enqueueWakeup`s an owner agent for each.
3. Those review runs **also have no internet**. They start, fail/hang → after 1 h each review run is a **new `running` row with a new run id** → satisfies the watchdog query → new issue + `enqueueWakeup`.
4. `resumeQueuedRuns` / `promoteDueScheduledRetries` keep re-launching queued/retry runs that immediately fail offline, each becoming another silent-run candidate.

**The population of runs grows without bound** because recovery runs are watched the same way as regular runs. No global offline gate, no cap on total open evaluations.

---

## Mechanism 2 — "productivity review"

**Code:** `dist/services/productivity-review.js`, `reconcileProductivityReviews()`

Same connectivity blind spot, same create-issue + `enqueueWakeup` pattern, but **built-in caps** (3 per issue per 24 h). This mechanism adds noise and wasted tokens but is **not** self-amplifying. It is bounded; Mechanism 1 is not.

During an outage: `long_active_duration` (≥ 6 h) and `no_comment_streak` (≥ 10 consecutive failed runs) both trip for offline agents.

---

## Shared root cause

The recovery pipeline cannot distinguish **"agent is genuinely stuck" (needs review)** from **"host has no connectivity" (review is pointless and harmful)**. Output-silence and long-active-duration are treated as agent-behavior signals; during an outage they are infrastructure signals. The remedy (spawn more agent runs) is exactly the wrong action when the cause is no netw
payload.title: Bug: heartbeat recovery has no connectivity awareness — network outages cause a self-amplifying storm of paid review runs
