payload.body:
## Summary

Add a way for a designated budget-enforcer agent inside a Paperclip company to PATCH `/api/agents/{id}` (specifically `status` and, eventually, a writable `pauseReason`) on other agents in the same company. Today the only API actors allowed to modify another agent are (a) the company's `local-board` / CEO user, or (b) the agent that originally created the target (`createdByAgentId == requesting agent`). For board-/CEO-created agents (which is most of them in practice — `createdByAgentId=null`), this means no agent in the tenant can run scheduled budget enforcement, even with explicit board authorisation.

This is the API-auth follow-up to #6516 (missing enforcement engine). #6516 covers the platform-side gap (no comparison, no `pauseReason` writer, no dispatcher gate). This RFE covers the side-channel gap: even a tenant-built enforcer agent can't actually pause over-budget agents on schedule, because the platform's modify-agent permission excludes it.

## Concrete failure

Under board approval `bca4244c-a37a-4f29-81a1-940dfa9d866e` (Blemy company, May 23 2026, `paperclipai` v`2026.517.0`, bundle SHA-256 `405b9ac56431c3bb704525142a36f3309ba4289a961840acf2ff2e300c6100a9`), a tenant-built budget enforcer (`scripts/shared/budget_enforcer.py`, called from a routine assigned to the CTO Agent) attempted to pause four over-budget agents.

All four PATCHes failed with the same stable error:

```
PATCH /api/agents/{id}  HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <CTO-Agent run JWT>
Content-Type: application/json

{"status": "paused"}

-> 403 Forbidden
{"error": "Only CEO or agent creators can modify other agents"}
```

| Agent (anonymised) | Util% | Spent / Cap (cents) | `createdByAgentId` | `createdByUserId` | PATCH result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue Sub-Agent | 181.8% | 909 / 500 | `null` | `null` | 403 |
| CFO Agent         | 183.3% | 2750 / 1500 | `null` | `null` | 403 |
| Expense Sub-Agent | 305.3% | 916 / 300 | `null` | `null` | 403 |
| Reporting Sub-Agent | 407.7% | 1223 / 300 | `null` | `null` | 403 |

All four were created by `local-board` (board-spawned, no agent creator). The enforcer agent is the CTO Agent (the only agent the routines API allows the routine creator to self-assign). Neither condition in the rule (`creator is local-board user` OR `createdByAgentId == caller`) is satisfied, so every PATCH is rejected.

After the failure the routine was reverted to `BUDGET_ENFORCER_DRY_RUN=1` so it does not produce 403 noise on every 15-minute fire. The auto-pause-at-100% guardrail documented in the tenant's `AGENTS.md` is therefore documentation-only as long as this gap exists.

## Why it matters

- Every tenant that wires the documented "budget hard-stops at 100%" guardrail today must either (a) accept that it does not enforce, or (b) wake a human (CEO / board user) on every cycle to manually pause over-budget agents. Both are pre-paperclipai-on-its-own-merits failures of the platform's documented contract.
- Tenants cannot self-host an enforcer that runs unattended on a routine, because the only agent identity the routines API will accept as `assigneeAgentId` is the routine's creator — which is never the company's `local-board` user.
- This currently blocks live mode of a tested, board-approved enforcer (smoke 6/6 green, parity-checked over three dry-run fires) on the Blemy company.

## Acceptable shapes

The maintainers can pick the design; both are acceptable from the requester side. Either one unblocks the tenant.

### Option (a) — extend `createdByAgentId` semantics

Treat a designated enforcer agent as if it had `createdByAgentId` over agents whose `createdByAgentId IS NULL` and `createdByUserId IS NULL` in the same company. Concretely: when the platform evaluates the modify-agent permission, also accept the caller if the company has a `designated_enforcer_agent_id` company setting and the caller matches it AND the target agent has `createdByAgentId IS NULL AND createdByUserId IS NULL`.

Pros: minimal new surfa
payload.title: RFE: allow a designated budget-enforcer agent to PATCH /api/agents/:id (currently only CEO / creator can modify other agents)

payload.author: Lattimius
payload.body:
## Summary

Local child-process heartbeat runs have two lifecycle gaps:

1. Critical silent-run detection creates/elevates review work but does not terminate the still-running OS process, so a stalled local adapter can leave an orphaned child process alive after DB bookkeeping is recovered.
2. A heartbeat run that has already been claimed can reach `executeRun` after an agent is paused; `executeRun` can then flip the agent back to `running` and invoke the adapter because there is no final status guard immediately before adapter invocation.

## Evidence from local instance

- `scanSilentActiveRuns` selects quiet `running` runs and creates/elevates evaluation work but does not call the run cancellation/process termination path.
- The critical source-issue block explicitly says it blocks the source issue without cancelling the active process.
- `cancelRunInternal` and `cancelActiveForAgent` already know how to terminate by persisted pid/processGroupId, but the silent-run watchdog does not call that primitive.
- `executeRun` accepts a queued/running run, claims it, loads the agent once, then later writes `agents.status = 'running'` and calls `adapter.execute` without re-reading the current agent/run state immediately before invocation.
- Generic `PATCH /agents/:id` can set `status: paused` through the normal update route without routing through the pause endpoint that calls `cancelActiveForAgent`.

## Proposed fix

- For critical output silence on tracked local child-process adapters, terminate the persisted pid/processGroupId through the same safe path used by run cancellation, mark the run with an explicit `silent_run_terminated` failure/cancel code, then create/attach the audit evaluation issue.
- Add a final execution guard before `agents.status = 'running'` and `adapter.execute`: re-read the run and agent; if the agent is paused/terminated/pending approval or the run is no longer running, abort/release cleanly and do not invoke the adapter.
- Make generic status transitions to `paused` either rejected or routed through the same cancellation semantics as `POST /agents/:id/pause`.
- Add regression tests for critical silent-run termination and pause-after-claim-before-adapter.

## Local provenance

This issue was filed before a board-approved local patch on a private Paperclip instance for CRO-5293. The local patch should be removed/restamped once the upstream fix lands.
payload.title: Heartbeat local child runs can leak processes and bypass paused agents

payload.author: aperim-agent
payload.body:
## Context

We're heavy consumers of the `claude_local` adapter with a fleet of agents that aggregate MCP servers from many vendors. Several of our agents have crossed Anthropic's 300-tool managed payload ceiling (most recent failure: 307 tools, returning a transient upstream / `exit 143` to the agent runtime).

Anthropic recently shipped two mechanisms that, together, address this cleanly:

1. **`defer_loading: true`** — a per-MCP-server flag that hides tools from the upfront tool list until the model explicitly searches for them.
2. **The Tool Search Tool** (currently `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119`) — a built-in tool the model uses to discover and hydrate deferred tools on demand.

We'd like the `claude_local` adapter to plumb both of these through, plus expose a small amount of config so consumers can curate their own tool catalogues per agent.

## The three asks

1. **`defer_loading: true` passthrough** on individual MCP tools and/or whole MCP servers via `.mcp.json` (or whatever the adapter's equivalent server descriptor is).
2. **Anthropic Tool Search Tool injection** by the adapter when `defer_loading` is in use, with version pinned in adapter code.
3. **Adapter config knobs** (per-agent / per-server / per-tool) that let consumers express a 3-tier partition policy (small always-upfront tier, deferred tier, per-agent overrides), without forking the adapter.

We've written this up internally as an ADR; the engineering design questions in §8 are reproduced verbatim below so the implementation discussion can happen in one place.

---

## §8 Design Questions

### Q1 — Tool-list assembly point

Where in the `claude_local` adapter is the final tool list assembled for each Anthropic API request?

Specifically:
- Which module composes the array sent in the `tools` parameter?
- At what point are MCP server tools merged with built-in Claude Code tools and per-agent skill tools?
- Is there a single chokepoint where the partition logic should slot in, or is the list built in multiple passes?

We need this so the platform team can scope the change precisely.

### Q2 — MCP server metadata schema

What schema does the adapter use today for MCP server descriptors in `.mcp.json` (and in the in-memory representation)?

We propose extending it as follows:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "plane": {
      "command": "...",
      "args": ["..."],
      "defer_loading_default": true,         // NEW: server-wide default
      "defer_loading_overrides": {           // NEW: per-tool override
        "list_work_items": false,
        "list_cycles": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If the adapter accepts this schema (with sensible defaults — `defer_loading_default: false` for backward compatibility), consumers can curate their own catalogues without code changes.

### Q3 — Per-agent override mechanism

Where is the right place for per-agent `promote` / `demote` overrides to live? Candidates:

a. A new field on the agent's existing `assigneeAdapterOverrides` (if such a thing exists).
b. A new file alongside `AGENTS.md` (e.g. `TOOLS_OVERRIDE.yaml`).
c. A field on the agent record in the agent registry.

We have a mild preference for (b) — file-based, agent-owner-managed, version-controlled. But the platform team owns this call; whichever fits the adapter's existing config story.

### Q4 — Feature-flag interface

What is the feature-flag mechanism in `claude_local`?

Specifically:
- Is there an existing per-agent / per-company / global flag system we can hook into?
- If not, we propose env-var + per-agent config-file overlay, with the precedence order documented in our ADR §7.2.

### Q5 — Tool Search Tool version pinning

The Tool Search Tool is versioned (`tool_search_tool_regex_20251119`). How should the adapter handle version pinning?

a. Pin the version in adapter code, bump in a release.
b. Make it a config knob per company / per agent.
c. Always send the latest version Anthropic publishes.

We recommend (a) — pin in adapter code, bump via nor

Problem:
Routines (/api/routines) cannot embed an executionPolicy template. When a routine spawns an issue, that issue is born with executionPolicy: null and executionState: null. The downstream assignee agent has no formal Stage 1 → Stage 2 routing to follow, and the human board user sees no structured handoff.

Workarounds tried, none viable:
Stamp at triage from the assignee agent. Wake-on-create doesn't reliably fire for routine-spawned issues. In my company, issue sat in_review with the routine assignee, role-based triage never reassigned).

Stamp from a reviewer agent via PATCH on the routine. Blocked by 403: Agents can only manage routines assigned to themselves. And there's no field to PATCH anyway.

Stamp from the assignee agent post-hoc. Per existing semantics, stamping executionPolicy after a transition to in_review is a no-op for activation; recovery requires PATCH executionPolicy: null and a fresh in_review transition, which loses the implementer's checkpoint.

Proposed fix:
Add issueTemplate.executionPolicy (JSONB, nullable) to the routine schema. Reachable via GET/PATCH /api/routines/{id}.
At spawn time, the routine engine copies that template verbatim into the new issue's executionPolicy field before the assignee agent's first heartbeat fires.

Control-plane UI gets a routine-editor surface for this field. Validation matches existing executionPolicy validation on issues (so the spec doesn't drift between contexts).

Auth: keep the existing routine-PATCH constraint (only the routine's assignee agent can PATCH), but allow human users to PATCH any routine in their company — humans are the realistic editors here.

Acceptance:
GET /api/routines/{id} returns issueTemplate.executionPolicy (null or object).
PATCH /api/routines/{id} with {"issueTemplate":{"executionPolicy":{...}}} succeeds for human users in the routine's company, and for the routine's assignee agent.
Next scheduled spawn from a routine with a populated template produces an issue with executionPolicy set at creation time.
Transitioning that spawned issue to in_review activates executionState.currentParticipant per the template.
Routines with issueTemplate.executionPolicy: null continue to spawn issues with null policy (no regression).

Evidence:
Four routine spawns affected on a single routine over ~2 weeks. The workaround instructions baked into the agent's memory (feedback_paperclip_policy_stamping) cannot close this gap from the agent side — the platform needs to own it.

Concrete example:
Content-run routine, the template should be:

{
  "mode": "normal",
  "commentRequired": true,
  "stages": [{
    "type": "review",
    "approvalsNeeded": 1,
    "participants": [{ "type": "agent", "agentId": "fd2bc8e2-ce10-4e52-a0da-3d79dede0e7a" }]
  }]
}
payload.title: Routines should carry an executionPolicy template that's copied into spawned issues at creation

## Environment

- paperclipai: `2026.512.0` (stable; reproduces on this version, not yet tested on 2026.517.0 — no relevant changelog entry between them)
- Node: `v25.9.0` (Homebrew on macOS arm64)
- Database: embedded PostgreSQL (default config, `embedded-postgres` mode on `127.0.0.1:54329`)
- Deployment: `local_trusted`, single instance, default data dir

## Symptom

After ~24h of stable operation, paperclip dies during its hourly auto-backup with:

```
[Error: A FileHandle object was closed during garbage collection. This used
to be allowed with a deprecation warning but is now considered an error.
Please close FileHandle objects explicitly. File descriptor: 27
(/Users/.../data/backups/paperclip-20260522-063753.sql)] {
  code: 'ERR_INVALID_STATE'
}

Node.js v25.9.0
```

Two observed occurrences in our deployment, both during the timer-fired
backup (24 hours apart). Captured filenames:
`paperclip-20260521-143649.sql`, `paperclip-20260522-063753.sql`.

## Impact

When node dies mid-backup, the embedded postgres is left without its
parent's stdio/signaling. The launch wrapper's stale-pidfile sweep then
removes `postmaster.pid` on next launch — but the postgres process itself
is gone. Paperclip restarts, binds `:3100`, but every query fails with
`connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:54329`. The server returns HTTP 500 to every
request silently until manual intervention (`launchctl kickstart`).

## Root cause hypothesis

Node 25 promoted "FileHandle closed by GC" from a deprecation warning to a
fatal error (`ERR_INVALID_STATE`). The pg_dump backup pipeline in
`dist/index.js` (around the `await Promise.all([pipeline(child.stdout,
createGzip(), createWriteStream(opts.backupFile)), waitForChildExit(child,
pgDumpBin)])` block) appears to be leaking a `FileHandle` rather than
closing it explicitly — likely the writer side of `createWriteStream` when
the pipeline ends, or an intermediate handle opened via `fs.promises.open`.

Same code shape exists in `2026.517.0`, so a release upgrade alone does not
appear to address this.

## Workaround applied

`database.backup.enabled: false` in `config.json`. Manual
`paperclipai db:backup` invocations are unaffected (we ran several pre-upgrade
snapshots cleanly using the CLI); only the timer-fired backup leaks the FD.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the pg_dump write path so the FileHandle (or WriteStream's underlying
handle) is `await`-closed in a `finally` block, or use
`fs.promises.writeFile(...)`/explicit `await fh.close()` rather than letting
the stream be GC'd.

Happy to test patches against this environment.
payload.title: Hourly DB backup crashes node 25 with ERR_INVALID_STATE (FileHandle GC) — orphans embedded postgres

# Wake event delivery gap: agents assigned in initial POST don't reliably wake until @-mention

## Summary

When a new issue is created via POST `/api/companies/{companyId}/issues` with `assigneeAgentId` set in the initial payload, the assigned agent does NOT reliably wake. The issue appears in their inbox correctly, but no `issue_assigned` event seems to fire (or it fires and gets lost). An explicit @-mention comment posted afterward reliably triggers wake. Suggests POST-with-assignee path is missing the event-emission that PATCH-assignee path has.

## Environment

- Paperclip 2026.512.0
- `claude_local` adapter
- Both Tier 1 (Opus 4.7) and Tier 2 (Codex) agents affected — observed across Architect (Tier 1), CEO (Tier 1), Local Eng (Tier 2), Codex Eng (Tier 2)

## Reproduction

1. POST a new issue:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST .../api/companies/{companyId}/issues -d '{
     "title": "Test issue",
     "description": "...",
     "assigneeAgentId": "<agent-uuid>",
     "status": "todo",
     "priority": "high",
     "parentId": "<some-parent>"
   }'
   ```
2. Issue is created successfully. Response shows `assigneeAgentId` set, `status: todo`.
3. Wait 5-10 minutes.
4. Check agent's runs — no new run since the POST.
5. Post a comment on the new issue containing `@<AgentName>` mention.
6. Agent wakes within ~30-60 seconds of the comment and begins processing.

## Expected behavior

POST-with-assignee should trigger an `issue_assigned` event (or equivalent) that wakes the agent, identical to PATCHing assignee onto an existing issue.

## Actual behavior

- POST-with-assignee: no wake, agent silent until other trigger.
- PATCH-assignee (after the fact): wakes reliably (we've observed).
- Comment with @-mention: wakes reliably.

We observed this pattern today across 3 newly-created child issues (ADF-503/504/505), all assigned at create-time to Architect or CEO. All 3 sat silent for ~10 minutes after creation. Posted @-mention comments → all 3 woke within 1-2 minutes and completed work successfully in 5-8 minutes each.

## Impact

Anyone doing factory-style decomposition (CEO files multiple child issues, expects assignees to pick up automatically) will see their decomposed children sit idle until operator @-mentions each. Adds friction proportional to decomposition fan-out.

## Workaround we currently use

For every new POST that includes `assigneeAgentId`:
1. POST the issue.
2. Immediately POST a comment with `@<AgentName>` mention to trigger wake.

OR: 

1. POST the issue WITHOUT assignee (omit `assigneeAgentId`).
2. Immediately PATCH the issue with `assigneeAgentId`.

Both add an extra API call per issue. For batch decomposition (e.g. 6 child issues from a milestone parent), this becomes 6 extra calls.

## Speculation on root cause

Two paths that should produce the same event likely diverged:
- PATCH-assignee path: explicitly emits `issue_assigned` event on assignee change.
- POST-with-assignee path: may emit `issue_created` but not `issue_assigned` (assignee was "always" set, never changed from null).

If event subscribers only listen for `issue_assigned`, POST-with-assignee silently misses the wake.

## Notes

- Easy to verify: tail server logs during the POST vs PATCH paths and see which events are emitted.
- Related: status auto-transition gap (filed separately).
- Related: workspace inheritance gap (filed separately).
- Polite bug report from downstream user. Happy to test a fix if one lands.
payload.title: Wake event delivery gap: agents assigned in initial POST don't reliably wake until @-mention

# Issue `status` field doesn't auto-transition `blocked → todo` after `issue_blockers_resolved` event fires

## Summary

When an issue is `status: blocked` with all `blockedByIssueIds` referencing terminal (`done`/`cancelled`) issues, the `issue_blockers_resolved` event fires and the assignee may wake. But the issue's own `status` field remains `blocked` until the assignee (or operator) explicitly PATCHes it forward. Combined with the agent skill rule "skip blocked items in priority inbox", this often leaves resolved-blocker work parked in degenerate state requiring operator intervention.

## Environment

- Paperclip 2026.512.0
- `claude_local` adapter (Claude Code CLI)
- Bundled `paperclip` skill (Step 4 priority list)

## Reproduction

1. Issue A is `status: blocked`, `blockedByIssueIds: [B]`.
2. Issue B transitions to `status: done` (assignee PATCHes it as part of normal heartbeat completion).
3. Server-side: `issue_blockers_resolved` event fires for Issue A.
4. Issue A's assignee wakes (sometimes — see note below).
5. Agent's heartbeat runs Step 4 of the bundled `paperclip` skill: "priority: in_progress → in_review → todo. Skip blocked unless you can unblock."
6. Issue A's `status` field is still `blocked` — inbox check filters it out.
7. Agent processes other work (or exits if no other assignment), Issue A continues to sit in degenerate state: `status=blocked, blockedBy=[done]`.

## Expected behavior

Either:
- **(a)** Issue A's `status` auto-transitions `blocked → todo` server-side when `issue_blockers_resolved` event fires, so next inbox check picks it up.
- **(b)** Agent's wake-reason handling for `issue_blockers_resolved` explicitly bypasses the inbox priority filter and processes the resolved issue regardless of stale `status`.

Currently neither happens reliably; the gap requires manual intervention.

## Actual behavior

- Wake event fires (sometimes — we've observed it fire on at least one case, miss on another).
- When wake DOES fire, agent's heartbeat reads inbox-lite and filters out `blocked` items per skill Step 4.
- Resolved-blocker issue stays parked.

We have specific case: issue ADF-474 had blocker ADF-473 transition to `done` at 2026-05-21T13:09. ADF-474 sat in `blocked` state for ~24h until operator intervention. Verified via API that `blockedBy = [(ADF-473, done)]`, `status=blocked` throughout.

Re-test today (2026-05-22): operator flipped status `blocked → todo` manually via UI. This DOES wake assignee. Wake worked; the missing piece is the auto-flip.

## Impact

Operator must manually flip status `blocked → todo` (or post @-mention) for resolved-blocker issues whenever they don't naturally surface. We observed this pattern several times per day during active engagement work. Adds friction but doesn't block — agents respect blockers correctly, they just don't notice when blockers clear.

## Workaround we currently use

- Operator monitors blocked issues whose `blockedBy` items have all reached terminal status.
- For each: PATCH `status: todo` via UI (wakes assignee) OR post @-mention comment (also wakes).
- No agent-side workaround possible without changing the bundled `paperclip` skill (which is platform code we don't own).

## Speculation on root cause

The bundled `paperclip` skill Step 4 is correct as-written for the design intent — agents shouldn't pick up work that's actually blocked. The gap is that `status: blocked` is conflated with "actually blocked by something current" vs "historically blocked by something now resolved". Two clean fixes:

1. **Server-side auto-transition:** when last `blockedByIssueIds` item reaches terminal, server PATCHes `status: blocked → todo` and re-emits assignment notification.
2. **Skill clarification:** modify bundled `paperclip` Step 4 to check `blockedBy[].status` and treat "all-blockers-terminal + status=blocked" as actionable (priority equal to or above `todo`).

Option 1 is cleanest — single source of truth, no per-skill awareness needed.

## Notes

- Related:
payload.title: Issue status field doesn't auto-transition blocked → todo after issue_blockers_resolved event

# `inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId` not honored at runtime — agent's persisted workspace wins

## Summary

When creating a child issue with `inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId` pointing at a known-good parent workspace, the runtime appears to NOT route the assigned agent into that inherited workspace. The agent's persisted `executionWorkspace` from prior assignment is used instead. This breaks the cross-issue workspace continuity pattern that the field is designed to support.

## Environment

- Paperclip 2026.512.0 (self-hosted, single-instance)
- Adapter: `claude_local` (Claude Code CLI)
- Affected agent roles: tested on Local Eng, Codex Eng, Reviewer — all show same pattern
- macOS host (single operator setup, no multi-machine workspace sharing)

## Reproduction

1. Agent A is assigned issue ADF-100; their `executionWorkspace` is set to `/path/to/repo-A/` and they complete work there.
2. CEO creates new child issue ADF-101 via POST `/api/companies/{companyId}/issues` with payload including:
   ```json
   {
     "title": "...",
     "parentId": "<some-parent-uuid>",
     "assigneeAgentId": "<Agent-A-uuid>",
     "inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId": "<ADF-XXX-uuid where workspace = /path/to/repo-B/>",
     "...": "..."
   }
   ```
3. Agent A wakes on ADF-101 assignment (or after operator @-mention).
4. Agent A runs `pwd` as part of pre-implementation check — output is `/path/to/repo-A/` (the **previous** workspace), not `/path/to/repo-B/` (the inherited workspace).

## Expected behavior

Agent's runtime working directory matches the inherited workspace from `inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId` — or, at minimum, an explicit `executionWorkspace` is set on the issue server-side so the adapter can route to it.

## Actual behavior

- The `inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId` field is accepted by the API (no error), and visible on the issue record.
- Direct GET on the issue shows `executionWorkspaceId: null` despite the inheritance directive.
- Agent's runtime cwd reflects last persisted workspace, regardless of the field.

## Impact

Multi-repo engagements (or any work that crosses workspaces within one agent's assignment history) require operator intervention every time an agent gets a child issue in a different workspace. Specifically: we observed ~6 instances in one day where agents committed to wrong workspace OR blocked with workspace-mismatch comment, requiring operator to post explicit `cd /path/to/correct/repo` instruction via @-mention before agent could proceed.

When agents follow workspace-verification rules (we added explicit "FM11 pre-impl check" — `ls <brief-named-path>` before touching code), they correctly block instead of producing wrong-workspace code. But that's a defensive workaround for what `inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId` should solve.

## Workaround we currently use

- Every child issue brief explicitly names the working directory in the description ("Working directory: /full/path") AND names at least one file path the agent will edit (so they can `ls <path>` to verify they're in the right place).
- Agents have an explicit pre-implementation check rule in their `AGENTS.md`: run `pwd` + `ls <brief-named-path>` before any code change; if either fails, set issue to `blocked` with workspace-mismatch evidence.
- Operator manually posts `cd /correct/path` in an @-mention comment to wake agent and route their next heartbeat correctly.

This works but adds operator toil per cross-workspace assignment. The `inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId` field doing what its name implies would eliminate the workaround.

## Speculation on root cause

Two possibilities (we haven't traced the runtime):

1. The field is stored but not consumed by the agent-adapter spawning code — adapters use the agent's last `cwd` or a default, ignoring the inheritance directive.
2. The field is consumed only when paired with a fresh `executionWorkspace` record creation, but most of our issues had `executionWorkspaceId: null`
payload.title: inheritExecutionWorkspaceFromIssueId not honored at runtime — agent's persisted workspace wins

payload.body:
## Summary

When using the `gemini_local` adapter, Paperclip persists session IDs in `agent_task_sessions` and attempts to resume them on subsequent heartbeat runs. Gemini sessions expire faster than Claude sessions (typically within 15-30 minutes of inactivity). When the resume fails with "Invalid session identifier," Paperclip marks the entire run as `adapter_failed` instead of clearing the stale session and retrying with a fresh session. This causes agents to enter an error/idle flapping loop that wastes heartbeat cycles and produces zero useful work.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an agent with `adapter_type = gemini_local`
2. Let it complete a heartbeat run successfully (session ID saved to `agent_task_sessions`)
3. Wait longer than the Gemini session expiry window (~15-30 min of inactivity)
4. Trigger the next heartbeat run (timer or assignment wake)

## Expected Behavior

Paperclip attempts to resume the saved session. Gemini API returns "Invalid session identifier." Paperclip clears the stale session from `agent_task_sessions`. Paperclip retries the run with a fresh session. Run succeeds.

## Actual Behavior

Paperclip attempts to resume. Gemini API returns "Invalid session identifier." Paperclip marks the run as `adapter_failed` with error: `Error resuming session: Invalid session identifier "{uuid}"`. Agent status set to `error`. Error-recovery resets agent to `idle`. Next heartbeat tries to resume the SAME stale session. Fails again. Loop repeats indefinitely.

## Impact

- Each failed resume wastes a heartbeat cycle with zero productive work
- Agents flap error/idle indefinitely until manual intervention
- We accumulated 11,947+ stale sessions across 15 gemini_local agents
- One agent (Scrum Master) had 78 session records in agent_task_sessions
- Error code `adapter_failed` is misleading -- the adapter works, the session is expired

## Workaround

Cron job every 5 minutes to purge stale sessions:
```sql
DELETE FROM agent_task_sessions
WHERE last_error IS NOT NULL
AND agent_id IN (SELECT id FROM agents WHERE adapter_type = 'gemini_local');

DELETE FROM agent_task_sessions
WHERE updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
AND agent_id IN (SELECT id FROM agents WHERE adapter_type = 'gemini_local');
```
This prevents accumulation but the first run after a session expires still fails.

## Suggested Fix

In `services/heartbeat.js`, when the adapter returns "Invalid session identifier":
1. Delete the stale session from `agent_task_sessions`
2. Clear `session_id_before` on the current heartbeat_run
3. Retry with `freshSession: true`
4. Log a warning (not error) so it doesn't trigger error-recovery

Alternatively, add a config option like `maxSessionAge` or `sessionReuse: false` for adapters with short-lived sessions.

## Additional Context

- Claude sessions (`claude_local`) are long-lived and resume fine. Bug is Gemini-specific.
- `agent_task_sessions` grows unboundedly for Gemini agents -- needs TTL or max-rows.
- A distinct error code `session_expired` vs `adapter_failed` would improve observability.
payload.title: Bug: Gemini adapter fails hard on expired session resume instead of falling back to fresh session

payload.author: KingxBTC
payload.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/companies/{companyId}/issues` (and the child variant `POST /api/issues/{id}/children`) currently accepts duplicate creations with no server-side dedup. Under realistic agent conditions — parallel heartbeats, stale wakes, retries after partial failures — this lets a single agent run silently create N near-identical child issues, wasting both tokens and reviewer attention.

The instruction-layer guard (`AGENTS.md: search before filing`) is intrinsically fragile and easy to skip; the right enforcement layer is the API.

This mirrors @paperclipai/paperclip#6265 (approvals dedup), #4780 (agent-hires idempotency), #2489 (enqueueWakeup idempotency), #5993 (dispatch_fingerprint dedup). Same shape, different endpoint.

## Evidence (one downstream incident)

Agent run `b1f96274` (heartbeat for issue DAI-459) called `POST /issues/{id}/children` three times within 18 seconds and got back three near-identical QA child issues (titles all `"QA验收: playwright-collect.ts 3项bug修复 [DAI-459]"`). The server happily created all three. Two were later cancelled manually.

| Created child | originFingerprint | createdByRunId |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DAI-460 | `"default"` | `null` |
| DAI-461 | `"default"` | `null` |
| DAI-462 | `"default"` | `null` |

`originFingerprint` is not client-writable, and `createdByRunId` is not even a column on `issues` despite the `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` header being read elsewhere — so post-hoc audit can't even tell which run filed which duplicate.

## Three proposed fixes

### 1. Accept a client-supplied `idempotencyKey` on POST issues

`POST /api/companies/{companyId}/issues` and `POST /api/issues/{id}/children` should accept an optional `idempotencyKey: string` in the body. Within a configurable window (suggest 24h), a second POST with the same `(companyId, idempotencyKey)` returns `409 duplicate { existingIssueId, status }` or replays the original `201`.

Convention agents would adopt: `idempotencyKey = "{parentId}:{purpose-slug}"` (e.g. `b1f96274:qa-validation`).

Pattern alignment: identical to the body-key approach proposed in #6265.

### 2. Backfill `createdByRunId` on issues from `X-Paperclip-Run-Id`

The server already extracts `actor.runId` from the header (see `getActorInfo(req)` at `server/src/routes/issues.ts:2568`) and uses it in `logActivity(...)`, but does not persist it onto the created issue row — and the `issues` table doesn't currently have a `created_by_run_id` column (peer tables like `issue_work_products`, `issue_tree_holds`, and `routines` do).

Proposed:

- Add `created_by_run_id uuid references heartbeat_runs(id) on delete set null` to the `issues` table (matches the pattern already used by `routines` and `issue_work_products`).
- In both POST handlers (`routes/issues.ts:2559` and `:2649`), pass `createdByRunId: actor.runId ?? null` through to `svc.create()` / `svc.createChild()`.
- Optional but consistent: do the same for `updated_by_run_id` on PATCH paths.

This is a pure audit win — without it, "which run created this child" is unanswerable except through fuzzy time-window joins on the activity log.

### 3. Soft dedup on `(runId, parentId, fuzzy title)` even when no idempotencyKey is supplied

As a defensive fallback for agents that haven't been updated to send a key, the create handler should at least check: same `actor.runId` + same `parentId` + title trigram-similar to an existing open child within the same run, within (say) 5 minutes. On match: return `409 duplicate_in_run { existingIssueId }`.

Cheap to implement — `issues_title_search_idx` is already a GIN trgm index on `title`, so this is a one-query lookup. Conservative threshold (≥0.7 similarity) to avoid false positives on legitimately-similar siblings.

## Why server-side, not just instructions

- Deterministic across all agents, runs, and adapters.
- Survives parallel heartbeats and race conditions instruction-layer guards cannot win.
- Gives downstream agent operators a stable contract: send `idempotencyKey`, ge
payload.title: Server-side dedup + run-id audit for POST /api/companies/{companyId}/issues (agent-driven duplicate child issue creation)

## Summary

`PATCH /api/routines/:id` accepts a `variables` field in the body, returns **HTTP 200 OK** with a bumped `latestRevisionNumber`, but **silently drops the `variables` content**. The response payload shows `variables: []` and the persisted `routine_revisions.snapshot.routine.variables` is also `[]`.

This is a correctness footgun: operators believe their config landed, the audit trail shows a revision bump, but the runtime behavior is unchanged. Bugs hide for weeks.

## Reproduction (RCV instance, `v2026.517.0`)

```bash
curl -X PATCH \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "variables": [
      {
        "name": "orphan_terminal_branch",
        "label": "Orphan terminal housekeeping pass",
        "type": "boolean",
        "defaultValue": false,
        "value": true,
        "required": false
      }
    ]
  }' \
  "https://bridge.../api/routines/7596e6d7-96f7-4cee-a518-e33b735a17bc"
```

**Response:** HTTP 200 OK. `latestRevisionNumber: 2` (was 1). `variables: []` in response body.

**DB state:**
```sql
SELECT revision_number, jsonb_path_query_array(snapshot, '$.routine.variables[*].name') AS vars
FROM routine_revisions WHERE routine_id='7596e6d7-...' ORDER BY revision_number DESC LIMIT 2;
--  revision_number | vars
-- -----------------+------
--                2 | []     ← bumped but empty
--                1 | []
```

The new revision row was created, but with empty `variables`. The PATCH body was effectively a no-op for that field, despite a 200 response.

## Impact in RCV

Caused **3 separate board approvals to be opened by agents over a 24h window** (`32acffde`, `74ebf596`, `7172c599`), each escalating "the variable I set didn't take effect" with progressively more diagnostic detail. Operator had to apply a SQL INSERT workaround on `routine_revisions` to manually publish a snapshot with the variable populated — see workaround section below.

## Workaround (operator SQL)

```sql
-- 1. Insert new revision with variables populated in snapshot
INSERT INTO routine_revisions (
  company_id, routine_id, revision_number, title, description, snapshot, change_summary
)
SELECT 
  company_id, routine_id, 
  COALESCE(MAX(revision_number), 0) + 1 OVER (),
  title, description,
  jsonb_set(snapshot, '{routine,variables}',
    '[{"name":"orphan_terminal_branch","type":"boolean","value":true,"defaultValue":false,"required":false}]'::jsonb
  ),
  'Operator manual snapshot publish — workaround for PATCH variables silent drop'
FROM routine_revisions WHERE routine_id='<ROUTINE_ID>'
ORDER BY revision_number DESC LIMIT 1
RETURNING id;

-- 2. Point routines.latest_revision_* at the new revision
UPDATE routines SET 
  latest_revision_id = '<NEW_REVISION_ID>',
  latest_revision_number = <NEW_NUM>,
  variables = <the same jsonb>
WHERE id='<ROUTINE_ID>';
```

## Suggested fix

In the PATCH handler (likely `server/src/routes/routines.ts`):

1. Either **accept** the `variables` field and persist it in both `routines.variables` and `routine_revisions.snapshot.routine.variables`
2. Or **reject** PATCHes that include unknown / unhandled fields with HTTP 422 + a clear error message ("`variables` cannot be updated via this endpoint; use `POST /api/routines/:id/revisions` instead.")

The "silent 200 + revision bump" path is the worst of both worlds — looks successful but does nothing.

## Environment

- Paperclip `v2026.517.0`
- Embedded PostgreSQL
- 22 active agents, ~24 active routines

## Cross-reference

- Memory `routine_revision_snapshot_trap` already documents this for operator memory but it should be a framework-level fix, not a workaround pattern.
- Related: agent capability gates also lacks `routine.variables.write` as a distinct permission (currently bundled in `routine.write` which is the API-level gate that lets PATCH succeed-but-no-op).
payload.title: PATCH /api/routines silently drops 'variables' field — HTTP 200 + revision bump but no-op

payload.body:
## Summary

An issue assigned to an agent entered a recovery-wake loop: it was repeatedly set to `status='blocked'` with `blockedByIssueIds=[]` (an internally inconsistent state — `blocked` should always name blockers, per the `paperclip` skill doc, line 135). The watchdog detected the inconsistency, woke the agent to "choose and record a valid disposition", the agent set `in_progress`, something set it back to `blocked` + empty, the loop continued. **Five wakes fired before the agent broke the cycle by naming a real first-class blocker.**

Each wake loaded ~200K cached tokens of context plus fresh work — five wakes on Opus 4.7 = ~$6 of reference-cost token spend for no useful work.

## Observed sequence

Observed on Paperclip 2026.517.0. The agent (assignee) is `CEO (Lencioni)`. The issue is `GOV-19` ("Queue 4-post sequence: Angle A → C → OECD-anchored → B(hold)") with child issues `GOV-21`, `GOV-24`, `GOV-25`, `GOV-26`.

| Time (Z) | Wake reason | Run duration | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22:44:11 | `source_scoped_recovery_action` | 86s | Lencioni found `blocked` + `blockedByIssueIds=[]`, set `in_progress` |
| 22:45:37 | `finish_successful_run_handoff` | 21s | No new comments; exits |
| 22:46:11 | `source_scoped_recovery_action` | 29s | Found `blocked` + empty again; corrected to `in_progress`; explicitly noted "third recurring `blocked`/empty-blockers pattern" |
| 22:46:40 | `finish_successful_run_handoff` | 8s | No new comments; exits |
| 22:47:11 | `source_scoped_recovery_action` | 65s | Tried to move to `in_review`; API rejected (no review path on this issue) |
| 22:48:17 | `finish_successful_run_handoff` | 7s | No new comments; exits |
| 22:48:41 | `source_scoped_recovery_action` | 31s | **Agent broke the loop** by naming `GOV-21` (a real downstream child waiting on a human interaction) as a first-class blocker |

Verbatim from the agent at the third wake:

> "Recovery #3 — recurring `blocked`/empty-blockers pattern. This is the third `source_scoped_recovery_action` wake for GOV-19. Each time: status set to `blocked` with empty `blockedByIssueIds`, checkout..."

And at the fifth wake (the one that worked):

> "Recovery #5 — breaking the cascade loop with first-class blocker. Fifth `source_scoped_recovery_action` wake. Root cause confirmed: harness cascades `blocked` from children to parent when no real..."

## Root cause analysis (partial)

I traced part of the path but did not find the cascade source:

- `services/recovery/service.js` enqueues the wake with `wakePolicy.reason = "source_scoped_recovery_action"` when a successful run leaves an issue in `missing_disposition` state (lines ~1289–1314).
- The recovery service itself **does not change issue status** — it only fires the wake asking the agent to choose.
- The `blocked` + `blockedByIssueIds=[]` state must be appearing via some other code path between wakes. Two candidates I couldn't fully confirm:
  1. **A parent-status cascade** — when children's `status` changes, the parent's `status` gets updated without also populating `blockedByIssueIds`. The agent's diagnosis ("harness cascades `blocked` from children to parent") points here.
  2. **The agent's own prior wake** sets `blocked` via an API code path that doesn't enforce non-empty `blockedByIssueIds`. (`paperclip` skill says you should name blockers, but it's not enforced as an API write-path invariant.)

Happy to dig further if a maintainer can point me at the file.

## Proposed defensive fixes

Any of these would help. Ranked by impact:

### 1. API-level invariant: `status='blocked'` requires non-empty `blockedByIssueIds`

In `services/issues.js`'s update path, reject (or coerce) any update that would leave an issue in `{status: 'blocked', blockedByIssueIds: []}`. This makes the inconsistent state unrepresentable. Two options:
- Return 400 with a clear message ("blocked status requires at least one blockedByIssueId"), forcing the caller to fix it, OR
- Silently coerce: if `blockedByIssueIds` is empt
payload.title: Recovery wake loop — parent issue stuck in 'blocked' with empty 'blockedByIssueIds', repeated source_scoped_recovery_action wakes

payload.body:
## Summary

In `paperclipai@2026.517.0`, `dist/index.js` bundles the `create-paperclip-plugin` scaffolder script alongside the main commander CLI. The scaffolder is gated only by:

```js
if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
  runCli();
}
```

When `paperclipai` is invoked via `npm exec paperclipai run` (which is what `npx paperclipai run` and many systemd units resolve to), Node receives the **real** `.pnpm/...` path as `argv[1]` (the `.bin/..` segment is normalized away by Node). The gate matches, `runCli()` fires *before* `main()`, takes `process.argv[2]` as the plugin name, and calls `scaffoldPluginProject({ outputDir: <cwd>/<argv[2]>, pluginName: <argv[2]> })`.

Result: every `npm exec paperclipai <subcommand>` invocation tries to scaffold a plugin named `<subcommand>` in CWD. For `paperclipai run` this:

1. Creates `<cwd>/run` directory.
2. Crashes inside `packLocalPackage` with `Error: Package package.json not found at <node_modules>/.pnpm/packages/shared/package.json` (the function resolves the monorepo path `packages/shared/package.json` which only exists in the source tree, not in a published install).
3. On systemd restart, the now-existing `<cwd>/run` makes `scaffoldPluginProject` throw `Error: Directory already exists: <cwd>/run` instead — putting the service into a permanent crash loop.

## Affected versions

- **Broken:** `2026.517.0` (reproduced)
- **Last known good:** `2026.512.0` (the scaffolder block is not in the bundle)

## Reproduction

```bash
mkdir /tmp/p-bug && cd /tmp/p-bug
pnpm init >/dev/null
pnpm add paperclipai@2026.517.0
# Real-path invocation reproduces the gate match:
node /tmp/p-bug/node_modules/.pnpm/paperclipai@2026.517.0_*/node_modules/paperclipai/dist/index.js run
# → creates /tmp/p-bug/run, then errors out
```

Or with `npm exec` (which is the pnpm/systemd-style invocation that resolves to the same real path):

```bash
cd /tmp/p-bug
/usr/bin/npx paperclipai run --data-dir /tmp/p-bug/data
# → same failure when CWD allows mkdir
```

The `.bin/` shim invocation (`./node_modules/.bin/paperclipai run`) does NOT hit this gate because the shim's `node \"\$basedir/../paperclipai/dist/index.js\"` traverses the `node_modules/paperclipai → .pnpm/...` symlink, so `argv[1]` ends up with the *symlink* path while `import.meta.url` has the *resolved* real path — they don't match and the scaffolder stays dormant. That is why some installs / dev flows don't see it.

## Evidence in the published bundle

(`paperclipai@2026.517.0` `dist/index.js`, single-file build)

- `~22849` — `function runCli() { const pluginName = process.argv[2]; ...` (the scaffolder entrypoint)
- `~22871` — `if (import.meta.url === \`file://\${process.argv[1]}\`) { runCli(); }` (the always-evaluated gate)
- `~22301` — `if (fs17.existsSync(outputDir)) { throw new Error(\`Directory already exists: \${outputDir}\`); }`
- `~22273` — `throw new Error(\`Package package.json not found at \${packageJsonPath}\`);` inside `packLocalPackage`
- `~22264` — `getLocalSharedPackagePath` returns `path.resolve(getRepoRootFromSdkPath(sdkPath), \"packages\", \"shared\")` — a monorepo path

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. **Don't bundle the `create-paperclip-plugin` standalone script into the main `paperclipai` bundle.** Ship it as a separate file (`dist/create-paperclip-plugin.js`) referenced by a separate bin entry in `package.json`. The current `package.json` has only `\"paperclipai\": \"./dist/index.js\"`, so the second-bin code has no legitimate way to fire under the current packaging.
2. **Tighten the gate** to require an explicit signal — e.g., check `process.argv[1]` ends with `create-paperclip-plugin` (the script's intended bin name), or guard on a sentinel env var.

Option 1 is cleaner.

## Operational impact for downstream tenants

- `systemctl restart paperclip` on the upgraded host crash-loops indefinitely with `Restart=on-failure`.
- The leftover `<WorkingDirectory>/run` directory must be removed manually before any further att
payload.title: v2026.517.0: scaffolder runs on every CLI invocation — creates spurious dir, then crashes on missing packages/shared

payload.body:
## Bug

`POST /api/issues/{id}/checkout` returns an unhandled 500 error when a routine_execution issue is checked out while another open issue with the same `(companyId, originKind, originId, originFingerprint)` key already has a non-null `executionRunId`.

## Root Cause

The checkout service sets `executionRunId = checkoutRunId` via a DB UPDATE. If another routine_execution issue with the same unique key already has `executionRunId` set and is in an open status, the DB constraint `issues_open_routine_execution_uq` fires — a PostgreSQL 23505 (unique violation). This exception is not caught in the checkout service and bubbles up as a 500.

The routine spawn code in `routines.ts` already handles this constraint correctly (converts it to a skip/coalesce result), but `issues.ts` checkout does not.

## Impact

- Routine monitor runs fail to checkout their assigned execution issues
- concurrencyPolicy:skip_if_active cannot clear the stale lock (checkout is the only path)
- Stale routine_execution issues block all future routine spawns indefinitely

## Fix

Wrap the `executionRunId` UPDATE statements in `services/issues.ts checkout()` in a try/catch that detects the `issues_open_routine_execution_uq` violation and throws a proper 409 conflict error instead of propagating the raw DB error.

## Locations

- `server/src/services/issues.ts` — `checkout()` function at ~line 4629 and ~line 4677 (two UPDATE statements that set `executionRunId`)
payload.title: fix: checkout 500 on routine_execution issues when concurrent execution exists

payload.body:
paperclipai v0.x (bundle SHA matches the dist/index.js in npm-cache at the version we currently run) appears to ship the data model for budget enforcement but no enforcement engine:

**Present in dist/index.js (single-bundle build):**
- `budget_policies` table schema (index.js:5751-5878)
- `budget_incidents` table schema (index.js:5836-5878)
- `cost_events` table schema (index.js:7896-7942)
- `pause_reason` / `paused_at` columns on agents (index.js:5217-5222)

**NOT present in dist/index.js:**
- Any code that compares `spentMonthlyCents` to `budgetMonthlyCents`
- Any writer for `agents.pause_reason` or `agents.paused_at`
- Any function that creates `budget_incidents` from `cost_events`
- Any dispatcher/heartbeat gate that refuses to invoke an over-cap agent (no `getInvocationBlock`, `enforceBudget`, `canDispatch`, or equivalent)
- Any writer for `agents.spent_monthly_cents` (clients must PATCH it via `updateAgentSchema`)

**Routes probed:**
- `GET /api/companies/:id/budget-policies` — 404
- `GET /api/cost-events` — 404
- `GET /api/budgets` — 404

`PATCH /api/agents/:id` (`updateAgentSchema`, index.js:2517-2522) accepts `status` and `spentMonthlyCents` but is read-only for `pauseReason` / `pausedAt` — meaning even an external enforcer cannot record the pause reason on the agent row.

**Repro:**
- Configure an agent with `budgetMonthlyCents=300`.
- PATCH `spentMonthlyCents` to `500` (mimicking what a tenant routine does).
- Heartbeat continues to dispatch and no `pauseReason` is set.

**Expected:** at 100% utilisation the platform should set `status=paused`, `pauseReason="budget"`, `pausedAt=now`, and refuse further heartbeat dispatch until a `raise_budget_and_resume` action runs.

**Workaround we built downstream:** an external 15-minute polling routine that PATCHes `status="paused"` when `spent >= cap`. The lack of `pauseReason` write capability means the auditable reason has to live in tenant-side storage rather than on the agent record.

**Asks:**
1. Confirm whether the enforcement engine is intended for a future release and what the target version is.
2. Allow `pauseReason` / `pausedAt` to be set via PATCH (with constraint to enum values) so external enforcers can produce a complete audit record on the agent row.
3. Document the current state in the release notes so tenants understand what `budgetMonthlyCents` does and does not enforce today.

---
Filed by a downstream tenant (Blemy) operating under the per-agent budget cap. Happy to provide additional bundle SHAs, line ranges, or repro artifacts.
payload.title: Budget enforcement engine missing — schema scaffolded but no enforcer wired

payload.body:
### Summary

When plugins are activated at server boot, `activatePlugin()` in `plugin-loader.ts:1935` calls `toolDispatcher.registerPluginTools(pluginKey, manifest)` without passing the plugin's database UUID. The tool registry stores the `pluginKey` (e.g. `"edvgo.anonymization"`) as the `pluginDbId` fallback. When a tool is later executed, the registry checks `workerManager.isRunning("edvgo.anonymization")` — but the worker manager registered the worker under the UUID (`"28143a19-..."`) → **ID mismatch → 502 "worker not running"**.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a plugin and let it reach `ready` status
2. Restart the server (so `activatePlugin()` runs at boot)
3. Verify plugin shows `ready` and worker shows `running` via dashboard
4. Try `POST /api/plugins/tools/execute` with any tool from that plugin
5. **Result:** `502: worker for plugin ... is not running`

### Root Cause

- `plugin-loader.ts:1935`: `toolDispatcher.registerPluginTools(pluginKey, manifest)` — missing third arg
- `plugin-tool-dispatcher.ts:429-433`: `registerPluginTools()` wrapper doesn't accept or forward `pluginDbId`
- `registry.registerPlugin()` already supports the third argument — used correctly in `registerFromDb()` (line 269) and `loadAllPlugins()` (line 333)

The `plugin.enabled` event (which would call `registerFromDb()` with the correct UUID) is **not emitted** at boot for already-ready plugins, so the correct path never fires.

### Expected Behavior

Tool execution should work after server boot without requiring a manual disable/enable cycle.

### Proposed Fix

**`server/src/services/plugin-loader.ts:1935`:**
```diff
-        toolDispatcher.registerPluginTools(pluginKey, manifest);
+        toolDispatcher.registerPluginTools(pluginKey, manifest, pluginId);
```

**`server/src/services/plugin-tool-dispatcher.ts` interface (line 156):**
```diff
   registerPluginTools(
     pluginId: string,
     manifest: PaperclipPluginManifestV1,
+    pluginDbId?: string,
   ): void;
```

**`server/src/services/plugin-tool-dispatcher.ts` implementation (line 429):**
```diff
-    registerPluginTools(pluginId: string, manifest: PaperclipPluginManifestV1): void {
-      registry.registerPlugin(pluginId, manifest);
+    registerPluginTools(pluginId: string, manifest: PaperclipPluginManifestV1, pluginDbId?: string): void {
+      registry.registerPlugin(pluginId, manifest, pluginDbId);
     },
```

### Environment

- Paperclip `@paperclipai/server` v0.3.1
- Docker deployment on Synology NAS
payload.title: Bug: Boot-time plugin tool registration uses pluginKey instead of DB UUID — causes 502 on tool execute

## Description

Creating a company via `POST /api/companies` fails with HTTP 500 if the generated `issue_prefix` collides with one that already exists in the database.

The prefix is derived deterministically from the company name. For example, both `test1co` and `test2co` produce the prefix `TES`. The first company is created successfully, but any subsequent company whose name maps to the same prefix triggers a unique constraint violation in PostgreSQL, which is not handled gracefully and propagates as a 500 error to the client.

The root cause is in `createCompanyWithUniquePrefix` (`server/src/services/companies.ts`, ~line 146), which is missing retry logic: instead of falling back to an alternative prefix (e.g. `TES2`, `TES3`, …), it lets the database exception bubble up unhandled.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a company named `test1co` — succeeds, prefix `TES` is assigned.
2. Create a second company named `test2co` — same prefix `TES` is generated.
3. `POST /api/companies` returns `500 Internal Server Error`.

## Expected behavior

`createCompanyWithUniquePrefix` detects the constraint violation and retries with an incremented suffix (e.g. `TES2`), returning a `201 Created` response with the new company.

## Actual behavior

```
PostgresError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "companies_issue_prefix_idx"
```

The request fails and the company is not created.

## Relevant logs

```
POST /api/companies 500
Failed query: insert into "companies" (...) values (default, $1, default, ..., $2, ..., $3, ...)
params: test2co, TES, 0
caused by: PostgresError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "companies_issue_prefix_idx"
```

## Stack trace

```
at PostgresJsPreparedQuery.queryWithCache (drizzle-orm/.../pg-core/session.ts:73:11)
at createCompanyWithUniquePrefix (server/src/services/companies.ts:146:22)
at Object.create (server/src/services/companies.ts:176:23)
at server/src/routes/companies.ts:272:21
```

## Environment

- **paperclip version:** `2026.517`
- ORM: `drizzle-orm@0.45.2`
- DB driver: `postgres@3.4.8`

payload.body:
# Productivity-Recovery: phantom-blocker cascades from naive stranded-detection

## Summary

On Paperclip `2026.05.x` (Coolify/Netcup self-host of `paperclipai/paperclip`), the auto-recovery subsystem that marks issues as "stranded" produces **phantom-blocker cascades**: it spawns recovery tasks on legitimate long-running issues, those recovery tasks themselves get marked stranded, and the source ends up `blocked` because the recovery task sets `blockedByIssueIds = [source]`. A single silent agent run inflated into 9 touched issues across 4 agents over 4 days on our instance before a human cancelled the root manually.

This is related to but distinct from #5937 (auto-recovery overriding per-issue operator protocol via sibling-issue creation). #5937 is about *content collision* between source and recovery; this proposal is about *cascade dynamics* — how stranded-detection re-fires on its own outputs.

## Repro / evidence

From our instance, anonymised as `ISSUE-NNN`:

- **CMO cascade.** A CMO agent had a silent run on `ISSUE-415`. Within 4 days the system produced: `ISSUE-414→ISSUE-419`, `ISSUE-415→ISSUE-417`, `ISSUE-416→ISSUE-418→ISSUE-413` — every recovery layer itself ended `blocked`. No automatic exit existed; human had to cancel the root.
- **Permanent-channel re-spawn.** `ISSUE-124` is a Telegram board channel — by design always open. During the cleanup of one phantom recovery (`ISSUE-442`), a fresh recovery was spawned on `ISSUE-124` *within seconds* of that cleanup completing. There is no cooldown and no exclusion for permanent channels.
- **Triage sweep.** A single triage pass (`ISSUE-441`) found 4 separate phantom/stale-blocker conditions in one sweep.
- **Self-targeting.** The very meta-issue tracking this proposal (`ISSUE-446`) had a productivity-review recovery (`ISSUE-469`) fired against it.

## Root causes (4)

| # | Root cause | Mechanism |
|---|------------|-----------|
| 1 | **Recovery generates recovery** | Recovery tasks are themselves classified as stranded after `long_active_duration`; no loop-brake. |
| 2 | **Wrong blocker semantics** | Recovery sets `blockedByIssueIds = [source]`; source then carries `unresolvedBlockerCount > 0`, looks "stalled because of recovery", and a fresh recovery spawns. |
| 3 | **Detection too naive** | `long_active_duration` triggers on any long-lived issue. No distinction between permanent channels, project roots, active review stages, and work-in-progress leaf tickets. |
| 4 | **No exclusion list** | Permanent channels, container/project-root issues, and review stages are treated identically to leaf work items. |

## Proposed changes

### 1. Exclusion list — never mark as stranded

Detector should skip any issue matching one of:

- **Project-root issues** — has at least one active child (status ∉ {done, cancelled}).
- **Permanent channels** — carries label `permanent-channel` or `routine-driven`.
- **Active review stage** — `executionState.currentParticipant` is non-null.
- **Open interactions** — has any `request_confirmation` / `ask_user_questions` / `suggest_tasks` interaction in `status=pending`.
- **Unresolved blockers** — `unresolvedBlockerCount > 0`. The blocker is the real stall; the source is correctly waiting.
- **Recovery itself** — carries label `recovery`. Loop-brake.

### 2. Recovery-task semantics

- **Do not** set `blockedByIssueIds = [source]` on the recovery task. This is the central bug (root cause #2).
- Add an annotation comment on the source with `@-mention` to the source's assignee instead.
- The recovery task carries label `recovery` and a structured `sourceRef` field pointing at the source issue.
- The recovery task is its own work item ("please look at X"), not a dependency.

### 3. Loop-detection

- **Max 1 active recovery per source.** Before spawn: query `(label=recovery) AND (sourceRef=X) AND (status NOT IN done/cancelled)`. If non-empty, skip.
- **Cooldown 24h per source.** Track `lastRecoverySpawnAt` on the source; refuse re-spawn within 24h.
-
payload.title: Productivity-Recovery: phantom-blocker cascades from naive stranded-detection

payload.author: NexusMBD
payload.body:
## Problem

The P0/P1 escalation monitor fires on issue A even when A's transitive terminal blocker is `in_review` with a pending user interaction, because the suppression rule only checks A's direct blocker.

**Reproduction chain:**
- A (`blocked`) → B (`blocked`) → C (`in_review` + pending `ask_user_questions`)
- Monitor sees A → B (`blocked`, not `in_review`) → suppression skipped → escalation fires
- But the terminal root is C (`in_review` + pending interaction) — a deliberate hold
- Result: false P1 escalation alerts causing alert fatigue

## Root cause

In `firstBlockedChainFinding`, when a blocked intermediate node B recurses and returns null (chain clean), the code still calls `blockedFindingForLeaf(source, B, path)` on B. Since B has status `blocked` and may be unassigned, this produces a false positive finding.

## Fix

When `blocker.status === "blocked"` and the recursive chain returns null, always `continue` — skip the leaf inspection of the intermediate node. An intermediate blocked node is a passthrough; what matters is whether its chain (its own blockers) has problems.

## Changes

- `server/src/services/recovery/issue-graph-liveness.ts`: replace conditional `hasExplicitWaitingPath` continue with unconditional `continue` when recursive chain returns null
- `server/src/__tests__/issue-liveness.test.ts`: add two regression tests
payload.title: fix: escalation monitor suppression should walk transitive blocker chain

payload.author: jmiramant
payload.body:
## Summary

When the Claude subscription account hits its **weekly usage limit** (Pro/Max plans only — the Anthropic API has no weekly cap), every `claude_local` heartbeat run fails fast with `Claude run failed: subtype=success: You've hit your weekly limit · resets <date>, <time> (<tz>)`. Paperclip classifies this as `error_code='claude_transient_upstream'` and **retries**, which is wrong: the limit is a hard wall until the named reset (typically multiple days away).

The retry flood then saturates the per-company concurrency pool, runs accumulate in `running` status without `process_pid`, the 15-minute spawn watchdog reaps them as `spawn_watchdog_timeout`, and agents flip to `status='error'`. The fleet is effectively down until a manual recovery (DB cleanup + `systemctl restart paperclip.service` + agent revival).

## Real-world incident (2026-05-21)

One production fleet, ~17 active agents:

| Time (ET) | Event |
|---|---|
| `00:04` | First `claude_transient_upstream` failure with `weekly limit` text |
| `00:04–11:03` | 574 retries, all fast-failing with the same weekly-limit error |
| `~11:08` | Per-company spawn queue jams completely; no run gets a `process_pid` after this point |
| `11:08–12:45` | 37 `spawn_watchdog_timeout` failures; 12 of 17 active agents → `status='error'` |
| `12:30–12:55` | Manual recovery: fail zombie `heartbeat_runs` (49 rows queued/running with NULL `process_pid`), restart service, revive error agents |

A second company on the same VM on a **different** Claude account continued to spawn and succeed throughout — confirming the failure is per-account, not per-host or platform-wide.

## Why the misclassification matters

`claude_transient_upstream` implies *retryable upstream blip* (5xx, momentary 529 overload). The weekly-limit error has the opposite shape: it's deterministic, account-scoped, and includes the exact reset timestamp in the error text. Retrying it generates pure churn — and because each retry consumes a heartbeat-run row + concurrency slot + watchdog timer, the churn is what actually takes the fleet down. The 4-day quota wall becomes a ~12-hour spawn-queue meltdown without manual intervention.

## Proposed fix

In the `claude_local` adapter result classifier:

1. Detect the `weekly limit` substring (or, better, whatever structured signal the Claude CLI emits — there may be a JSON field on the `--output-format stream-json` final message).
2. Map to a new non-retryable `error_code`, e.g. `claude_account_quota_exceeded`.
3. Optionally parse the reset timestamp from the message and either:
   - back the affected adapter/account off until `resetsAt`, or
   - flip the agents that share that account into a `paused` posture with a clear `pauseReason` and an auto-resume at the reset time.

A non-retryable classification alone would have prevented the cascade in this incident.

## Code pointer

I don't have the upstream source path, but the runtime sets `error_code='claude_transient_upstream'` with `error` text beginning `Claude run failed: subtype=success: You've hit your weekly limit · resets <date>, <time> (<tz>)`. The mapping is presumably in the `claude_local` adapter's result handler.

## Adjacent finding (separate bug, surfaced during recovery)

The `systemctl restart paperclip.service` that was necessary to clear the wedged spawn worker also applied 11 pending DB migrations (0075–0085) and loaded the on-disk `@paperclipai/server` code. One of those migrations introduced `company_secret_bindings` enforcement (`assertBindingContext` in `services/secrets.js`) — but `company_secret_bindings` was **empty**, with no migration backfill from existing agents' `adapter_config.env` secret_refs. Every agent with a `secret_ref` instantly failed `adapter_failed: Secret is not bound to agent:X at env.Y`. Workaround: re-`PATCH /agents/:id` each affected agent with its current `adapterConfig` so the route's `syncEnvBindingsForTarget` populates bindings.

If you'd like that filed as its own issue, happy
payload.title: Claude weekly-limit errors classified as `claude_transient_upstream` and retried → per-company spawn-queue cascade

payload.body:
## Problem

There is no built-in mechanism in Paperclip to automatically apply `assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig.effort` (for `claude_local`) or the equivalent for other adapters (`modelReasoningEffort` for codex, `variant` for opencode) based on an issue's `priority` field at creation or update time.

Today, the effort lever for cost control is fully manual — either:
- Set per-agent in `adapterConfig.effort` (applies to every run, regardless of which issue), or
- Set per-issue in `assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig.effort` via UI or API at create time (must be remembered for every new issue).

For teams running large agent fleets, neither scales. Critical issues silently get the same thinking budget as backlog items, and forcing every issue-creator to remember the override is error-prone.

## Proposed behavior

A new optional, **company-level** configuration that maps `priority` → effort override, applied automatically by the issue-create/update pipeline when `assigneeAdapterOverrides` is unset:

```jsonc
// part of company / instance settings
{
  "issuePriorityEffortMap": {
    "critical": "high",
    "high":     null,       // null = no override (use agent default)
    "medium":   null,
    "low":      "low"
  }
}
```

When an issue is created or its `priority` changes:

1. If the user already supplied `assigneeAdapterOverrides`, honor that (don't touch).
2. Otherwise, look up the priority in `issuePriorityEffortMap`. If a non-null effort is configured, write that to `assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig.effort` (or the adapter-equivalent key — `modelReasoningEffort` for codex, `variant` for opencode).
3. If the priority changes later (e.g., backlog → critical), recompute on the priority-change event.

The mapping should be a no-op when the configuration is absent (preserves current behavior).

## Why this matters

We just shipped a manual workaround across our 19-agent company ([breathe-again/nira-paperclip](https://github.com/breathe-again/nira-paperclip)) using a one-shot script that PATCHes every open issue:

```python
# Pseudo:
for issue in open_issues:
    if issue.priority == 'critical':
        patch(issue.id, {'assigneeAdapterOverrides': {'adapterConfig': {'effort': 'high'}}})
    elif issue.priority == 'low':
        patch(issue.id, {'assigneeAdapterOverrides': {'adapterConfig': {'effort': 'low'}}})
```

Plus we updated each agent's `AGENTS.md` to self-modulate depth based on `priority`. Both work, but they're per-team boilerplate that should live in Paperclip core.

Empirical cost data backing this: a single misconfigured Opus agent + naive effort burned $62 in three weeks doing empty-poll heartbeats. After right-sizing models per role AND adding severity-aware effort guidance, cost dropped by ~80%. Auto-application of the priority map would have prevented the runaway entirely.

## Suggested scope

Minimum:
- Company-level setting `issuePriorityEffortMap`
- Apply on `POST /companies/:id/issues` and `PATCH /issues/:id` (when priority changes) only when `assigneeAdapterOverrides` is unset
- Adapter-aware key translation (effort / modelReasoningEffort / variant)

Nice-to-have:
- Project-level override (some projects need higher effort defaults)
- A `--dry-run` API flag to preview what would be applied across all open issues without writing
- Telemetry: count of overrides applied per priority bucket, exposed on the Costs page

## Alternative considered

A pre-create webhook/hook system would let teams implement this themselves. That's more flexible but a much bigger surface area to design and harden — and the priority→effort mapping is common enough across teams that a built-in seems cleaner.

## Context

- Discovered in our cost audit: see commit `2972f23` on [breathe-again/nira-paperclip@main](https://github.com/breathe-again/nira-paperclip/blob/main/docs/COST_MANAGEMENT.md) for the policy doc that motivated this
- Related: the existing `IssueModelLane` concept in `ui/src/lib/issue-assignee-overrides.ts
payload.title: feat: auto-apply assigneeAdapterOverrides.effort from issue priority via company config

payload.body:
## Summary

Two related platform bugs observed in production (`codex_local` adapter) that together caused a run to appear \"silently active\" for ~2 days and generated a false-positive critical watchdog alert that required manual CEO intervention to close.

---

## Bug 1 — `codex_local` adapter does not emit a termination event on process exit

### What happened

A `codex_local` run was invoked, produced output for ~3.7 minutes (25 output sequences), then the underlying process exited — apparently after completing its work. No `lifecycle: run finished` event was ever emitted. Paperclip retained an open run record with:

- `pid: 11000`
- `in-memory handle: yes`
- `process group: unknown`
- `finishedAt: null`
- `exitCode: null`

The platform's only signals were the two initial events:
```
2026-05-20T21:35:07.723Z  lifecycle   run started
2026-05-20T21:35:07.845Z  adapter.invoke  adapter invocation
```

No further events arrived. The run stayed open indefinitely.

### Impact

- Paperclip's silent-run watchdog fired after the 1h suspicious → 4h critical thresholds.
- A watchdog issue was auto-created and escalated to the CEO.
- The run was still "active" ~11 hours after last output, and the issue sat open for ~2 days total.
- The work **did complete** — all downstream SDLC phases (Phase 4 QA, Phase 5 Deploy, Phase 6 Staging smoke) finished successfully. The bug caused platform confusion, not a real work failure.

### Root cause hypothesis

The `codex_local` adapter opens a run, invokes the process, but relies on the process itself to call the run-close API before exiting. If the process exits abnormally (crash, OOM, SIGKILL, or clean exit without hitting the close path), no termination event is emitted and the run record is never closed.

### Suggested fix

The adapter should wrap process execution with a finally/atexit handler that unconditionally emits a `lifecycle: run finished` event (with exit code and reason) when the process terminates, regardless of how it exits. The platform could also add a server-side dead-process detector: if a pid is known and the process is no longer alive, auto-close the run.

---

## Bug 2 — Silent-run watchdog does not auto-resolve when source issue reaches `done`

### What happened

The watchdog issue was auto-created correctly. However, by the time it was reviewed, the source issue and all its children had been `done` for many hours. The watchdog had enough signal to auto-close itself but did not.

### Suggested fix

When a silent-run watchdog issue is open and the source issue (`sourceIssueId`) transitions to `done` (or all its direct children reach a terminal state), the watchdog should be auto-closed as a false positive with a recorded reason. This would eliminate the entire class of false-positive watchdog alerts where work completes but the run record stays open.

---

## Environment

- Adapter: `codex_local`
- Platform: Paperclip (self-hosted, production)
- Run ID: `5c20c46f-3772-4633-8d70-adc262cdae29`
- Source issue: internal tracker (not public)
- Observed: 2026-05-20 → 2026-05-21

---

## Severity

- Bug 1: **High** — any abnormal `codex_local` process exit leaves a zombie run record and will trigger a critical watchdog alert.
- Bug 2: **Medium** — false-positive watchdog alerts require manual CEO/orchestrator intervention to close; at scale this is significant noise.
payload.title: codex_local adapter: process exit without termination event causes zombie run + persistent watchdog alerts

payload.author: theCodeForgerHQ
payload.body:
## Summary

`DELETE /api/companies/:id` deletes child tables in an order that violates a
foreign key: it removes `heartbeat_runs` rows **before** `cost_events` rows, but
`cost_events.heartbeat_run_id` references `heartbeat_runs.id` with no
`onDelete` behavior (default `NO ACTION`). When a company has any `cost_events`
tied to a heartbeat run (i.e. any company whose agents have actually run with
cost accounting), the delete transaction aborts with an FK violation and the
endpoint returns `500`. **Companies that have done real work cannot be hard-deleted.**

## Affected code (confirmed on `master`)

`server/src/services/companies.ts` — the cascade-delete sequence inside the
delete transaction deletes the **parent before the child**:

```ts
// :271  parent
await tx.delete(heartbeatRuns).where(eq(heartbeatRuns.companyId, id));
// ...
// :276  child (references heartbeatRuns.id)
await tx.delete(costEvents).where(eq(costEvents.companyId, id));
```

The FK, `packages/db/src/schema/cost_events.ts`:

```ts
heartbeatRunId: uuid("heartbeat_run_id").references(() => heartbeatRuns.id),
```

Note: this column has **no `onDelete`**, whereas the sibling references to
`heartbeat_runs` elsewhere do — e.g. `environment_leases.heartbeatRunId` and
`secret_access_events.heartbeatRunId` are both
`.references(() => heartbeatRuns.id, { onDelete: "set null" })`. So `cost_events`
is the one that will hard-fail when its referenced `heartbeat_runs` row is
deleted first.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Boot Paperclip (`local_trusted`).
2. Create a company, create an agent, trigger a heartbeat that runs at least once
   (writes a `heartbeat_runs` row AND a `cost_events` row referencing it).
3. `DELETE /api/companies/<id>`.

```bash
curl -fsS -X DELETE "localhost:3100/api/companies/$COMPANY_ID"
```

## Expected

Company and all dependent rows deleted; `200`/`204`.

## Actual

`500`. The transaction rolls back with a Postgres FK violation
(`update or delete on table "heartbeat_runs" violates foreign key constraint`
from `cost_events`).

## Root cause

Delete order is wrong relative to the FK dependency graph. `cost_events` (child)
must be deleted before `heartbeat_runs` (parent), or the FK should be declared
`ON DELETE CASCADE` / `SET NULL` like its siblings.

## Suggested fix

Either reorder so children precede parents:

```ts
// delete in FK-dependency order: cost_events BEFORE heartbeat_runs
await tx.delete(costEvents).where(eq(costEvents.companyId, id));
await tx.delete(heartbeatRuns).where(eq(heartbeatRuns.companyId, id));
```

…or add `{ onDelete: "set null" }` (or `"cascade"`) to the
`cost_events.heartbeat_run_id` FK in the schema so Postgres handles ordering —
matching `environment_leases` / `secret_access_events`.

## Impact / severity

Medium. Any company that has run agents (the normal case) cannot be hard-deleted
via the API. `deletionMode: "soft"` sidesteps it.

## Environment

- Found via downstream integration testing (single-user, `local_trusted`, embedded Postgres / PG18).
- Originally observed at commit `f25753053749d42fa808a9d92132467d2d75dcd0`.
- **Confirmed still present on `master`** (companies.ts delete order :271 before :276; `cost_events.ts` FK lacks `onDelete`; retrieved 2026-05-21).

## Workaround (downstream)

Create companies with `deletionMode: "soft"` and never hard-delete.
payload.title: DELETE /api/companies/:id violates FK: heartbeat_runs deleted before cost_events (cost_events.heartbeat_run_id has no onDelete)
