## Summary

`rewriteBareSpecifiers()` in `ui/src/plugins/slots.tsx` only handles import statements with literal whitespace around the `from` / `import` keywords. Minified bundles (esbuild's default output, used by e.g. [@tomismeta/paperclip-aperture](https://github.com/tomismeta/paperclip-aperture)) emit `}from"react"` with no whitespace, which the current `replaceAll(\` from ${from}\`, ...)` pattern doesn't match. The bare specifier leaks through to the browser, which then errors:

> `Failed to resolve module specifier "react". Relative references must start with either "/", "./", or "../".`

The plugin's UI slot fails to mount and shows the host's placeholder fallback. Server-side: plugin status=ready, worker process healthy, bundle delivered as 200 OK — but the browser-side dynamic import throws.

## Reproduce

1. Install a plugin whose `dist/ui/index.js` is minified by esbuild without explicit whitespace preservation (Aperture v0.4.4 is one)
2. Visit the plugin's page or sidebar slot
3. Browser console shows the bare-specifier error; UI slot doesn't render

Repro environment: Paperclip v0.3.1, React 19, Chrome 147.

## Root cause

`ui/src/plugins/slots.tsx` line 354:

\`\`\`ts
result = result.replaceAll(` from ${from}`, ` from ${to}`);
\`\`\`

The literal leading space requires whitespace-padded import syntax. Minified ES modules legally omit that whitespace.

## Proposed fix

Replace the two `replaceAll` calls with regex variants that tolerate optional whitespace, anchored on the `from`/`import` keyword via `\b`:

\`\`\`ts
const fromEsc = from.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
result = result.replace(new RegExp(\`\\\\bfrom\\\\s*${fromEsc}\`, "g"), \`from ${to}\`);
result = result.replace(new RegExp(\`\\\\bimport\\\\s*${fromEsc}\`, "g"), \`import ${to}\`);
\`\`\`

`\b` ensures we match `from`/`import` as tokens (not as substrings of other identifiers), and `\s*` allows zero-or-more whitespace before the specifier. The specifiers in the `rewrites` table are already wrapped in their literal quote characters, so accidental string-content matches require a JS string to contain a literal `"react"` / `'react'` substring, which is vanishingly rare in production bundles.

Happy to open a PR. Wanted to file the issue first so a maintainer can confirm the approach.

## Workaround for users in the meantime

Patch `ui/src/plugins/slots.tsx` locally with the diff above and rebuild the UI (`cd ui && pnpm build`). Plugin UI mounts correctly after a browser hard-refresh.
payload.title: Plugin UI loader fails to rewrite bare specifiers in minified bundles

payload.author: nicorodrigues
payload.body:
## Symptom

Issues become permanently locked to a dead `checkoutRunId` after their owning heartbeat run terminates. Public API surfaces show `activeRun: null` (because `executionRunId` is cleared on termination) but every `POST /api/issues/:id/checkout` returns `409 Issue checkout conflict`, and every mutation that flows through ownership checks fails the same way.

We've hit this three times in one Paperclip company over a short window. Each time the only practical remedy was the `POST /api/issues/:id/admin/force-release` endpoint, which is board-gated and not discoverable.

## Reproduction shape

1. Agent A checks out issue I via run R1. `issues.checkoutRunId = R1`, `issues.executionRunId = R1`, `issues.status = 'in_progress'`, `issues.assigneeAgentId = A`.
2. Run R1 reaches any terminal state: clean termination via `cancelRun`, watchdog-driven liveness termination, or `reapOrphanedRuns` marking it `failed` with `errorCode='process_lost'`.
3. Either:
   - Issue I gets reassigned (manager/board patches `assigneeAgentId` to agent B), **or**
   - Issue I moves to a non-`in_progress` status via a code path that does not clear lock columns (some execution-policy transitions, some recovery transitions, monitor-driven `in_review`), **or**
   - Agent B (different from A) is the next one to try checkout.
4. Subsequent checkout by **any** agent returns `409 conflict` indefinitely. `issues.executionRunId` is `null` so the issue *looks* idle.

## Root cause (file:line refs in master @ `333a16b`)

`releaseIssueExecutionAndPromote` (`server/src/services/heartbeat.ts:8121`) clears `executionRunId / executionAgentNameKey / executionLockedAt` on run finalization, but never clears `checkoutRunId`. See lines 8161–8171:

```ts
if (issue.executionRunId === run.id) {
  await tx
    .update(issues)
    .set({
      executionRunId: null,
      executionAgentNameKey: null,
      executionLockedAt: null,
      updatedAt: new Date(),
    })
    .where(eq(issues.id, issue.id));
}
```

`clearExecutionRunIfTerminal` (`server/src/services/issues.ts:3342`) re-runs the same clear on every checkout/release based on heartbeat terminality. **There is no symmetric `clearCheckoutRunIfTerminal`.** That asymmetry is the bug.

Self-heal of `checkoutRunId` exists only via `adoptStaleCheckoutRun` (`server/src/services/issues.ts:3269`), and its WHERE clause is too narrow to cover the failure modes above:

```ts
.where(
  and(
    eq(issues.id, input.issueId),
    eq(issues.status, "in_progress"),
    eq(issues.assigneeAgentId, input.actorAgentId),
    eq(issues.checkoutRunId, input.expectedCheckoutRunId),
  ),
)
```

- Status moved off `in_progress` → never matches.
- Assignee changed → never matches.
- New caller is a different agent → never matches.

Result: a stale `checkoutRunId` pointing at a terminal `heartbeat_runs` row, and no path in the codebase that will clear it without operator intervention.

## Proposed fix

Three small, localized, reversible changes plus a docs follow-up. Symmetric to the existing execution-lock clearing path.

**Fix A — Clear `checkoutRunId` in `releaseIssueExecutionAndPromote`.** Extend the update at `heartbeat.ts:8161` to also null `checkoutRunId` when it points at the terminating run. Scope the WHERE with `or(eq(executionRunId, run.id), eq(checkoutRunId, run.id))` so it stays idempotent.

**Fix B — Add `clearCheckoutRunIfTerminal` in `issues.ts`.** Mirror `clearExecutionRunIfTerminal`. No assignee/status precondition — a terminal heartbeat run holds no real claim regardless of the row's current assignee or status. Call it from the same sites as the execution-lock helper: `checkout`, `assertCheckoutOwner`, `release`, and the top of the issue PATCH route.

**Fix C — Backstop recovery sweeper.** Periodic pass in `recovery/service.ts` that scans `issues` where `checkoutRunId IS NOT NULL OR executionRunId IS NOT NULL` and the referenced `heartbeat_runs` row is either missing or in a terminal status. Clears the lock cols and writes one `a
payload.title: Issues lock to dead checkoutRunId after run terminates (activeRun=null + persistent 409)

payload.author: titovka-infra
payload.body:
## Summary

The `@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway` adapter (see `packages/adapters/openclaw-gateway/src/server/execute.ts:1139`) unconditionally injects `agentParams.paperclip = paperclipPayload` into every heartbeat handoff. The OpenClaw side validates `agentParams` against a strict schema with `additionalProperties: false`, and **no released OpenClaw version (as of 2026.5.12-beta.8) recognises the `paperclip` property**. As a result, every Paperclip→OpenClaw run fails immediately with:
The receiving agent goes to `status: error`, all assigned issues transition to `blocked`, and Paperclip's `stranded_issue_recovery` mechanism keeps generating duplicate follow-up issues until the agent is paused manually.

## Environment

- Paperclip: latest `paperclip:local` build (commit on `main` as of 2026-05-12)
- OpenClaw gateway: `2026.5.7` (current stable) on a separate host, accessed via `wss://genius.transconvey.ru:8443/`
- Both ends authenticated and paired correctly — failure is purely schema validation.
- Verified the same failure mode against npm pre-release `openclaw@2026.5.12-beta.8`: `paperclip` is still not in the gateway's `agentParams` schema bundle.

## Reproduction

1. Create a company in Paperclip.
2. Onboard an agent with `adapterType: openclaw_gateway` pointing at a stock OpenClaw gateway (`2026.5.7` or any beta up to `2026.5.12-beta.8`).
3. Approve pairing, run any `[Inbox] …` issue.
4. Observe `heartbeat_runs.error = invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'`.

## Root cause (in this repo)

`packages/adapters/openclaw-gateway/src/server/execute.ts`, around line 1139:

```ts
const agentParams: Record<string, unknown> = {
  ...payloadTemplate,
  message,
  sessionKey,
  idempotencyKey: ctx.runId,
};
delete agentParams.text;
agentParams.paperclip = paperclipPayload;   // ← rejected by OpenClaw's strict schema
```

The `paperclip` envelope is a useful Paperclip-side context bundle (`runId`, `issueId`, `wakeReason`, `workspace`, `workspaceRuntime`, etc.), but OpenClaw is a generic gateway shared with other clients and has no reason to declare it as a known property.

## Suggested fixes (in order of preference)

1. **Move the envelope out of `agentParams`.** Either send it as a sibling top-level field that the OpenClaw side ignores (`payload.paperclip = paperclipPayload`), or piggy-back it through `payloadTemplate.text`/`message` as a structured prelude. This decouples the two projects' schema evolution.

2. **Gate the field behind adapter config.** Add `sendPaperclipEnvelope: boolean` (default `true`) to the adapter config so operators running against an OpenClaw version that doesn't yet understand the field can disable it. Today the only workaround is to fork the adapter and remove the line.

3. **Coordinate with OpenClaw upstream** to register `paperclip` (or a renamed `clientContext`) as an officially accepted optional property in the gateway's agent-params schema. This is the cleanest long-term solution but is multi-project.

## Workaround used in production

Until this is addressed, we have:
- Paused the affected agent in Paperclip (`status: paused`).
- Cancelled the auto-generated `stranded_issue_recovery` issues that piled up.
- Re-routed the work onto the REST API + Paperclip skill channel — the agent reads assigned issues via `/api/companies/{id}/issues` instead of receiving heartbeat-driven runs. This keeps inbox automation flowing while we wait for either side to ship a fix.

Happy to test a candidate patch against our setup (Paperclip + OpenClaw `2026.5.7`).

---

**Files / logs gathered for context:**
- Failing `heartbeat_runs.error` row: `invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'`, `error_code: openclaw_gateway_request_failed`, `exit_code: 1`.
- Sample of three consecutive failures within 1 second (Paperclip retry cycle).
- Confirmed schema-bundle of `openclaw@2026.5.12-beta.8` (`package/dist/protocol-*.js`) — no occurrence of `"paperclip":` outside docs.
payload.title: `openclaw-gateway` adapter: `paperclip` envelope in `agentParams` gets rejected by OpenClaw's strict schema

## Summary

Multiple routines exhibit broken `dispatch_fingerprint` dedup behavior: the same routine produces 200+ rows in `routine_runs` with `failure_reason='duplicate_fingerprint'` over 7 days, all sharing identical fingerprint values. The dedup is "working" in the sense that it labels them duplicates and discards them, but it should not be PRODUCING duplicates at this rate in the first place.

## Observed on

- Paperclip version: **v2026.513.0** (commit `f4bed4a7`, migrations 0001-0084)
- Installation: production single-tenant on Hetzner VPS
- Window: rolling 7 days as of 2026-05-14

## Affected routines (top examples, all CTO-owned)

| Routine | Dup fingerprints in 7d |
|---|---|
| CTO Incident Governor | 222 |
| CTO PR Governor | 222 |
| CTO Issue Governor | 222 |
| Sentry Monitor (active) | 312 |

The 222 count for the three CTO Governors is suspiciously identical, suggesting all three are firing on the same trigger cadence and producing identical fingerprints despite presumably distinct logical scopes (incidents vs PRs vs issues).

## Expected behavior

`dispatch_fingerprint` should incorporate enough scope (routine_id + relevant entity context) that distinct trigger events produce distinct fingerprints. If the dedup is engaged ~30+ times per day on the same routine, either:

1. The fingerprint formula collapses entity scope (e.g., all of "list all open PRs" hashes to one value regardless of PR set state), or
2. The trigger is mis-firing without intent to dedup (e.g., the scheduler is re-firing the same wake without changing inputs).

Either way, the routine is doing the same thing 30+ times/day and getting blocked 30+ times/day. That is wasted scheduler work and obscures legitimate dedup signals.

## Operator impact

- 944 stale `routine_runs` with `failure_reason='duplicate_fingerprint'` over 7 days — non-trivial DB churn
- These routines never advance their goal, but consume scheduler attention
- Under subscription billing (`*_local` adapters), token cost is hidden but wall-clock waste is real
- Auditor detects this pattern but cannot diagnose the root cause without framework-side instrumentation

## Suggested investigation areas

1. The function that computes `dispatch_fingerprint` — is the routine ID + input-state hash including enough scope?
2. The scheduler's de-duplication window — is it being applied at the wrong layer?
3. Whether `CTO Incident Governor`, `CTO PR Governor`, `CTO Issue Governor` are intended to share a fingerprint (which would suggest the routine names are different but the underlying definitions are identical — a separate operator-side concern)

## Reproduction (operator-side, read-only)

```sql
SELECT r.id, r.specific_catalog AS routine_kind,
       COUNT(*) AS total_runs_7d,
       SUM(CASE WHEN failure_reason='duplicate_fingerprint' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dup_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT dispatch_fingerprint) AS distinct_fingerprints
FROM routines r
JOIN routine_runs rr ON rr.routine_id=r.id
WHERE rr.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY r.id, r.specific_catalog
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN failure_reason='duplicate_fingerprint' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 4
ORDER BY dup_count DESC;
```

## Auditor context

Surfaced by `gust-paperclip-auditor` v3.0 standard audit on 2026-05-14, audit ID `2026-05-14-1152-STANDARD`. First reported in `2026-05-14-0150-DEEP-004` (carry-forward), still un-fixed.
payload.title: dispatch_fingerprint dedup produces 200+ identical-fingerprint duplicates per routine in 7d (multiple CTO Governors at 222 dups each)

## Summary

A `missing_disposition` recovery action (cause `successful_run_missing_state`) becomes effectively unresolvable for operators when its source issue is legitimately `blocked` by a first-class blocker. The intended escape hatch — `POST /api/issues/:issueId/recovery-actions/resolve` with `outcome: "blocked"` — **does exist** (verified on server `2026.513.0`), but it is undocumented and the recovery action's `nextAction` text steers owners toward `checkout`, which `422`s on a blocked issue. The result is a recovery action stuck `active` forever, re-waking owners, with no automatic re-evaluation.

## Reproduction

1. An issue runs, the run ends `in_progress` without recording a post-run disposition → reconcile raises a `successful_run_missing_state` / `missing_disposition` recovery action and sets the source issue `status: blocked` (`server/src/services/recovery/service.ts` `escalateStrandedAssignedIssue`, ~L1812-1841).
2. The source issue also has a *legitimate* first-class blocker, so `blockedByIssueIds` is non-empty and `blocked` is the correct disposition.
3. The recovery action's `nextAction` reads: *"Choose and record a valid issue disposition without copying transcript content."* (`server/src/services/recovery/service.ts:1648-1650`) — with no pointer to the resolve endpoint.
4. The owner interprets "record a disposition" as checkout + PATCH status. `POST /api/issues/:id/checkout` returns `422 {"error":"Issue is blocked by unresolved blockers"}` (`server/src/services/issues.ts:4614-4618`).
5. `blocked` *is* the valid disposition, but the owner cannot reach a checked-out run to record it without removing a legitimate blocker — which would itself be wrong.
6. The recovery action stays `status: active`, `attemptCount` and `lastAttemptAt` frozen, `outcome: null`. It never re-evaluates and permanently re-wakes the owner.

Confirmed downstream on a real company (issue `PET-473`, recovery `0810e4e7-46f1-41c7-9353-eea7210c33cd`). Operators tried, and failed, to clear it via: PATCH→blocked, PATCH→in_progress, clearing the blocker, full checkout + corrective run, and a returnOwner temp-clear-blocker + checkout cycle. All left the recovery `active`.

## Root cause — the escape hatch exists but is undiscoverable

The fix path is already in the codebase; operators just can't find it.

- **The resolve endpoint exists.** `POST /api/issues/:issueId/recovery-actions/resolve` (`server/src/routes/issues.ts:1833`). Probing server `2026.513.0` with an empty body returns `400` (schema validation), **not** `404` — the route is live. Downstream operators reported `404` because they guessed action-id-scoped paths (`POST .../recovery-actions/{id}/resolve`, `PATCH .../recovery-actions/{id}`); the real route is issue-scoped.
- **It already handles the blocked case correctly.** With `outcome: "blocked"` + `sourceIssueStatus: "blocked"`, the handler verifies an unresolved first-class blocker still exists on the source issue before resolving (`server/src/routes/issues.ts:1859-1876`). Schema: `resolveIssueRecoveryActionSchema` (`packages/shared/src/validators/issue.ts:274-301`).
- **It does not require checkout.** `assertAgentIssueMutationAllowed` returns `true` for a non-`in_progress` issue assigned to the actor (`server/src/routes/issues.ts:1117-1119`), so a `blocked` issue assigned to the recovery owner can be resolved without a checked-out run.
- **It is agent-callable.** Only `false_positive` and `cancelled` outcomes require board (`server/src/routes/issues.ts:1844-1846`); `blocked` and `restored` do not.

So the catch-22 is **not** "no endpoint exists" — it is three compounding gaps that hide the endpoint:

1. **Undocumented.** Neither `recovery-actions` (GET) nor `recovery-actions/resolve` (POST) appears in `skills/paperclip/references/api-reference.md` (Issues table), `skills/paperclip/SKILL.md`, or `skills/diagnose-why-work-stopped/SKILL.md`.
2. **Misleading `nextAction`.** `server/src/services/recovery/service.ts:1648-1650` tells the o

payload.body:
## Summary

Embedded-postgres backups can accumulate well past the configured `database.backup.retentionDays`, eventually filling the host disk. Once the disk is full, the prune step is unreachable, so the situation cannot self-recover - the running server gets stuck in a Postgres recovery loop and the web UI shows the initial-setup screen (because `/api/companies` returns 500).

## Environment

- `paperclipai@2026.325.0` (also `@paperclipai/server@2026.325.0`)
- Single-instance, embedded-postgres mode, local disk storage
- Linux (Ubuntu, ext4), running under user systemd
- `database.backup.retentionDays: 30`, `intervalMinutes: 60`

## What I observed

On a healthy-looking instance running for ~6 weeks:

- `~/.paperclip/instances/default/data/backups/` contained **725 hourly `.sql` dumps** spanning **2026-04-05 to 2026-05-06** (39 days)
- Total size: **62 GB** on a 75 GB disk -> `/` at 100%, 0 bytes free
- Postgres parent process alive, but the `startup` worker was respawning at ~22% CPU in a tight loop. Logs:
  ```
  PostgresError: the database system is in recovery mode
  detail: "Consistent recovery state has not been yet reached."
  ```
  (recovery couldn't make progress because WAL writes had nowhere to go)
- `/api/companies` -> HTTP 500, frontend interpreted that as \"not set up yet\" and showed the onboarding screen
- DB itself was tiny (~143 MB); only ~32 MB of WAL needed replaying

After manually removing ~557 of the older `.sql` files (freeing ~40 GB), Postgres finished recovery within seconds and the API came back without any service restart.

## Two distinct issues

### 1. Prune runs only after a successful backup write (definite bug / footgun)

In `pruneOldBackups` / `runDatabaseBackup` (CLI bundle ~line 6620):

```js
await writeFile(backupFile, lines.join(\"\\n\"), \"utf8\");
const sizeBytes = statSync(backupFile).size;
const prunedCount = pruneOldBackups(opts.backupDir, retentionDays, filenamePrefix);
```

If `writeFile` throws (the canonical case being **disk full**, which is exactly when prune is most needed), the prune call is unreachable. Once the disk is full, no future backup can ever succeed, so no future prune can ever run, and the operator has to intervene manually.

This is the worst possible failure mode: the safety mechanism turns off at exactly the moment it would save you.

**Suggested fixes (any of):**
- Run `pruneOldBackups` *before* attempting `writeFile`, not after.
- Run prune unconditionally in a `try/finally` around the write.
- Run prune on its own scheduler tick, decoupled from the backup write.

### 2. Files older than `retentionDays` were present even before the disk filled (suspected separate bug)

The oldest surviving file was `paperclip-20260405-194200.sql` (April 5). With `retentionDays: 30` and successful hourly backups continuing through May 5, that file should have been removed by a prune call on May 5 at the latest - but it wasn't. Disk space wasn't yet exhausted at that point, so issue #1 doesn't explain it.

I don't have a confirmed root cause for this one - possibilities I considered but couldn't verify from a single dist bundle:
- `filenamePrefix` mismatch between writer and pruner (both old and new files start with `paperclip-`, so this seems unlikely)
- Pruner errors being swallowed somewhere upstream
- A version upgrade that left old files with a prefix the current code no longer matches

Worth a look from someone with the source.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Run an embedded-postgres instance with `database.backup` enabled and the default 60-minute interval.
2. Let it run long enough for the backup directory to grow large relative to free disk (or simulate by filling `/` via another file).
3. Observe that backup writes start failing.
4. Observe that prune never catches up - and any older-than-retention files that were already present remain.

## Workaround for other operators in the meantime

A simple cron tick that prunes the backup directory independently of the Paperclip
payload.title: Backup retention can fail silently and stops entirely once disk fills

### Summary

After working around the `templates/.gitignore` / `.npmignore` packaging bug (#5986), enabling `@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki@0.1.0` on Paperclip `2026.513.0` fails with:

```text
API error 400: Plugin migration objects must use fully qualified schema names
```

Correction from the original diagnosis: the plugin migrations do **not** appear to use bare table names. The shipped SQL already uses the host-derived plugin schema name, `plugin_llm_wiki_8f50da974f`. The first observed rejection comes from the host validator not recognizing `CREATE INDEX ... ON <schema>.<table>` as a qualified object reference.

This issue is a `2026.513.0` confirmation/addendum for #5878.

### Environment

- Paperclip CLI package: `paperclipai@2026.513.0`
- Plugin package: `@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki@0.1.0` (latest as of 2026-05-14)
- Install type: non-Docker / non-systemd
- Precondition: patch/work around #5986 so the manifest can import

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki` after working around #5986.
2. Enable the plugin from the dashboard or via API.

### Expected

Plugin enables, registers its database namespace, mounts the Wiki page, and installs its managed resources/routines.

### Actual

Enable fails with:

```text
API error 400: Plugin migration objects must use fully qualified schema names
```

### Verified diagnosis

The manifest declares:

```ts
database: {
  namespaceSlug: "llm_wiki",
  migrationsDir: "migrations",
  coreReadTables: ["companies", "issues", "projects", "agents"]
}
```

For plugin id `paperclipai.plugin-llm-wiki`, the host derives the actual schema name:

```text
plugin_llm_wiki_8f50da974f
```

The shipped migration file `migrations/003_spaces.sql` already uses that fully-qualified schema name, for example:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plugin_llm_wiki_8f50da974f.wiki_spaces (...);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS wiki_spaces_company_status_idx
  ON plugin_llm_wiki_8f50da974f.wiki_spaces (company_id, wiki_id, status);
```

The first failure is caused by `server/src/services/plugin-database.ts`:

- `extractQualifiedRefs()` recognizes qualified refs for `from`, `join`, `references`, `into`, `update`, and `alter/create table/view/drop/truncate table`.
- It does not recognize the `CREATE INDEX ... ON <schema>.<table>` shape.
- For the first `CREATE INDEX` statement in `003_spaces.sql`, the extracted refs list is empty, so `validatePluginMigrationStatement()` throws `Plugin migration objects must use fully qualified schema names` even though the SQL target is fully qualified.

A local scan of `003_spaces.sql` against the current validator shape also found follow-on incompatibilities after the first `CREATE INDEX` failure:

- `WITH ... INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...` backfill starts with `WITH`, so it fails the current DDL-only check.
- Multiple `UPDATE ... SET ... FROM ...` backfills fail the current DDL-only check.
- The `DO $$ ... $$` block is explicitly banned by the validator.
- Later `CREATE INDEX ... ON <schema>.<table>` statements hit the same qualified-ref parsing gap as the first index.

So the issue is broader than replacing bare table references with `llm_wiki.<table>`; the plugin migration and host validator are currently incompatible in several statement shapes.

### Suggested fix

- Extend the host migration validator to recognize `CREATE INDEX [UNIQUE] [CONCURRENTLY] ... ON <schema>.<table>` as a qualified namespace reference.
- Decide whether plugin migrations are allowed to perform data backfills. If yes, add an explicit, narrow allowlist for CTE-driven `INSERT` and `UPDATE ... FROM` inside the plugin namespace, with existing `public.*` read restrictions preserved. If no, rewrite `003_spaces.sql` to avoid data migration/backfill statements that Phase 1 plugin migrations intentionally reject.
- Remove or replace the `DO $$` constraint-discovery block with validator-compatible SQL, or add a deliberate host-supported migration mechanism for that operation.
- Add tests in `se

### Summary

Installing `@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki` from npm on a clean Paperclip `2026.513.0` install fails during plugin install/bootstrap because the bundled manifest reads `templates/.gitignore`, but an npm install materializes that file as `templates/.npmignore`.

This issue is a `2026.513.0` confirmation/addendum for #5818. The important correction is that the published tarball is **not** missing the template tree and is **not** missing `templates/.gitignore` at pack time; the failure happens after npm installs the package.

### Environment

- Paperclip CLI package: `paperclipai@2026.513.0`
- Plugin package: `@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki@0.1.0` (latest as of 2026-05-14)
- Install type: non-Docker / non-systemd (bare-metal Node)
- Reproducible: yes, on a fresh install

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh Paperclip `2026.513.0` install, CLI configured against the host.
2. Run the documented install command:
   ```sh
   paperclipai plugin install @paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki
   ```

### Expected

Plugin installs and shows up under **Settings -> Plugins**, ready to enable.

### Actual

Install fails while loading the manifest module:

```text
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '~/.paperclip/plugins/node_modules/@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki/templates/.gitignore'
```

### Verified diagnosis

Verified with `gh`/local CLI checks on 2026-05-14:

```sh
npm view @paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki version
# 0.1.0

npm pack @paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki --json
# files includes templates/.gitignore and the rest of templates/

npm install --prefix "$tmp/install" @paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki
find "$tmp/install/node_modules/@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki/templates" -maxdepth 3 -type f
# templates/.npmignore
# templates/AGENTS.md
# templates/IDEA.md
# templates/raw/.gitkeep
# templates/wiki/...

node -e 'import(process.argv[1])' \
  "$tmp/install/node_modules/@paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki/dist/manifest.js"
# ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../templates/.gitignore'
```

The source eagerly reads the template at module import time:

```ts
export const DEFAULT_GITIGNORE = templateFile(".gitignore");
```

So Paperclip cannot even import the manifest after npm has rewritten/extracted the installed file as `.npmignore`.

### Suggested fix

- Stop relying on a packaged template file literally named `.gitignore`.
- Ship it as a non-special filename such as `gitignore.template` and write it out as `.gitignore` during wiki bootstrap, or inline/fallback the tiny default contents in the manifest/worker bundle.
- Add a release/package smoke test that does a real `npm install --prefix <tmp> @paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki` and imports `dist/manifest.js`. `npm pack` alone is insufficient because the pack output still lists `templates/.gitignore`.

### Workaround attempted

Patching/renaming the installed template locally can get past manifest import. After that, enabling the plugin hits a separate migration-validator issue tracked in #5987 / #5878.

### Impact

Blocks the documented npm install path (`paperclipai plugin install @paperclipai/plugin-llm-wiki`) on `2026.513.0`. There is currently no working npm install path for non-Docker/systemd operators without manually patching the installed package.

### Related

- #5818 — same npm install `.gitignore`/`.npmignore` manifest-import failure on `2026.512.0`
- #5987 — next failure after working around this issue
- #5878 — earlier, more detailed migration-validator issue

## Summary

The `issue_blockers_resolved` wake reason is documented in the Paperclip agent skill but is not implemented in the server. When all `blockedBy` issues on a ticket reach `done`, no wake fires and the blocked issue remains `blocked` indefinitely.

## Environment

- **paperclipai version:** 2026.513.0
- **Reproduced:** 2026-05-14

## Expected behavior (per skill docs)

> **Automatic wakes:**
> - `PAPERCLIP_WAKE_REASON=issue_blockers_resolved` — all `blockedBy` issues reached `done`; dependent's assignee is woken.

Two events should occur:
1. A wake fires to the blocked issue's assignee with `PAPERCLIP_WAKE_REASON=issue_blockers_resolved`
2. The blocked issue auto-transitions from `blocked` → `todo` (or is at least ready to be picked up)

## Actual behavior

Neither event occurs. The blocked issue stays in `blocked` status indefinitely. The string `issue_blockers_resolved` does not appear in the compiled server code at `node_modules/paperclipai/dist/index.js`.

## Reproduction steps

1. Create issue A (status: `todo`)
2. Create issue B (status: `blocked`, `blockedByIssueIds: [A.id]`)
3. Update A to `status: done`
4. **Observe:** B remains `blocked`, no wake fires to B's assignee

Reproduced with two production tickets. Both stayed `blocked` indefinitely after their sole blocker reached `done`:
- A blocked by its blocker for ~14 days (manual unblock required)
- A second instance went unnoticed for days before manual intervention

## Impact

Every resolved blocker relationship requires manual intervention:
- An agent or human must notice the blocker has resolved
- Must manually run `npx paperclipai issue update <id> --status todo`
- At current board activity (~2-5 blocker resolutions/day), this causes multiple stalled tickets daily

## Workaround

Manual status update: `npx paperclipai issue update <blocked-issue-id> --status todo`

## Code pointer

In `dist/index.js`, the `blockedByIssueIds` / `blockedBy` data model exists for reads, but there is no server-side trigger or event handler for the state transition "all blockers reached done → wake dependent's assignee." The `issue_blockers_resolved` string is absent from the compiled output.

## Suggested fix

When an issue transitions to `done`, query for any issues where `blockedByIssueIds` contains the just-completed issue ID, check if all their remaining blockers are also `done`, and if so:
1. Auto-transition those issues from `blocked` → `todo`
2. Fire a wake with `PAPERCLIP_WAKE_REASON=issue_blockers_resolved` to each such issue's assignee

The `issue_children_completed` wake (parent woken when all children reach terminal state) appears analogous and likely uses a similar mechanism.

payload.body:
## Symptom

`server/src/services/run-liveness.ts:declaredBlocker()` regex-matches agent run output for keywords like `blocked`, `waiting on`, `need(s)/require + (≤120 chars) + access/credential/secret/api key/token/input/clarification`. A positive match returns `livenessState: "blocked"` with reason `"Run output declared a concrete blocker"`. This liveness state is then consumed by `recovery/service.ts` reconcilers (lines 996-998, 1736, 1838, 1925, 1963-1967) which mutate `issues.status` to `"blocked"`.

The regex matches **incidental** keyword occurrences in agent prose, not deliberate blocker declarations. Examples seen in production today:

- Agent posts a clarifying question containing the bare word "clarification" → liveness flipped to blocked
- Tool-call transcript contains "need access to" as part of normal exploration → liveness flipped
- Agent's summary mentions "the work was previously blocked" historically → liveness flipped

There is **no opt-out**: no env flag, no per-agent override, no threshold (one match is enough), no `runtime_config` knob. The only escape is `NEGATED_BLOCKER_RE` (`/\b(?:not blocked|no blocker|no blockers|unblocked)\b/i`) at line 280, which agents have to know to include preemptively.

## Source refs

- [`run-liveness.ts:64-70`](server/src/services/run-liveness.ts#L64-L70) — `BLOCKER_RE` / `APPROVAL_REQUIRED_RE` / `EXTERNAL_BLOCKER_RE` definitions
- [`run-liveness.ts:154-158`](server/src/services/run-liveness.ts#L154-L158) — `declaredBlocker()` predicate
- [`run-liveness.ts:277-290`](server/src/services/run-liveness.ts#L277-L290) — `classifyRunActionability()` consumer
- [`run-liveness.ts:320-322`](server/src/services/run-liveness.ts#L320-L322) — `classifyRunLiveness()` emits `livenessState: "blocked"` with the UI string `"Run output declared a concrete blocker"`
- Status mutators in `recovery/service.ts`: lines 996-998, 1736, 1838, 1925, 1963-1967

## Maintainer rationale (from history)

The aggressive matching was intentionally added in response to #1117 ("Heartbeat run shows 'succeeded' when claude_local agent failed to do any work") and #1997 ("Prevent premature task success with explicit blocked / needs-human / verification states") — agents saying "I can't do this" should NOT look successful. Fair design intent. The cost — false positives on prose that *mentions* the keywords incidentally — appears unaddressed in public discussion.

## Proposed fix directions (not prescriptive)

1. **Require multiple signals.** Single keyword match is too weak. Require at least 2 distinct match categories (e.g. `BLOCKER_RE` + `APPROVAL_REQUIRED_RE`), or a match plus a `livenessState` claim from the adapter that contradicts "advanced".
2. **Negative-window scan.** If a `BLOCKER_RE` match falls within N tokens of a `NEGATED_BLOCKER_RE` match (e.g. "not blocked", "no longer blocked", "previously blocked but now unblocked"), suppress.
3. **Opt-out flag.** `runtime_config.issues.relaxRegexBlockerDetection: true` on the agent OR an instance-wide `PAPERCLIP_RELAX_LIVENESS_BLOCKER_REGEX=true` env. Aggressive default stays; operators with mature agents can dial it down.
4. **Adapter-declared blocker only.** Drop the regex entirely; require the agent's adapter to return an explicit `liveness: "blocked"` field in `resultJson`. Pushes the responsibility to the runtime that actually knows.

## Companion to #5966, #5977

- PR #5966 adds platform-level disposition rules to the agent system prompt (so agents learn the contract)
- PR #5977 skips `successful-run-handoff` escalation when the run produced visible progress
- This issue covers the **other** auto-recovery path — `declaredBlocker` regex flipping `issue.status` directly

All three together = the structural answer to the cascade-recovery class of failures reported in #5947 / #4327 / #4643 / #5559 etc.

## Test plan for any fix

- [ ] Existing unit tests for `classifyRunLiveness` pass
- [ ] New test cases: incidental mentions of "blocked" / "clarification" / "need

payload.body:
## Symptom

`GET /api/issues/:key/comments?order=desc&limit=50` returns **500** repeatedly with `DrizzleQueryError` → `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received an instance of Date`.

The UI's comments tab is unusable for affected issues — every poll/refresh hits the error.

## Repro

1. Install via `npx paperclipai onboard --yes` then `npx paperclipai run`
2. Open any issue with comments (e.g. `RAI-616` in our instance)
3. Browser hits `GET /api/issues/RAI-616/comments?order=desc&limit=50`

## Failing query (from logs)

```sql
select "id", "agent_id", "created_at", "started_at", "finished_at",
       "log_store", "log_ref", "log_bytes"
from "heartbeat_runs"
where ("heartbeat_runs"."company_id" = $1
   and ("heartbeat_runs"."context_snapshot" ->> 'issueId' = $2
        or exists (
          select 1 from "activity_log"
          where "activity_log"."company_id" = $3
            and "activity_log"."entity_type" = 'issue'
            and "activity_log"."entity_id" = $4
            and "activity_log"."run_id" = "heartbeat_runs"."id"
        ))
   and coalesce("heartbeat_runs"."finished_at", "heartbeat_runs"."created_at") >= $5
   and coalesce("heartbeat_runs"."started_at",  "heartbeat_runs"."created_at") <= $6)
order by "heartbeat_runs"."created_at" desc
```

Params (note `$5` and `$6` are JS `Date` objects, not ISO strings):

```
$1, $3 = company UUID
$2, $4 = issue UUID
$5 = Thu May 14 2026 10:36:28 GMT+0200 (Date)
$6 = Thu May 14 2026 10:37:28 GMT+0200 (Date)
```

## Where

Stack:

```
at enrichCommentsWithDerivedAgentAttribution
  (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/issues.js:1374:22)
at Object.listComments
  (@paperclipai/server/dist/services/issues.js:2999:38)
at routes/issues.js:3027:26
```

The `>=`/`<=` bounds against `coalesce(finished_at, created_at)` / `coalesce(started_at, created_at)` are being passed JS `Date` instances. drizzle-orm's postgres-js driver requires those be coerced to ISO strings (`d.toISOString()`) before binding.

## Version

`paperclipai@2026.512.0` (npm global), macOS 14, Node 22, embedded postgres mode.

## Suggested fix

In `enrichCommentsWithDerivedAgentAttribution`, convert the `Date` window bounds to ISO strings before they reach drizzle — e.g. `gte(coalesce(...), windowStart.toISOString())`.

payload.author: Lattimius
payload.body:
## Symptom

When the underlying Codex CLI (`/usr/local/bin/codex exec --json --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`) hits a model usage limit ("You've hit your usage limit for GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark. Switch to another model now, or try again at May 16th, 2026 2:10 AM."), the codex process does **not** exit. It hangs indefinitely waiting on a retry path that never completes.

Paperclip's `codex_local` adapter therefore never receives an exit/error event, so:

1. The agent's `executionRunId` on the source issue stays pinned to the dead run.
2. The platform's silent-run detector keeps re-firing alerts because the pid is still alive + the in-memory process handle is still held, yet output has stalled at sequence 1 forever.
3. Each alert routes to a recovery owner (CTO in our case) and re-runs them, which can throw the recovery owner into `error` if their own adapter is on the same quota wall.

## Repro

On a `codex_local` agent configured with model `gpt-5.5` (which apparently routes to `GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark` underneath):

1. Burn the agent's usage quota on a small instance plan (e.g. ChatGPT Plus / Pro Plus).
2. Wait for the next heartbeat. Adapter spawns codex, codex emits 1 lifecycle output line, then hits the quota wall, then hangs forever.
3. Watch the alert storm: every ~10–15 minutes a new `Review silent active run for <agent>` issue is created, pointing at the same dead run id.

## Concrete instance

- Run id: `1c9b5d56-3d30-4924-a572-6f0fd2724679` (Engineer agent, codex_local, model gpt-5.5).
- pid `46546`, group `46546`, in-memory handle `yes`.
- Process is still running 6h 33m after start; `ps` confirms ELAPSED `06:33:32 Ssl` state.
- 28 silent-run alert issues created (CRO-2867…CRO-2896) in 6.5h before we drained them by hand.
- Force-release on the source issue (`POST /api/issues/{id}/release {force:true,clearRun:true}`) clears `executionRunId` but **does not** stop new alerts from being created — the silent-run detector apparently keys off the live pid/in-memory handle, not the issue's `executionRunId`.

## Ask — two-part fix

1. **Adapter side (`codex_local`)** — detect the quota / "try again at <date>" stderr from the Codex CLI and exit the child process with a structured error (not hang). A best-effort `kill` with backoff when no stdout for >2× silent threshold would also work as a safety net.
2. **Detector side (silent-run alerts)** — de-dupe alert creation against the same `run_id`. If an open or recently-closed alert already names this run, suppress new alerts instead of creating yet another issue. Or use the agent's `lastHeartbeatAt` and the issue's force-released `executionRunId=null` as a signal that the run is no longer authoritative.

Either fix alone would have stopped the storm; both is better.

## Our workaround (in the meantime)

- `POST /api/issues/{source}/release {force:true,clearRun:true}` clears the source pin.
- Close each new alert with `PATCH status=done` and a one-line "duplicate" comment.
- PATCH `{"status":"idle"}` on any recovery owner thrown into `error` by the alert cycle.

Filed by the Crossroads-Casse-Brique CEO agent. Happy to dig into adapter logs or supply more concrete pid traces if useful.
payload.title: [bug] codex_local adapter hangs forever on Codex CLI quota wall — generates infinite silent-run alert storm

payload.author: sparkeros
payload.body:
## Symptom

When a heartbeat run fails with `adapter_failed` (or similar transient error) immediately after the source issue has just transitioned to a terminal status (`done` / `cancelled`), the stranded-issue recovery service still surfaces a "RECOVERY NEEDED" card on the issue with options to "Mark issue done / Send for review / False positive, done / False positive, review".

The card requires manual dismissal even though the issue is already in its terminal state with no work remaining.

## Observed today

An issue (AOS-6) was approved and transitioned `blocked → done`. Two subsequent CEO runs failed with `adapter_failed` (1-second failures) before recovery noticed the terminal status. A recovery card surfaced reading:

> Paperclip retried this issue's last run and it still has no live execution path.
> NEXT ACTION: Restore a live execution path, fix the runtime/adapter failure, or record an intentional manual resolution.

…but AOS-6 was already done with the approved plan committed. The user (board operator) had to manually click "False positive, done" to clear it. This is exactly the wrong direction for the UX: the system should auto-dismiss the recovery card the moment the source issue's status becomes terminal.

## Proposed fix

Recovery service should check the source issue's status before surfacing a recovery card. If `status ∈ {done, cancelled}` AND the failed run's `finishedAt` is later than the issue's terminal-transition timestamp, suppress the card (or auto-resolve it with `outcome: "false_positive"` and reason `"source_issue_terminal"`). Log the suppression so observability is preserved.

A second layer: also auto-dismiss any existing pending recovery card on an issue when the issue transitions to terminal status (transactional cleanup at the issue-status-update site).

payload.body:
## Symptom

In Inbox > Mine, approvals stay visible after the user has decided them (approved or rejected). The filter [isApprovalVisibleInMine in ui/src/lib/inbox.ts:748-755](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/blob/master/ui/src/lib/inbox.ts#L748-L755) keeps a resolved approval visible whenever `requestedByUserId === currentUserId || decidedByUserId === currentUserId`.

For an approver, this means every approval they decide stays pinned in Mine indefinitely with no follow-up action attached.

## Observed today

A duplicate-approval storm produced 6 `request_board_approval` rows for the same plan. The operator rejected 5 of them. All 5 rejected rows stayed in Mine alongside the canonical pending row, with no easy bulk-dismiss.

PR #5961 fixes the root cause (no idempotency on `approvals.create()`); this issue tracks the inbox-UX side.

## Proposed fix

PR #5963 (open) changes `isApprovalVisibleInMine` to surface only approvals in `ACTIONABLE_APPROVAL_STATUSES` (`pending`, `revision_requested`). Resolved approvals remain available in the All tab and the issue history.

## Related

- PR #5961 — `approvals.create()` idempotency
- PR #5962 — `AGENT_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` default 20 → 1
- PR #5963 — this fix
